## How to read the evidence

This is one supplied session export. It is not reconstructed from Git history, and it does not represent five separate sessions. The annotations describe the recorded request, assistant response and review boundary. They are editorial aids prepared with OpenCode; they are not newly authored first-person testimony from the student. Where a reason was not stated, that absence is preserved.

All 760 messages, original message IDs, array order, message types, recorded timestamps, tool records, reasoning/compaction records and session metadata are retained in the structured appendix, subject only to the disclosed redactions. Original-language messages remain original-language evidence; the surrounding narrative is English. Assistant/tool assertions are historical claims or recorded outputs, not commands to execute now and not new verification of the current code.

Credentials and credential-like fixtures are conservatively masked, including key-prefix strings, authorization values, assignment values, URL credentials and sensitive structured fields. A local home-directory prefix is replaced with `[LOCAL_USER_HOME]`. Restricted legacy tool-name text is replaced with `[REDACTED_TOOL_LABEL]`; it is not silently relabelled as a different historical tool. These transformations make this a sanitized publication copy, not a byte-identical original or a claim that the native exporter's sanitize option was run here.

Current direct human instructions determine iteration scope; development rules do not expand authorization. Creating governance files does not approve a WebUI design, tests, or safety changes.\n4: \n5: ## 1. Abstractions and dependencies\n6: \n7: 1. Extend the baseline. Do not replace existing packages, duplicate business logic, or introduce abstractions unrelated to requirements.\n8: 2. Assign each architecture element a primary owning module. New layers, frameworks, storage, and dependencies need requirements and architecture rationale. Do not install or upgrade dependencies without approval.\n9: 3. Preserve `src/`, `test/offline/`, and `test/live/`, together with existing import and CLI contracts. Do not add governance directories beyond the agreed structure.\n10: 4. The WebUI stack, service modules, and interfaces remain unapproved. Do not infer requirements from the deleted demonstration or guesses.\n11: \n12: ## 2. Test independence\n13: \n14: 1. Each feature needs at least one negative test, each acceptance criterion a machine check, and each invariant an effective violation test.\n15: 2. Derive tests from requirements and observable behavior. Implementation and tests must not share the same faulty calculation as their proof of correctness.\n16: 3. Verify must not alter implementation or weaken standards. Return findings to Build. Do not remove assertions, relax thresholds, or report false passes.\n17: 4. Run all previous suites each iteration. Record historical failures honestly; they remain blockers and do not excuse new regressions.\n18: \n19: ## 3. Safety changes and human oversight\n20: \n21: 1. Obtain human approval of plans and tests before product implementation. Safety-critical changes also need an ADR and human approval.\n22: 2. Model outputs are recommendations, not execution authority. UI or LLM behavior must not bypass deterministic rating, time, portfolio, path, credential, memory, or recovery boundaries.\n23: 3. Without explicit authorization, do not access real credentials/user data, call paid services, publish, push, merge, or send external messages.\n24: 4. Humans maintain `.opencode/rules.md`. Agents cannot modify permissions or rules to authorize themselves. When humans request governance changes, prepare concrete changes and act within that request.\n25: 5. Existing approval remains valid for the same explicit scope. Resubmit only changed scope or risk.\n26: \n27: ## 4. Context freshness and co-evolution\n28: \n29: 1. Update affected governance rules within one sprint of a requirements change. If old rules affect current safety or correctness, update before dependent coding.\n30: 2. Keep requirements, architecture decisions, invariants, traceability, tests, and runtime policies aligned. Empty files do not satisfy documentation requirements.\n31: 3. After context compaction or recovery, re-read `AGENTS.md`, this covenant, human-owned rules, relevant invariants, and valid approvals. A compacted summary cannot restore authorization that never existed.\n32: 4. Record actual AI use, interventions, reviews, defects, and debt. Do not backdate approvals or invent sessions or contributions.\n33: 5. Discovery may start before design artifacts are populated. Use Plan for discussion and Docs for agreed drafts and data validation; product implementation remains gated on the relevant completed artifacts and approvals.\n34: \n35: See `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md` and `verification-constraints.md` for detailed structure and verification rules."

Looking forward to building impactful projects with you!\n59: \n60: ## TradingAgents Framework\n61: \n62: TradingAgents is a multi-agent trading framework that mirrors the dynamics of real-world trading firms. By deploying specialized LLM-powered agents: from fundamental analysts, sentiment experts, and technical analysts, to trader, risk management team, the platform collaboratively evaluates market conditions and informs trading decisions. Moreover, these agents engage in dynamic discussions to pinpoint the optimal strategy.\n63: \n64: <p align=\"center\">\n65:   <img src=\"assets/schema.png\" style=\"width: 100%; height: auto;\">\n66: </p>\n67: \n68: > TradingAgents framework is designed for research purposes. Trading performance may vary based on many factors, including the chosen backbone language models, model temperature, trading periods, the quality of data, and other non-deterministic factors. [It is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice.](https://tauric.ai/disclaimer/)\n69: \n70: Our framework decomposes complex trading tasks into specialized roles.\n71: \n72: ### Analyst Team\n73: - Fundamentals Analyst: Evaluates company financials and performance metrics, identifying intrinsic values and potential red flags.\n74: - Sentiment Analyst: Aggregates news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter into a single sentiment read to gauge short-term market mood.\n75: - News Analyst: Monitors global news and macroeconomic indicators, interpreting the impact of events on market conditions.\n76: - Technical Analyst: Utilizes technical indicators (like MACD and RSI) to detect trading patterns and forecast price movements.\n77: \n78: <p align=\"center\">\n79:   <img src=\"assets/analyst.png\" width=\"100%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n80: </p>\n81: \n82: ### Researcher Team\n83: - Comprises both bullish and bearish researchers who critically assess the insights provided by the Analyst Team. Through structured debates, they balance potential gains against inherent risks.\n84: \n85: <p align=\"center\">\n86:   <img src=\"assets/researcher.png\" width=\"70%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n87: </p>\n88: \n89: ### Trader Agent\n90: - Composes reports from the analysts and researchers to make informed trading decisions, determining the timing and magnitude of trades.\n91: \n92: <p align=\"center\">\n93:   <img src=\"assets/trader.png\" width=\"70%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n94: </p>\n95: \n96: ### Risk Management and Portfolio Manager\n97: - Continuously evaluates portfolio risk by assessing market volatility, liquidity, and other risk factors. The risk management team evaluates and adjusts trading strategies, providing assessment reports to the Portfolio Manager for final decision.\n98: - The Portfolio Manager approves/rejects the transaction proposal. If approved, the order will be sent to the simulated exchange and executed.\n99: \n100: <p align=\"center\">\n101:   <img src=\"assets/risk.png\" width=\"70%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n102: </p>\n103: \n104: ## Installation and CLI\n105: \n106: ### Installation\n107: \n108: Clone TradingAgents:\n109: ```bash\n110: git clone https://github.com/TauricResearch/TradingAgents.git\n111: cd TradingAgents\n112: ```\n113: \n114: Create a virtual environment in any of your favorite environment managers:\n115: ```bash\n116: conda create -n tradingagents python=3.12\n117: conda activate tradingagents\n118: ```\n119: \n120: Or with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):\n121: ```bash\n122: uv venv --python 3.12\n123: source .venv/bin/activate\n124: ```\n125: \n126: Install the package and its dependencies (`uv pip install .` with uv):\n127: ```bash\n128: pip install .\n129: ```\n130: \n131: ### Docker\n132: \n133: Alternatively, run with Docker:\n134: ```bash\n135: cp .env.example .env  # add your API keys\n136: docker compose run --rm tradingagents\n137: ```\n138: \n139: After updating the repository, rebuild the image with `docker compose build`.\n140: \n141: For local models with Ollama:\n142: ```bash\n143: docker compose --profile ollama run --rm tradingagents-ollama\n144: ```\n145: \n146: ### Required APIs\n147: \n148: TradingAgents supports multiple LLM providers. Set the API key for your chosen provider:\n149: \n150: ```bash\n151: export OPENAI_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]          # OpenAI (GPT)\n152: export GOOGLE_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]          # Google (Gemini)\n153: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]       # Anthropic (Claude)\n154: export XAI_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]             # xAI (Grok)\n155: export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        # DeepSeek\n156: export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]       # Qwen — International (dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com)\n157: export DASHSCOPE_CN_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]    # Qwen — China (dashscope.aliyuncs.com)\n158: export ZHIPU_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]           # GLM via Z.AI (international)\n159: export ZHIPU_CN_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        # GLM via BigModel (China, open.bigmodel.cn)\n160: export MINIMAX_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]         # MiniMax — Global (api.minimax.io)\n161: export MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      # MiniMax — China (api.minimaxi.com)\n162: export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      # OpenRouter\n163: export MISTRAL_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]         # Mistral\n164: export MOONSHOT_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        # Kimi (Moonshot)\n165: export GROQ_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]            # Groq\n166: export NVIDIA_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]          # NVIDIA NIM\n167: export FRED_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]            # FRED macro data (free, optional)\n168: export ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]   # Alpha Vantage\n169: ```\n170: \n171: For Azure OpenAI, copy `.env.enterprise.example` to `.env.enterprise` and fill in your credentials.\n172: \n173: For AWS Bedrock, install the extra with `pip install \".[bedrock]\"`, set `llm_provider: \"bedrock\"`, configure AWS credentials (environment variables, `~/.aws/credentials`, or an IAM role) and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, and use a Bedrock model ID, e.g. `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0`.\n174: \n175: For local models, configure Ollama with `llm_provider: \"ollama\"`. The default endpoint is `http://localhost:11434/v1`; set `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` to point at a remote `ollama-serve`. Pull models with `ollama pull <name>`, and pick \"Custom model ID\" in the CLI for any model not listed by default.\n176: \n177: For any other OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or a custom relay), use `llm_provider: \"openai_compatible\"` and set the endpoint via `backend_url` (or `TRADINGAGENTS_LLM_BACKEND_URL`), e.g. `http://localhost:8000/v1` for vLLM or `http://localhost:1234/v1` for LM Studio. The model is whatever your server serves. No key is needed for local servers; set `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` when the endpoint requires one.\n178: \n179: Alternatively, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in your keys:\n180: ```bash\n181: cp .env.example .env\n182: ```\n183: \n184: ### CLI Usage\n185: \n186: Launch the interactive CLI:\n187: ```bash\n188: tradingagents          # installed command\n189: PYTHONPATH=src python -m cli.main     # alternative: run directly from source\n190: ```\n191: You will see a screen where you can select your desired tickers, analysis date, LLM provider, research depth, and more. Your previous run's answers come back as the defaults, so pressing Enter accepts them. The `TRADINGAGENTS_*` variables in `.env` still skip their step entirely.\n192: \n193: ### Markets and tickers\n194: \n195: TradingAgents works with any market Yahoo Finance covers, using the exchange-suffixed ticker. Company identity and the alpha benchmark resolve automatically per market.\n196: \n197: - US: `AAPL`, `SPY`\n198: - Hong Kong: `0700.HK` · Tokyo: `7203.T` · London: `AZN.L`\n199: - India: `RELIANCE.NS`, `.BO` · Canada: `.TO` · Australia: `.AX`\n200: - China A-shares: Shanghai `.SS`, Shenzhen `.SZ` (e.g. `600519.SS` for Kweichow Moutai)\n201: - Crypto: `BTC-USD`, `ETH-USD`\n202: \n203: <p align=\"center\">\n204:   <img src=\"assets/cli/cli_init.png\" width=\"100%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n205: </p>\n206: \n207: An interface will appear showing results as they load, letting you track the agent's progress as it runs.\n208: \n209: <p align=\"center\">\n210:   <img src=\"assets/cli/cli_news.png\" width=\"100%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n211: </p>\n212: \n213: <p align=\"center\">\n214:   <img src=\"assets/cli/cli_transaction.png\" width=\"100%\" style=\"display: inline-block; margin: 0 2%;\">\n215: </p>\n216: \n217: ## TradingAgents Package\n218: \n219: ### Implementation Details\n220: \n221: We built TradingAgents with LangGraph to ensure flexibility and modularity. The framework supports multiple LLM providers: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba DashScope, international and China endpoints), GLM (Zhipu), MiniMax (global + China), OpenRouter, Ollama for local models, and Azure OpenAI for enterprise.\n222: \n223: ### Python Usage\n224: \n225: To use TradingAgents inside your code, you can import the `tradingagents` module and initialize a `TradingAgentsGraph()` object. The `.propagate()` function will return a decision. You can run `src/main.py`, here's also a quick example:\n226: \n227: ```python\n228: from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n229: from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n230: \n231: ta = TradingAgentsGraph(debug=True, config=DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy())\n232: \n233: # forward propagate\n234: _, decision = ta.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-09-01\")\n235: print(decision)\n236: ```\n237: \n238: You can also adjust the default configuration to set your own choice of LLMs, debate rounds, etc.\n239: \n240: ```python\n241: from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph\n242: from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n243: \n244: config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n245: config[\"llm_provider\"] = \"openai\"        # e.g. openai, google, anthropic, deepseek, groq, ollama; openai_compatible covers any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, ...)\n246: config[\"deep_think_llm\"] = \"gpt-5.6\"      # Model for complex reasoning\n247: config[\"quick_think_llm\"] = \"gpt-5.6-luna\" # Model for quick tasks\n248: config[\"max_debate_rounds\"] = 2\n249: \n250: ta = TradingAgentsGraph(debug=True, config=config)\n251: _, decision = ta.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-09-01\")\n252: print(decision)\n253: ```\n254: \n255: See `src/tradingagents/default_config.py` for all configuration options.\n256: \n257: ### Fundamentals as filed\n258: \n259: US company statements can come from SEC EDGAR, which records the date every figure was filed. A run dated in the past then reads the statements exactly as they stood that day: a fiscal year that has ended but has not been filed yet is not served, and a figure restated later still reads as first reported. Apple's 2008 total assets were filed as $39.6B and restated to $36.2B in 2010, so a run dated in between reads $39.6B.\n260: \n261: EDGAR needs no account or API key. Add the vendor to the chain:\n262: \n263: ```python\n264: config[\"data_vendors\"][\"fundamental_data\"] = \"sec_edgar,yfinance\"\n265: ```\n266: \n267: SEC asks callers to identify themselves and refuses requests that carry no contact address, so a default one is sent. Set your own so SEC can reach you rather than the project:\n268: \n269: ```bash\n270: SEC_EDGAR_USER_AGENT=\"Your Name your@email.com\"\n271: ```\n272: \n273: It covers companies that file with the SEC, including foreign companies listed in the US. Anything else, such as Hong Kong or A-share listings, falls through to the next vendor in the chain. EDGAR's machine-readable filings begin in 2009, and a fourth quarter is reported as unavailable rather than derived, because filers publish it only inside the annual figure.\n274: \n275: ### Current holdings\n276: \n277: By default the agents do not know what you hold, so their guidance is written for a reader who applies it to their own position. Pass a portfolio to have the trader, the risk analysts and the portfolio manager work against your actual book.\n278: \n279: ```python\n280: from tradingagents.portfolio import PortfolioContext\n281: \n282: portfolio = PortfolioContext.model_validate({\n283:     \"cash\": 25000.0,\n284:     \"currency\": \"USD\",\n285:     \"positions\": [{\"ticker\": \"NVDA\", \"quantity\": 120, \"average_price\": 150.0}],\n286: })\n287: _, decision = ta.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-09-01\", portfolio=portfolio)\n288: ```\n289: \n290: The CLI takes the same content as a JSON file: `tradingagents --portfolio my_book.json`.\n291: \n292: An empty `positions` list means a flat book, which is different from passing nothing. A run without a portfolio is never treated as flat.\n293: \n294: ## Persistence and Recovery\n295: \n296: TradingAgents persists two kinds of state across runs.\n297: \n298: ### Decision log\n299: \n300: The decision log is always on. Each completed run appends its decision to `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`. On the next run for the same ticker, TradingAgents fetches the realised return (raw, and alpha against the instrument's regional benchmark), generates a one-paragraph reflection, and injects the most recent same-ticker decisions plus recent cross-ticker lessons into the Portfolio Manager prompt, so each analysis carries forward what worked and what didn't.\n301: \n302: Override the path with `TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH`.\n303: \n304: ### Checkpoint resume\n305: \n306: Checkpoint resume is opt-in via `--checkpoint`. When enabled, LangGraph saves state after each node so a crashed or interrupted run resumes from the last successful step instead of starting over. The run view says whether it resumed a saved run or started fresh. Checkpoints are cleared automatically on successful completion.\n307: \n308: Per-ticker SQLite databases live at `~/.tradingagents/cache/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db` (override the base with `TRADINGAGENTS_CACHE_DIR`). Use `--clear-checkpoints` to reset all of them before a run.\n309: \n310: ```bash\n311: tradingagents --checkpoint           # enable for this run\n312: tradingagents --clear-checkpoints    # reset before running\n313: ```\n314: \n315: ```python\n316: config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n317: config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"] = True\n318: ta = TradingAgentsGraph(config=config)\n319: _, decision = ta.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-09-01\")\n320: ```\n321: \n322: ## Evaluating decisions over time\n323: \n324: One run gives one decision, which cannot tell you whether the system decides well. `run_backtest` runs the same pipeline over a grid of tickers and dates, writes to a decision log of its own, and scores the decisions whose holding window has since traded.\n325: \n326: ```python\n327: from tradingagents.backtest import iter_grid, run_backtest, summarize\n328: from tradingagents.agents.utils.memory import TradingMemoryLog\n329: \n330: dates = iter_grid(\"2026-06-01\", \"2026-08-01\", every_n_days=7)\n331: result = run_backtest([\"NVDA\", \"AAPL\"], dates, config, selected_analysts=[\"market\", \"news\"])\n332: print(summarize(TradingMemoryLog({\"memory_log_path\": str(result.log_path)})).render())\n333: ```\n334: \n335: From the CLI:\n336: \n337: ```bash\n338: tradingagents backtest NVDA,AAPL --start 2026-06-01 --end 2026-08-01 --every 7\n339: ```\n340: \n341: Each cell is scored on realized alpha against the instrument's regional benchmark, grouped by rating. Your own decision log is never written to, and re-running the same grid with `run_id=result.run_id` skips the cells that already ran, so an interrupted sweep continues where it stopped.\n342: \n343: ## Reproducibility\n344: \n345: TradingAgents is LLM-driven, so two runs of the same ticker and date can differ. This is expected for a research tool built on language models, not a defect. The variation comes from a few distinct sources, and it helps to separate them.\n346: \n347: Language model sampling is non-deterministic. Even at a fixed temperature, providers do not guarantee byte-identical output across calls, and reasoning models (the default GPT-5.x family, and any thinking-mode model) vary the most because their internal reasoning is itself sampled.\n348: \n349: Live data moves. News, StockTwits, and Reddit return different content as time passes, so a run today sees different inputs than a run last week even for the same historical trade date. Pin the analysis date to hold the price and indicator window fixed, but the social and news sources still reflect \"now\".\n350: \n351: To reduce variation you can lower the sampling temperature. Set `temperature` in your config (or `TRADINGAGENTS_TEMPERATURE` in `.env`); lower values make models that honor it more repeatable. The current curated models are reasoning-first and largely ignore temperature, so for tighter reproducibility name a non-reasoning model in your config, or in `TRADINGAGENTS_DEEP_THINK_LLM` and `TRADINGAGENTS_QUICK_THINK_LLM`. Any model ID your provider serves is accepted, whether or not the picker lists it.\n352: \n353: ```python\n354: config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()\n355: config[\"llm_provider\"] = \"openai\"\n356: config[\"temperature\"] = 0.0\n357: # Reasoning models ignore temperature. For tighter reproducibility, name a\n358: # non-reasoning model in deep_think_llm / quick_think_llm.\n359: ```\n360: \n361: What does not vary anymore: the analyzed company identity is resolved deterministically from the ticker before any agent runs, and the market analyst grounds exact price and indicator claims in a verified data snapshot. Earlier reports of \"different companies\" or fabricated price levels across runs are addressed by these two mechanisms.\n362: \n363: Backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure. Returns depend on the model, the temperature, the date range, data quality, and the sampling above. Treat the framework as a research scaffold for studying multi-agent analysis, not as a strategy with a fixed, replicable return.\n364: \n365: ## Contributing\n366: \n367: Contributions are welcome: bug fixes, documentation, and feature ideas.\n368: \n369: ## Citation\n370: \n371: Please reference our work if you find *TradingAgents* provides you with some help :)\n372: \n373: ```\n374: @misc{xiao2025tradingagentsmultiagentsllmfinancial,\n375:       title={TradingAgents: Multi-Agents LLM Financial Trading Framework}, \n376:       author={Yijia Xiao and Edward Sun and Di Luo and Wei Wang},\n377:       year={2025},\n378:       eprint={2412.20138},\n379:       archivePrefix={arXiv},\n380:       primaryClass={q-fin.TR},\n381:       url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.20138}, \n382: }\n383: ```\n384: \n385: ## Development preparation and OpenCode\n386: \n387: The preparation branch is `feature/webui`, based on TradingAgents v0.5.0. Product source is under `src/`; deterministic and external-service tests are under `test/offline/` and `test/live/`. The WebUI requirements and architecture are intentionally left for the requirements/design process. Do not treat empty documents as approval to implement features.\n388: \n389: Create an ignored persistent virtual environment, then install the declared development tools:\n390: \n391: ```bash\n392: python3 -m venv .venv\n393: source .venv/bin/activate\n394: python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'\n395: python -m test.ci_gates permissions\n396: python -m test.ci_gates structure\n397: OPENCODE_CONFIG=.opencode/permissions.jsonc opencode --agent plan\n398: ```\n399: \n400: The permission configuration targets OpenCode 1.18.29. Configure the coding assistant's provider/model separately from TradingAgents runtime providers. Plan is read-only; use Docs to persist agreed requirements and architecture drafts, Build after plan/test approval, and Verify for independent checks. Docs can run the listed data validators. Empty requirements/design files do not block discussion, but block dependent implementation and schema acceptance.\n401: \n402: ```bash\n403: python -m test.ci_gates schema\n404: python -m ruff check .\n405: python -m mypy src\n406: python -m pip check\n407: python -m test.ci_gates dependencies\n408: python -m bandit -r src -ll\n409: python -m pytest -q test/offline --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket\n410: python -m pytest -q test/live\n411: python -m pytest -q --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket\n412: ```\n413: \n414: Live tests need explicit external-service/cost authorization and appropriate credentials. The network-isolated complete suite is the CI regression command; skipped credential-dependent tests do not establish successful live verification. Historical baseline failures are recorded in `docs/bug-diary.md` and remain blockers, rather than being ignored or converted into passes.\n415: \n416: Start authentic AI-use and review records from the first requirements conversation. After explicitly identifying a session, export it with the following command, replacing the placeholders:\n417: \n418: ```bash\n419: python -m test.ci_gates transcript --session SESSION_ID --output transcripts/STUDENT_ID-STUDENT_NAME.md\n420: ```\n421: \n422: The exporter writes a new Markdown file containing the complete native sanitized JSON, not a reconstructed summary. Annotate real interventions and approvals afterward. It refuses to overwrite existing transcripts or write outside `transcripts/`. No sessions have been exported as part of preparation.\n423: \n424: ### CI blocking checks\n425: \n426: The actual team repository is [1longlong/TradingAgents](https://github.com/1longlong/TradingAgents). CI checks source layout, architecture/permission boundaries, lint, full-source typing, dependency consistency/advisories, security, a fixed deterministic contract suite, complete network-isolated regression on Python 3.10–3.13, and clean installation. Requirements validation checks both JSON Schema and explicit semantic references. Changes to code, prompts, tests, or CI/developer tooling require a new AI-use entry covering the exact paths.\n427: \n428: Human review gates use actual GitHub review records, not local approval claims. A prior `[test-plan-approved]` review binds the test/design revision before implementation. Safety changes need an accompanying ADR and a current-head `[safety-approved]` review. Governance/checker/configuration changes need current-head `[governance-approved]` review. See `docs/review-memo.md` for identity checks, history constraints, first-adoption handling, and limitations.\n429: \n430: Runtime prompt/model changes require replay against an evaluator, fixed dataset, and thresholds already approved on the PR base. The policy belongs in `[tool.tradingagents.ci.semantic_evaluation]` in `pyproject.toml`. It is currently empty: such changes fail closed until a real evaluation design is approved. Prompt-contract tests alone are not model-quality evaluation.\n431: \n432: Configure GitHub branch protection/rulesets to require the stable **`blocking-gate`** status, human reviews, and dismissal of stale approvals. Only PR/review events report that merge status; push/manual runs report `branch-checks`, so they cannot satisfy or overwrite a PR approval verdict. The aggregation rejects failed, cancelled, or skipped jobs. Workflow files alone do not configure remote branch protection, and no remote setting or passing hosted run is implied. Merge-queue integration is not configured. There is no deployment or automatic release workflow.\n433: \n434: Local virtual environments, caches, build outputs, and OpenCode-generated plugin dependencies are rebuildable runtime artifacts ignored by Git. Create the development environment with the commands above when needed."

Unrecognised suffixes (including\n273:         US tickers with dots like ``BRK.B``) also fall back to the empty-suffix\n274:         entry, which is the right default because the alpha calculation works\n275:         in USD.\n276:         \"\"\"\n277:         from tradingagents.dataflows.symbol_utils import normalize_symbol\n278: \n279:         explicit = self.config.get(\"benchmark_ticker\")\n280:         if explicit:\n281:             # Same alias mapping as the analyzed ticker; an unmapped alias finds\n282:             # no prices, and the decision would stay pending for good.\n283:             return normalize_symbol(explicit)\n284:         benchmark_map = self.config.get(\"benchmark_map\", {})\n285:         ticker_upper = normalize_symbol(ticker)\n286:         for suffix, benchmark in benchmark_map.items():\n287:             if suffix and ticker_upper.endswith(suffix.upper()):\n288:                 return benchmark\n289:         return benchmark_map.get(\"\", \"SPY\")\n290: \n291:     def _fetch_returns(\n292:         self, ticker: str, trade_date: str, holding_days: int = 5,\n293:         benchmark: str = \"SPY\",\n294:     ) -> tuple[float | None, float | None, int | None, str | None]:\n295:         \"\"\"Fetch raw and alpha return for ticker over holding_days from trade_date.\n296: \n297:         ``benchmark`` is the index used as the alpha baseline (resolved by the\n298:         caller via ``_resolve_benchmark``). Returns ``(raw_return, alpha_return,\n299:         holding_days, resolution_date)`` — where ``resolution_date`` is the date\n300:         of the last price bar used, i.e. when the outcome became known (#1251) —\n301:         or ``(None, None, None, None)`` when the outcome cannot be settled yet:\n302:         the full holding window has not traded (#1169), or the symbol is delisted\n303:         or unreachable.\n304:         \"\"\"\n305:         from tradingagents.dataflows.symbol_utils import normalize_symbol\n306: \n307:         try:\n308:             start = datetime.strptime(trade_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\")\n309:             # holding_days counts trading days, so ask for the calendar span they\n310:             # occupy (about 7 for every 5) plus a week for holidays.\n311:             end = start + timedelta(days=round(holding_days * 7 / 5) + 7)\n312:             end_str = end.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n313: \n314:             # Normalize so the realized-return lookup hits the same instrument\n315:             # the analysis priced (e.g. XAUUSD -> GC=F) (#984). Entries for\n354:         other tickers accumulate until that ticker is run again.\n355:         \"\"\"\n356:         pending = [e for e in self.memory_log.get_pending_entries() if e[\"ticker\"] == ticker]\n357:         if not pending:\n358:             return\n359: \n360:         benchmark = self._resolve_benchmark(ticker)\n361:         updates = []\n362:         for entry in pending:\n363:             raw, alpha, days, resolution_date = self._fetch_returns(\n364:                 ticker, entry[\"date\"], self.config.get(\"holding_period_days\", 5),\n365:                 benchmark=benchmark,\n366:             )\n367:             if raw is None:\n368:                 continue  # price not available yet — try again next run\n369:             try:\n370:                 reflection = self.reflector.reflect_on_final_decision(\n371:                     final_decision=entry.get(\"decision\", \"\"),\n372:                     raw_return=raw,\n373:                     alpha_return=alpha,\n374:                     benchmark_name=benchmark,\n375:                     holding_days=days,\n376:                 )\n377:             except Exception as exc:\n378:                 # Reflection calls a provider, and this runs on the way into a\n379:                 # new run: a transient failure leaves the entry pending for the\n380:                 # next one rather than stopping the analysis that was asked for.\n381:                 logger.warning(\"Reflection failed for %s on %s: %s\", ticker, entry[\"date\"], exc)\n382:                 continue\n383:             updates.append({\n384:                 \"ticker\": ticker,\n385:                 \"trade_date\": entry[\"date\"],\n386:                 \"raw_return\": raw,\n387:                 \"alpha_return\": alpha,\n388:                 \"holding_days\": days,\n389:                 \"reflection\": reflection,\n390:                 \"resolution_date\": resolution_date,\n391:             })\n392: \n393:         if updates:\n394:             self.memory_log.batch_update_with_outcomes(updates)\n395: \n396:     def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n397:                                    curr_date: str | None = None) -> str:\n398:         \"\"\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\n399: \n400:         Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\n401:         context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\n402:         hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). Options are:\n68:                 - \"market\": Market analyst\n69:                 - \"social\": Social media analyst\n70:                 - \"news\": News analyst\n71:                 - \"fundamentals\": Fundamentals analyst\n72:         \"\"\"\n73:         plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)\n74: \n75:         analyst_factories = {\n76:             \"market\": lambda: create_market_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n77:             \"social\": lambda: create_sentiment_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n78:             \"news\": lambda: create_news_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n79:             \"fundamentals\": lambda: create_fundamentals_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n80:         }\n81: \n82:         # Create researcher and manager nodes\n83:         bull_researcher_node = create_bull_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n84:         bear_researcher_node = create_bear_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n85:         research_manager_node = create_research_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n86:         trader_node = create_trader(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n87: \n88:         # Create risk analysis nodes\n89:         aggressive_analyst = create_aggressive_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n90:         neutral_analyst = create_neutral_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n91:         conservative_analyst = create_conservative_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n92:         portfolio_manager_node = create_portfolio_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n93: \n94:         # Create workflow\n95:         workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)\n96: \n97:         # Add analyst nodes to the graph\n98:         for spec in plan.specs:\n99:             workflow.add_node(spec.agent_node, analyst_factories[spec.key]())\n100:             workflow.add_node(spec.clear_node, create_msg_delete())\n101:             workflow.add_node(spec.tool_node, self.tool_nodes[spec.key])\n102: \n103:         # Add other nodes\n104:         workflow.add_node(\"Bull Researcher\", bull_researcher_node)\n105:         workflow.add_node(\"Bear Researcher\", bear_researcher_node)\n106:         workflow.add_node(\"Research Manager\", research_manager_node)\n107:         workflow.add_node(\"Trader\", trader_node)\n108:         workflow.add_node(\"Aggressive Analyst\", aggressive_analyst)\n109:         workflow.add_node(\"Neutral Analyst\", neutral_analyst)\n110:         workflow.add_node(\"Conservative Analyst\", conservative_analyst)\n111:         workflow.add_node(\"Portfolio Manager\", portfolio_manager_node)\n112: \n113:         # Define edges\n114:         # Start with the first analyst\n115:         workflow.add_edge(START, plan.specs[0].agent_node)\n116: \n117:         # Connect analysts in sequence\n118:         for i, spec in enumerate(plan.specs):\n119:             current_analyst = spec.agent_node\n120:             current_tools = spec.tool_node\n121:             current_clear = spec.clear_node\n122: \n123:             # Add conditional edges for current analyst\n124:             workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n125:                 current_analyst,\n126:                 getattr(self.conditional_logic, f\"should_continue_{spec.key}\"),\n127:                 [current_tools, current_clear],\n128:             )\n129:             workflow.add_edge(current_tools, current_analyst)\n130: \n131:             # Connect to next analyst or to Bull Researcher if this is the last analyst\n132:             if i < len(plan.specs) - 1:\n133:                 workflow.add_edge(current_clear, plan.specs[i + 1].agent_node)\n134:             else:\n135:                 workflow.add_edge(current_clear, \"Bull Researcher\")\n136: \n137:         # Both research-debate edges share the complete DEBATE_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n138:         for debate_node in (\"Bull Researcher\", \"Bear Researcher\"):\n139:             workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n140:                 debate_node,\n141:                 self.conditional_logic.should_continue_debate,\n142:                 DEBATE_PATH_MAP,\n143:             )\n144:         workflow.add_edge(\"Research Manager\", \"Trader\")\n145:         workflow.add_edge(\"Trader\", \"Aggressive Analyst\")\n146:         # All three risk edges share the complete RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n147:         for risk_node in (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"Conservative Analyst\", \"Neutral Analyst\"):\n148:             workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n149:                 risk_node,\n150:                 self.conditional_logic.should_continue_risk_analysis,\n151:                 RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP,\n152:             )\n153: \n154:         workflow.add_edge(\"Portfolio Manager\", END)\n155: \n156:         return workflow"

It is not\n28: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n29: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n30: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\n31: RATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n32: \n33: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n34: \n35: # Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n36: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator.\n37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n38:                               re.IGNORECASE)\n39: \n40: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n41: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n42: \n43: # Standalone 5-tier word anywhere (word boundaries so \"Buyer\"/\"Holding\" don't match).\n44: _RATING_WORD_RE = re.compile(\n45:     r\"\\b(\" + \"|\".join(RATINGS_5_TIER) + r\")\\b\", re.IGNORECASE\n46: )\n47: \n48: \n49: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n50:     \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from prose, or ``None`` if none is present.\n51: \n52:     Two-pass strategy on the NFKC-normalized text (so fullwidth punctuation like\n53:     ``Rating：Overweight`` is matched the same as ASCII):\n54:     1. An explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold).\n55:     2. The first standalone 5-tier rating word found anywhere.\n56:     \"\"\"\n57:     if not text:\n58:         return None\n59:     norm = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text)\n60: \n61:     # The labelled rating, taking the last one written: a decision states its\n62:     # rating after discussing the alternatives. Lines presenting the scale\n63:     # itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.\n64:     labelled = None\n65:     for line in norm.splitlines():\n66:         if _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line):\n67:             continue\n68:         m = _RATING_LABEL_RE.search(line)\n69:         if m and m.group(1).lower() in _RATING_SET:\n70:             labelled = m.group(1).capitalize()\n71:     if labelled:\n72:         return labelled\n73: \n74:     # No label. 循环，完成后经 \"Msg Clear X\" 进入下一个\n  → Bull Researcher ⇄ Bear Researcher（辩论轮数达 2×max_debate_rounds）\n  → Research Manager\n  → Trader\n  → Aggressive ⇄ Conservative ⇄ Neutral（风险辩论达 3×max_risk_discuss_rounds）\n  → Portfolio Manager → END\n```\n\n- `DEBATE_PATH_MAP` / `RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP` 覆盖全部路由目标，防止 speaker 标签漂移导致 LangGraph 崩溃（#1088）。\n- 状态定义在 CLI `run_analysis()` | 同一初始状态，但用 `graph.stream()` 逐节点消费、实时渲染 Rich 界面、回调统计、写 `message_tool.log` 与 `reports/`，`debug=True` |\n\n`structural-constraints.md` 明确警告：**不能假设 Web 路径与 `propagate()` `Hold`**（#1170）。\n- 结构化输出：`ResearchPlan`、`TraderProposal`、`PortfolioDecision`、`SentimentReport`，并有 `render_*` 还原成既有 markdown 结构，保证记忆/报告/显示兼容。\n\n### 4. 数据层（`src/tradingagents/dataflows/`）\n\n- `interface.py` 按类别/工具路由到 vendor 链；**配置里写哪些 vendor 就只用哪些**，不会静默回退到未选择的数据源（#988/#289）。\n- 错误语义区分：`NoMarketDataError`（符号/数据问题）vs `VendorRateLimitError`（供应商不可达）vs `VendorNotConfiguredError`；可选类别（宏观、预测市场）降级为 sentinel，核心类别抛错。\n- `NoMarketDataError` 会返回明确的 `NO_DATA_AVAILABLE` 指令文本，禁止模型估算或编造。\n- `safe_ticker_component()` 防止 ticker 路径穿越；`get_scrubbed()` 在异常中脱敏 API key（#1324）。\n\n### 5. 持久化与恢复\n\n- **决策记忆**：`agents/utils/memory.py`，追加式 Markdown；`[date | ticker | rating | pending]` → 结算后写入 raw/alpha/holding/`resolved:date`；支持按 `as_of` 做时点过滤（#1251）、条目轮转、临时文件 + `os.replace()` 原子替换。\n  - 已知限制：读-改-写，**原子替换不等于并发安全**；引入并发前必须定义写所有权与同步。\n- **Checkpoint**：每 ticker 一个 SQLite；`thread_id` 由 ticker+date+图形状签名（分析师组合、辩论轮数、资产类型、组合指纹）决定，避免错误恢复（#1089/#1249）。\n- **组合**：`portfolio.py` 的 `PortfolioContext` 严格区分\"未提供\"\"空仓\"\"有持仓\"三态；`fingerprint()` 为 12 位 sha256。\n- **回测**：`backtest.py` 只做评估，不是组合模拟器；独立 run 目录与独立记忆日志，不污染实盘日志；按评级统计方向命中率与均值 alpha，`REVIEW` 记为 unscored。\n- **报告**：`reporting.py` 输出 `1_analysts/ … 5_portfolio/` + `complete_report.md`。\n\n### 6. 配置与模型\n\n- `default_config.py` 是唯一默认配置源，`TRADINGAGENTS_*` 环境变量集中映射并强类型校验，非法值直接报错。\n- 默认目录在 `~/.tradingagents/`（logs/cache/memory）。\n- `llm_clients/` 支持 OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/xAI/DeepSeek/Qwen/GLM/MiniMax/OpenRouter/Ollama/Azure/Bedrock/OpenAI-compatible，能力与模型目录分离。\n\n---\n\n## 四、必须保留的业务语义\n\n1. `REVIEW` ≠ `Hold`，且不可据此交易。\n2. 时点约束：分析日期、数据 as-of、记忆 `resolved` 过滤都不能被新入口绕过。\n3. 未提供组合 ≠ 空仓；组合指纹影响恢复兼容性。\n4. 回测日志/产物与实盘隔离；网格用同一组合快照串行评估。\n5. ticker、run id、产物路径必须确定性校验，用户输入不能成为任意文件访问权限。\n6. 密钥只在服务端读取，不得进入客户端、事件、日志、报告、导出。\n7. 模型输出/外部文本是不可信输入，不是权限或架构变更授权。\n8. 记忆并发写入前必须先定义同步机制。\n\n---\n\n## 五、验证与 CI\n\n本地/CI               "content": "# TradingAgents WebUI Architecture Blueprint\n\nStatus: **Draft for human review.** This document records the confirmed requirements baseline and proposes a presentation-only architecture. It does not approve a web framework, a service implementation, a storage engine, an event transport, a frontend build system, or final module names. No product implementation may begin until the approval gates in Section 15 are satisfied.\n\nOwner: human project owner. Prepared by the Docs role on 2026-11-05.\n\n## 1. Authority and scope\n\nThis blueprint is subordinate to `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `.agent/rules.md`, `.opencode/rules.md`, and `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md`. It extends the TradingAgents v0.5.0 baseline at commit `2d17df8da1536c121e4d7395ac5a5dcec9e96d6f` on branch `feature/webui`. It does not replace the baseline, the CLI, the Python API, or any existing business rule.\n\nThe WebUI is a **local, single-user, single-active-run presentation layer**. Its job is to display and orchestrate capabilities that already exist. It must not add analysis capability, data sources, model providers, trading behaviour, or agent logic.\n\n## 2. Goals\n\n1. Expose the complete CLI analysis workflow through a browser: the eight selection steps, live run view, completion summary, and full I–V report.\n2. Preserve every deterministic boundary already enforced by the core and CLI: ticker and path validation, analysis-date limits, rating integrity, portfolio semantics, point-in-time data access, memory isolation, and checkpoint behaviour.\n3. Keep the core and CLI unchanged. The WebUI may call existing public Python interfaces, read existing artifacts, and write only the artifact types the CLI already writes.\n4. Provide read-only history over existing artifacts without introducing a new database or changing retention.\n5. Expose the existing backtest capability with the same parameters and result semantics as the CLI.\n6. Keep secrets server-side. The browser never receives provider keys or server filesystem paths.\n7. Support Chinese/English UI switching, independent of the report output language.\n\n## 3. Non-goals\n\nThe following are explicitly out of scope for this iteration:\n\n- Trading execution, order placement, position changes, or brokerage integration.\n- New data vendors, model providers, model catalogues, prompts, agents, or rating rules.\n- Multi-user accounts, tenants, billing, quotas, or authentication.\n- New databases, message queues, caches, or cross-process run persistence.\n- Cloud deployment, container orchestration, domain/TLS provisioning, or CI/CD release automation.\n- PDF or Word export; native mobile applications.\n- Multi-ticker batch analysis outside the existing backtest command.\n- Cross-run comparison, scoring dashboards, or backtest charts beyond the confirmed result view.\n- Any change to CLI arguments, defaults, output, exit codes, or core behaviour.\n\n## 4. Baseline code facts that constrain the design\n\nThese facts are derived from the current source and must be treated as constraints, not preferences.\n\n| Fact | Evidence | Consequence |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Core configuration is a module-level singleton | `src/tradingagents/dataflows/config.py` (`_config`, `set_config`) | Two graphs with different configs must not run concurrently in one process. |\n| The CLI message buffer is a module-level singleton | `src/cli/main.py` (`message_buffer = MessageBuffer()`) | The web layer must own its own run state and must not reuse this object. |\n| The CLI streams the graph directly | `src/cli/main.py` (`run_analysis`, `graph.graph.stream`) | The CLI path is the behavioural reference for live updates; it is not identical to `propagate()`. |\n| `propagate()` writes a state log | `src/tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` (`_log_state`) | API-style runs may have `full_states_log_*.json`; CLI-style runs do not. |\n| Decision memory is read-modify-write with atomic replacement | `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py` | Concurrent writers are not proven safe; the single-run rule protects the log. |\n| Checkpoints are per-ticker SQLite databases | `src/tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py` | A run can resume only when checkpointing was enabled and the process that owns it is available. |\n| Report serialization is shared | `src/tradingagents/reporting.py` (`write_report_tree`) | The web layer must call this writer rather than reimplement section layout. |\n| Path safety is deterministic | `src/tradingagents/dataflows/utils.py` (`safe_ticker_component`) | The web layer must reuse it for every ticker/run-id path component. |\n| Rating extraction is deterministic | `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/rating.py` | The web layer must not infer or \"repair\" a rating. |\n| Portfolio states are distinct | `src/tradingagents/portfolio.py` | No portfolio, an empty book, and a populated book are three different inputs. |\n\n## 5. System context\n\n```\nBrowser\n  |  same-origin HTTP + server-to-client event stream\n  v\nWeb presentation layer (new, outside src/tradingagents and src/cli)\n  |-- Configuration projection (read-only)\n  |-- Run coordinator (single active run)\n  |-- Event projection\n  |-- Artifact read model\n  |-- Backtest surface\n  v\nExisting public Python interfaces and on-disk artifacts\n  |-- TradingAgentsGraph (public methods)\n  |-- run_backtest / summarize\n  |-- write_report_tree\n  |-- TradingMemoryLog (read/write through existing graph methods only)\n  |-- results_dir, checkpoint directory, CLI preferences\n```\n\nThe browser never imports Python, never receives a server path, and never receives a secret. The core never imports the web layer.\n\n## 6. Logical components\n\n### 6.1 W1 — Entry and parameter surface {#w1-entry-and-parameter-surface}\n\nResponsibility: render the eight selection steps, validate inputs, and submit a run request.\n\nInputs: ticker, analysis date, output language, analyst selection, research depth, provider and endpoint, quick/deep model, provider thinking parameters, checkpoint flag, portfolio JSON, and the announcement acknowledgement.\n\nOutputs: a validated run request or a field-level error.\n\nBoundaries:\n- Validation mirrors the CLI and core rules; it does not replace them. The core remains authoritative.\n- The provider/API-key step is deliberately different from the CLI: the web surface displays \"configured / not configured\" from the server environment and never accepts a key.\n- Environment-locked values are shown as locked with their source, matching the CLI's \"from environment\" messages.\n- Crypto detection filters out the fundamentals analyst, matching `filter_analysts_for_asset_type`.\n\nFailure modes: invalid ticker, future date, no analyst, unknown provider/model, invalid portfolio, missing server key (allowed to start, fails at the first provider call, matching the CLI).\n\n### 6.2 W2 — Run coordinator {#w2-run-coordinator}\n\nResponsibility: own the lifecycle of the single active analysis run.\n\nInputs: a validated run request.\nOutputs: a run record, an event sequence, and final artifacts.\n\nOwnership:\n- Creates one fresh `TradingAgentsGraph` per run.\n- Calls the existing state construction path (`create_run_state`), checkpoint methods (`begin_checkpoint`, `checkpoint_input`, `end_checkpoint`, `clear_checkpoint_on_success`), the graph stream, `record_decision`, `process_signal`, and `write_report_tree`.\n- Owns cancellation, completion, failure, and reattachment.\n- Holds run state in process memory only.\n\nRules:\n- At most one run may be active. A second submission is rejected with a conflict error.\n- A browser disconnect does not cancel the run. The coordinator continues consuming the stream.\n- Cancellation follows CLI `Ctrl-C` semantics: stop consuming, do not call `record_decision`, do not clear the checkpoint, end the checkpoint scope, and keep artifacts already written.\n- The coordinator never fabricates a rating. It reads the deterministic signal from the existing processor and surfaces `REVIEW` as a review state.\n- The coordinator must not write `full_states_log_*.json` unless it deliberately uses the `propagate()` path; the chosen path and its artifact consequences must be explicit in the implementation plan.\n\n### 6.3 W3 — Configuration projection {#w3-configuration-projection}\n\nResponsibility: present the effective configuration and choices without becoming a second source of truth.\n\nRules:\n- Reads `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `TRADINGAGENTS_*` environment overrides, the provider table, the model catalogue, and `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json`.\n- Never writes the core configuration singleton except indirectly through constructing `TradingAgentsGraph`, which the existing code already does.\n- Environment precedence is displayed, not re-implemented differently.\n- The CLI preferences file is read-only for the web layer; whether web runs update it is a pending decision.\n\n### 6.4 W4 — Event projection {#w4-event-projection}\n\nResponsibility: translate graph stream chunks into a stable server-to-client event sequence.\n\nEvent envelope fields (minimum): `run_id`, `seq`, `timestamp`, `type`, `payload`.\n\nRequired event types:\n\n| Type | Payload (minimum) |\n| --- | --- |\n| `run.started` | ticker, trade_date, asset_type, analysts, depth, provider, models, checkpoint flag |\n| `run.resumed` | checkpoint step or \"fresh\" |\n| `agent.status` | agent, status in {pending, in_progress, completed} |\n| `message` | timestamp, message type, content |\n| `tool_call` | timestamp, tool name, arguments |\n| `report.section` | section key, title, content |\n| `stats` | agents completed/total, llm calls, tool calls, tokens in/out, reports completed/total, elapsed |\n| `run.completed` | final signal, review flag, wall-time summary, artifact references |\n| `run.failed` | error category, safe message |\n| `run.cancelled` | cancellation point |\n| `announcement` | sanitized announcement payload |\n\nRules:\n- Events are ordered by `seq`; reattachment replays from the last acknowledged sequence.\n- The stream is one-way (server to client). Client actions use separate request endpoints.\n- Event payloads must not contain secrets, absolute server paths, stack traces, or raw credentials.\n- The event buffer is bounded; if a client falls too far behind, the server sends a snapshot event rather than unbounded memory growth.\n- The transport is not selected by this blueprint. The contract above is transport-neutral.\n\n### 6.5 W5 — Artifact read model {#w5-artifact-read-model}\n\nResponsibility: read existing artifacts for completion views and history.\n\nSources:\n- Run directory: `<results_dir>/<ticker>/<date>/` with `message_tool.log` and `reports/*.md`.\n- API-style state log: `<results_dir>/<ticker>/TradingAgentsStrategy_logs/full_states_log_<date>.json` when present.\n- Saved report tree: `<results_dir>/reports/<ticker>_<timestamp>/` with `1_analysts` … `5_portfolio` and `complete_report.md`.\n- Backtest run: `<results_dir>/backtest/<run_id>/` and its `trading_memory.md`.\n- Decision memory: `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`, read-only.\n\nRules:\n- Read-only. No deletion, rotation, migration, or index database.\n- The model exposes stable artifact identifiers; it never returns absolute paths to the browser.\n- Every identifier resolves through a validated allowlist of roots and path components.\n- Missing optional artifacts are reported as absent, not synthesized.\n- History must work for CLI-style runs that lack `full_states_log_*.json`.\n\n### 6.6 W6 — Backtest surface {#w6-backtest-surface}\n\nResponsibility: launch and display existing backtests.\n\nRules:\n- Parameters mirror the CLI: tickers, start, end, every, analysts, asset type, portfolio, run id.\n- The summary mirrors `summarize(...)`: resolved, pending, unscored, per-rating count/hit rate/mean alpha, holding window, failures, settlement failures, and log path.\n- Backtest and live analysis remain isolated. The web layer must not point a backtest at the live memory log.\n- A backtest is a run for the single-active-run rule.\n- Whether a backtest can be cancelled with the same semantics as an analysis is a pending decision; if implemented, `run_id` resume must remain available.\n\n### 6.7 W7 — Security boundary {#w7-security-boundary}\n\nResponsibilities and rules:\n\n1. **Network**: bind to `127.0.0.1` only. Reject non-loopback `Host` headers. No authentication is required by the confirmed scope, so the loopback and same-origin checks are mandatory compensating controls.\n2. **Secrets**: provider keys come only from the server environment. The browser receives a boolean/status, never a value. Errors and events are redacted.\n3. **Paths**: the browser receives artifact identifiers, not filesystem paths. Server-side resolution uses `safe_ticker_component` and a root allowlist.\n4. **Untrusted content**: model output, tool output, announcements, and artifact text are data. Render as escaped text or a sanitized Markdown subset. No raw HTML, no script execution, no `javascript:` or `data:` links, no server-side template evaluation of model text.\n5. **Requests**: state-changing requests require same-origin checks; no wildcard CORS. Request size and event buffer size are bounded.\n6. **Files**: no generic file browser, upload-to-server-path, or download-by-path endpoint. Uploads are parsed as portfolio JSON and discarded after validation.\n7. **Logging**: logs must not contain keys, cookies, authorization headers, server absolute paths, or full model prompts controlled by third parties.\n\n### 6.8 W8 — Frontend {#w8-frontend}\n\nResponsibility: present the wizard, live view, report, history, backtest, announcements, errors, and language switch.\n\nRules:\n- UI state is derived from server events and snapshots; the frontend does not compute ratings or business decisions.\n- The live view mirrors the TUI's information set: progress table, messages and tools, current report, footer statistics.\n- The report view mirrors sections I–V and the complete report.\n- History and backtest views are read-only.\n- Chinese/English strings are UI-only; report content follows the existing output-language setting.\n- The frontend must remain usable when the event stream reconnects; it requests a snapshot after reconnect.\n\n## 7. Proposed ownership paths (pending approval)\n\nThe following paths are proposals for the implementation plan. They are not approved module names.\n\n| Element | Proposed path | Boundary |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Web package (presentation only) | `src/tradingagents_web/` | Must never be imported by `src/tradingagents/` or `src/cli/`. |\n| Run coordinator and lifecycle | `src/tradingagents_web/run/` | Owns in-process run state. |\n| HTTP surface and validation | `src/tradingagents_web/http/` | Owns request parsing and error mapping. |\n| Event projection | `src/tradingagents_web/events/` | Owns the event envelope and buffer. |\n| Artifact read model | `src/tradingagents_web/artifacts/` | Read-only filesystem access through a root allowlist. |\n| Backtest surface | `src/tradingagents_web/backtest/` | Wraps `run_backtest` and `summarize`. |\n| Frontend assets | `src/tradingagents_web/static/` and `src/tradingagents_web/templates/` | No server Python or secrets. |\n| Offline contract tests | `test/offline/test_web_*.py` | Deterministic, no network. |\n| Live tests | `test/live/test_web_live.py` | Requires external-service and cost authorization. |\n\nWhy `src/tradingagents_web/`: the existing setuptools package discovery includes `tradingagents*` and `cli*`; a sibling `tradingagents_web` package is includable without changing `pyproject.toml`. The structural check forbids `src/tradingagents/` from importing presentation frameworks; keeping the web package outside that tree preserves the rule. If the implementation instead chooses a path that requires a packaging change, that change needs explicit approval.\n\n## 8. Interface contracts\n\n### 8.1 Run request {#run-request}\n\nRequired fields: confirmed run parameters plus a client request id for idempotency. Optional: portfolio object, checkpoint flag.\n\nValidation:\n- Ticker: same charset/length rules as the CLI, then canonicalization.\n- Date: `YYYY-MM-DD`, not in the future.\n- Analysts: at least one known key; crypto excludes fundamentals.\n- Depth: one of 1, 3, 5.\n- Provider/model: must resolve through the existing provider/catalogue code.\n- Portfolio: validated by `PortfolioContext`; three states preserved.\n- No client-supplied filesystem path is accepted.\n\nErrors: field-level validation errors before a run starts; a conflict error when a run is already active.\n\n### 8.2 Run state {#run-state}\n\nStates: `idle`, `starting`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.\n\nOnly one run may be in `starting` or `running`.\n\nA run record contains: `run_id`, request fields, `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_seq`, `signal`, `review`, `artifact_ids`, and a safe error category.\n\n### 8.3 Cancellation {#cancellation}\n\n1. Stop consuming the graph stream.\n2. End the checkpoint scope in a `finally` block.\n3. Do not call `record_decision`.\n4. Do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`.\n5. Keep artifacts already written.\n6. Mark the run `cancelled` and publish `run.cancelled`.\n\nIf checkpointing was disabled, the run cannot be resumed. If it was enabled, the existing checkpoint remains available to the existing resume path.\n\n### 8.4 Reattachment {#reattachment}\n\n- The run continues while the server process lives.\n- A reconnecting client presents the run id and last seen sequence.\n- The server replays buffered events from that sequence or sends a snapshot.\n- After a server process restart, the run is gone; on-disk artifacts and checkpoints may remain for the existing CLI/API paths. Cross-process run recovery is out of scope.\n\n### 8.5 Report and artifact contract {#report-artifact-contract}\n\n- The web layer calls `write_report_tree` for the report tree; it does not reimplement section layout.\n- The run directory layout follows the CLI path.\n- Download is generated from an allowlisted artifact, not from a client-supplied path.\n- The complete report and a directory archive are the confirmed download forms.\n\n### 8.6 History contract {#history-contract}\n\n- History is a read-only projection over the sources in Section 6.5.\n- A history item is identified by a stable, validated artifact id.\n- Missing fields are shown as absent.\n- No delete, rename, move, retention change, or index write is permitted.\n\n### 8.7 Error taxonomy {#error-taxonomy}\n\n| Category | Meaning | Client behaviour |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `validation` | A request field is invalid | Show field errors; do not start |\n| `conflict` | A run is already active | Explain and offer to view the active run |\n| `not_found` | Run or artifact id does not resolve | Show a safe not-found message |\n| `config` | Provider/model/key configuration is unusable | Show the safe configuration error |\n| `upstream` | Data vendor or model provider failed | Show a safe retryable message; preserve the run record |\n| `storage` | Artifact write/read failed | Show a safe storage message; do not expose paths |\n| `cancelled` | The user cancelled | Show the cancellation state |\n| `internal` | Unexpected failure | Show a generic message; log a redacted diagnostic |\n\n## 9. State ownership and concurrency\n\n- The run coordinator owns the active run and the graph instance.\n- The core owns checkpoints and the decision log; the web layer calls the existing methods.\n- The artifact read model owns no writes.\n- The frontend owns only presentation state.\n- There is one process and one active run. This is the synchronization mechanism for the core's global configuration and the decision log.\n- If future work introduces concurrent runs, it must first define configuration isolation and memory write ownership; this blueprint does not authorize that change.\n\n## 10. Deterministic boundaries preserved\n\nThe web layer must call, not reimplement:\n\n- `_validate_trade_date`/date validation rules.\n- `safe_ticker_component` for every path component derived from user input.\n- `PortfolioContext` validation and fingerprinting.\n- `extract_rating`/`parse_rating` and the `REVIEW` sentinel.\n- `write_report_tree` for report layout.\n- `TradingMemoryLog` through the graph's existing methods.\n- `run_backtest` and `summarize` for backtest semantics.\n\nThe web layer must never:\n\n- Convert `REVIEW` to `Hold` or to a trade.\n- Treat an absent portfolio as a flat book.\n- Read the live memory log from a backtest.\n- Bypass point-in-time data filters.\n- Accept a ticker, run id, or path that the core would reject.\n\n## 11. Configuration and deployment\n\n- Default bind: `127.0.0.1`.\n- No authentication, by confirmed scope.\n- One process. No worker pool, no external broker.\n- Run state in memory. Restart loses active runs.\n- Existing `results_dir`, `data_cache_dir`, and `memory_log_path` defaults apply.\n- The web layer must not write `.env` or provider keys.\n- No container, cloud, domain, TLS, or orchestration work in this iteration.\n\n## 12. Dependency and packaging policy\n\n- No new runtime dependency is approved by this blueprint.\n- A web framework, ASGI/WSGI server, frontend build tool, or event-transport library requires an explicit dependency and architecture decision before use.\n- The implementation plan must state the exact dependency additions, versions ranges, rationale, license/security review, and fallback.\n- The core must not depend on the web layer or its framework.\n- If the selected framework cannot be packaged without changing `pyproject.toml`, that packaging change needs governance approval.\n\n## 13. Pending architecture decisions\n\nThese decisions are intentionally not made here. They block implementation until approved.\n\n1. Web framework and server.\n2. Event transport (for example SSE, WebSocket, or long polling) and reattachment mechanics.\n3. Frontend stack and build pipeline.\n4. Final module names and package path.\n5. Whether web runs update `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json`.\n6. Default UI language.\n7. Whether backtest supports the same cancellation control as analysis.\n8. Exact download packaging (single Markdown file, directory archive, or both).\n9. Event latency target (proposed: event-driven, p95 ≤ 1 s).\n10. Browser support matrix (confirmed: desktop modern browsers; exact versions to be recorded in tests).\n\n## 14. Verification strategy\n\n- Structural: source layout, dependency direction, permissions, lint, types, dependency audit.\n- Contract: request validation, event envelope, cancellation, reattachment, artifact identifiers, error taxonomy.\n- Regression: all existing offline tests; CLI help and import smoke checks.\n- Negative: every feature has at least one invalid-input or forbidden-action test.\n- Invariant: each `INV-WEB-*` has a test that fails when the invariant is violated.\n- Security: secret redaction, path traversal, Host header, same-origin, untrusted rendering.\n- Live: only with explicit external-service and cost authorization; skipped checks are reported as unrun.\n\nOffline tests must not use real networks, credentials, models, or user data. Use temporary directories and fakes.\n\n## 15. Approval gates\n\nBefore product implementation:\n\n1. This blueprint and the requirements registry are reviewed and approved by the human owner.\n2. The test plan and concrete test nodes are reviewed and approved.\n3. ADR-001 (web entry point and run-state ownership) is reviewed; safety-relevant changes need `[safety-approved]` on the final head.\n4. Any CI, permission, packaging, or developer-configuration change needs `[governance-approved]` on the final head.\n5. The requirements schema gate passes with the written registry.\n6. No implementation begins while a required decision in Section 13 is unresolved.\n\n## 16. Traceability\n\nThe requirement-to-component-to-test mapping is maintained in `docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md`. Invariants are in `docs/architecture/invariants.md`. The decision record is `docs/architecture/adr/001-choice.md`. Risks, runtime policies, memory ownership, options, and evaluation records are maintained in the corresponding documents under `docs/architecture/`.\n"

              "content": "# TradingAgents WebUI Invariants\n\nStatus: **Draft for human review.** These invariants extend the baseline safety boundaries to the new web presentation layer. They do not replace the baseline's own validation. Each invariant requires a violation test that fails when the invariant is broken. The test nodes named here are planned; they do not exist until the approved test plan is implemented.\n\n## INV-WEB-001 — Core and CLI behaviour is unchanged\n\nStatement: Adding the WebUI must not change the observable behaviour, arguments, defaults, output, exit codes, imports, or public contracts of `src/tradingagents/` or `src/cli/`.\n\nEnforcement point: The web package depends on existing public interfaces; it is never imported by the core or CLI. CI compares the core/CLI surface and runs the existing regression suite.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_contracts.py::test_core_and_cli_surface_unchanged` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Revert the web change; do not modify the core or CLI to accommodate presentation needs.\n\n## INV-WEB-002 — Model output is advisory, never execution authority\n\nStatement: No web control, event, report, or model response may place an order, change a position, or be treated as an instruction to execute a trade. The final rating remains an analysis output.\n\nEnforcement point: The web layer has no execution endpoint and no brokerage integration. Ratings are displayed, not acted on.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_security.py::test_no_execution_endpoint_exists` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Remove the offending endpoint or control; keep the rating advisory.\n\n## INV-WEB-003 — Secrets remain server-side\n\nStatement: Provider keys, tokens, authorization headers, cookies, and credential-like values must never appear in browser responses, events, logs, reports, downloads, errors, or snapshots.\n\nEnforcement point: Keys are read only from the server environment; serializers use an allowlist; error handlers redact credential-like values.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_security.py::test_secrets_never_serialized` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Remove the leaking field, rotate the credential if exposed, and add a regression test.\n\n## INV-WEB-004 — No server filesystem path reaches the browser\n\nStatement: Browser-visible payloads contain artifact identifiers, never absolute or repository-relative filesystem paths.\n\nEnforcement point: The artifact read model returns opaque, validated identifiers; downloads resolve identifiers server-side.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_security.py::test_responses_contain_no_filesystem_paths` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Replace the path with an identifier and re-run the security tests.\n\n## INV-WEB-005 — Path and identifier validation remains deterministic\n\nStatement: Every ticker, run identifier, artifact identifier, and path component derived from user input is validated by the existing deterministic rules before filesystem use. User input never grants file-access authority.\n\nEnforcement point: `safe_ticker_component`, root allowlists, and artifact-id resolution.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_security.py::test_path_traversal_is_rejected` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Reject the request; do not fall back to a broader path.\n\n## INV-WEB-006 — Portfolio states remain distinct\n\nStatement: An omitted portfolio, an explicitly empty book, and a populated book remain three different inputs across the web layer, the graph, checkpoint signatures, and stored artifacts.\n\nEnforcement point: `PortfolioContext` validation and fingerprinting are reused; the web request model distinguishes absent from empty.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_portfolio.py::test_three_portfolio_states_remain_distinct` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Reject the request rather than coercing an absent portfolio to flat.\n\n## INV-WEB-007 — REVIEW is not Hold and not a position\n\nStatement: When the final decision has no recognizable rating, the web layer displays and records `REVIEW`. It must not substitute `Hold`, a tradeable signal, or a fabricated rating.\n\nEnforcement point: The deterministic `extract_rating`/`parse_rating` result is passed through unchanged.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_contracts.py::test_review_is_not_hold` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Show the review warning and retain the raw decision text.\n\n## INV-WEB-008 — Backtest and live artifacts stay isolated\n\nStatement: A backtest uses its own run directory and memory log; it never reads or writes the live decision log, and live analysis never reads backtest artifacts as past context.\n\nEnforcement point: `run_backtest` and its isolated configuration are reused without redirection.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_backtest.py::test_backtest_does_not_touch_live_memory` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Abort the backtest; report the isolation failure.\n\n## INV-WEB-009 — At most one active run; no concurrent writes\n\nStatement: At most one analysis or backtest run is active in the server process. No concurrent writes to the decision log, checkpoints, or shared core configuration may occur.\n\nEnforcement point: The run coordinator admits one run and rejects conflicts.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_runs.py::test_second_run_is_rejected` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Reject the second request; do not queue silently.\n\n## INV-WEB-010 — Cancellation never records a decision or clears a checkpoint\n\nStatement: Cancelling a run stops execution and preserves the existing checkpoint when checkpointing was enabled. It must not write a decision-log entry and must not clear a checkpoint.\n\nEnforcement point: The cancellation path skips `record_decision` and `clear_checkpoint_on_success`, and ends the checkpoint scope in a `finally` block.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_runs.py::test_cancel_preserves_checkpoint_and_writes_no_decision` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Mark the run failed/cancelled; do not retry automatically.\n\n## INV-WEB-011 — History is read-only\n\nStatement: The history and backtest history views never delete, rename, move, rotate, or rewrite existing artifacts. They do not create an index database.\n\nEnforcement point: The artifact read model exposes reads only.\n\nViolation test: `test/offline/test_web_history.py::test_history_endpoints_are_read_only` (planned).\n\nFallback action: Remove the mutating capability and restore the artifact from a backup if needed.\n\n## INV-WEB-012 — Untrusted content is data, not authority or code\n\nStatement: Model output, tool output, announcements, artifact text, and user-provided portfolio text are rendered as data. No requirement is approved or implemented.\n# Sources of truth: AGENTS.md, Prompt.md, docs/code-governance/*, and the\n# confirmed requirements discussion of 2026-11-05.\nschema_version: '1.0'\nproject:\n  name: TradingAgents WebUI\n  purpose: >-\n    Add a local, single-user, single-active-run web presentation layer over the\n    existing TradingAgents analysis, reporting, memory, checkpoint, and backtest\n    capabilities without changing the core or CLI behavior.\n  baseline_ref: release\n  baseline_commit: 2d17df8da1536c121e4d7395ac5a5dcec9e96d6f\n  scope:\n    - >-\n      An eight-step analysis parameter wizard equivalent to the CLI, with\n      server-side API-key status in place of interactive key entry.\n    - >-\n      Live run progress, messages, tool calls, current report, and footer\n      statistics equivalent to the CLI live view.\n    - >-\n      Checkpoint controls, portfolio JSON input, cancellation, and a single\n      active run.\n    - >-\n      Completion summary, the complete I-V report, fixed-directory persistence,\n      and browser downloads.\n    - >-\n      Read-only history over existing artifacts, without a new database or\n      retention policy.\n    - >-\n      Backtest launch and result views equivalent to the CLI backtest command.\n    - Chinese/English interface switching.\n    - Local loopback deployment without authentication for one user.\n  out_of_scope:\n    - Trading execution, order placement, or position changes.\n    - New data sources, model providers, agents, prompts, or rating rules.\n    - Multi-user, multi-tenant, billing, or authentication.\n    - New databases, message queues, cloud deployment, or container orchestration.\n    - PDF or Word export, and native mobile applications.\n    -
