              "path": "[LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents/docs/architecture/adr/001-choice.md",
              "content": "# ADR-001: Web Entry Point and Run-State Ownership\n\n- Status: Proposed for human review. Not approved.\n- Date: 2026-11-05\n- Baseline: TradingAgents v0.5.0, commit `2d17df8da1536c121e4d7395ac5a5dcec9e96d6f`\n- Related requirements: `REQ-WEB-001` through `REQ-WEB-014`, `REQ-WEB-020` through `REQ-WEB-031`\n- Related invariants: `INV-WEB-001` through `INV-WEB-012`\n- Related blueprint: `architecture-blueprint.md`\n\n## Context\n\nTradingAgents currently exposes one interactive entry point: the Typer/Rich CLI in `src/cli/`, backed by the Python API in `src/tradingagents/`. The project owner has confirmed a local, single-user WebUI that must display every capability already visible in the TUI without adding analysis capability, data sources, models, agent logic, or trading behavior. The core and CLI must remain unchanged.\n\nThree facts make the entry point and state ownership decisions safety-relevant:\n\n1. `src/tradingagents/dataflows/config.py` stores configuration in a process-global singleton. Two graphs with different configurations cannot safely run concurrently in one process.\n2. `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py` updates the decision log with read-modify-write plus atomic replacement. Atomic replacement prevents torn files, not lost updates from concurrent writers.\n3. The CLI owns a module-level `message_buffer` singleton and streams the graph directly. That buffer cannot serve multiple runs, and the CLI stream path is not automatically equivalent to `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()`.\n\nThe WebUI therefore needs its own presentation entry point and run-state owner, while reusing the existing deterministic business logic.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **Add a presentation-only web package outside the core.** The proposed path is `src/tradingagents_web/`. It may import `tradingagents` and `cli` public interfaces; neither `src/tradingagents/` nor `src/cli/` may import it. This keeps the structural rule that the core does not depend on presentation frameworks.\n2. **Use one in-process run coordinator.** The coordinator owns the single active analysis or backtest, creates one fresh `TradingAgentsGraph` per run, consumes its stream, and publishes a bounded event sequence. A second submission is rejected with a conflict error. This single-run rule is the synchronization mechanism for the global configuration and decision log.\n3. **Reuse existing public methods.** The coordinator calls `create_run_state`, `begin_checkpoint`, `checkpoint_input`, `graph.stream`, `record_decision`, `clear_checkpoint_on_success`, `end_checkpoint`, `process_signal`, `write_report_tree`, `run_backtest`, and `summarize` rather than reimplementing their semantics.\n4. **Keep run state in memory only.** A browser disconnect does not cancel the run; the client can reattach within the server process lifetime. After a process restart, the active run is not recovered. On-disk artifacts and checkpoints remain available to the existing CLI/API paths.\n5. **Expose history as a read-only projection.** History reads existing run directories, saved report trees, backtest runs, and the decision memory. It creates no database, index, or retention policy and performs no deletions.\n6. **Treat the browser as an untrusted presentation client.** The server binds only to `127.0.0.1`, rejects non-loopback Host headers and cross-origin state-changing requests, never sends provider keys or server filesystem paths, and renders model/external text as escaped data or a sanitized Markdown subset.\n7. **Use server environment variables for provider keys.** The web layer does not accept, persist, or return keys. It displays configured/not-configured status and allows a run to start without a key, matching the CLI's skip behavior; the first provider call then fails safely.\n8. **Preserve cancellation semantics.** Cancellation stops the stream, writes no decision-log entry, clears no checkpoint, ends the checkpoint scope, and keeps artifacts already written.\n\n## Consequences\n\n### Positive\n\n- The core and CLI remain byte-for-byte behaviorally unchanged, so existing tests and consumers keep their contracts.\n- The single-run rule avoids unproven concurrency in the global configuration and decision log.\n- Reusing existing writers and validators avoids a second report format and a second rating parser.\n- Read-only history adds discoverability without a new storage system.\n- Server-only keys and loopback binding keep the credential and network surface small.\n\n### Negative / costs\n\n- Analyses cannot run in parallel; a second request is rejected rather than queued.\n- A server restart loses active runs. Recovery remains a CLI/API capability, not a web capability.\n- The web UI cannot complete the CLI's interactive API-key prompt; users must configure keys in the server environment.\n- The event buffer and snapshot logic add memory-management work.\n- A sanitizer and a strict identifier layer are required for safe rendering and file access.\n\n### Risks and mitigations\n\n- **Localhost is not a complete security boundary.** Mitigate with loopback-only binding, Host header validation, same-origin state-changing requests, no wildcard CORS, and no secrets in responses.\n- **Event loss on reconnect.** Mitigate with monotonic sequence numbers and snapshot fallback.\n- **Artifact path traversal.** Mitigate by never accepting paths from the browser and resolving identifiers through `safe_ticker_component` and an allowlist.\n- **Model output injection.** Mitigate by escaping or sanitizing all untrusted content and rejecting unsafe URL schemes.\n- **Accidental core modification.** Mitigate with the structural gate and a contract test that compares the core/CLI surface.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. **Run the web layer inside `src/tradingagents/`.** Rejected: the structural check forbids core imports of presentation frameworks, and it would invert the dependency direction.\n2. **Reuse `propagate()` only.** Rejected as the sole path: the CLI's live display depends on streamed chunks. The implementation may still choose a path after contract tests prove artifact and cancellation equivalence.\n3. **Add a database for run state and history.** Rejected: it would create a second source of truth, require a storage design and dependency approval, and contradict the read-only-history decision.\n4. **Allow concurrent runs with per-run configuration.** Rejected for this iteration: it requires replacing the global configuration and defining memory write ownership, which is a core change outside the approved scope.\n5. **Accept API keys in the browser.** Rejected: it transmits plaintext credentials into a client surface and conflicts with the server-only secret boundary.\n\n## Approval\n\nThis ADR is a proposal. It requires human review. Because it introduces a new entry point that touches ratings, paths, secrets, cancellation, and recovery, the change is safety-relevant and needs a human `[safety-approved]` review on the final head before implementation. Any dependency, packaging, CI, or permission change additionally needs `[governance-approved]`.\n"

              "content": "# TradingAgents WebUI Runtime Policy Catalog\n\nStatus: **Draft for human review.** These policies describe how the proposed web layer must behave at runtime. They do not approve an implementation. Every policy names an enforcement point and a fallback action.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-001 — Loopback-only listener\n\nTrigger: server start.\nRule: bind to `127.0.0.1` only. Reject non-loopback `Host` headers. Do not enable wildcard CORS.\nEnforcement: startup configuration and request middleware.\nFallback: refuse to start on a non-loopback address.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-002 — Single active run\n\nTrigger: a new analysis or backtest request.\nRule: if a run is `starting` or `running`, reject the request with a conflict error that identifies the active run. Do not queue silently.\nEnforcement: run coordinator admission check.\nFallback: return the active run id so the client can reattach.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-003 — Process-lifetime run state\n\nTrigger: browser disconnect, refresh, or network loss.\nRule: continue the run; allow reattachment from the last acknowledged event sequence within the server process lifetime. A process restart loses the active run.\nEnforcement: run coordinator and event buffer.\nFallback: show \"run no longer available\"; on-disk artifacts and checkpoints remain for CLI/API paths.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-004 — Cancellation\n\nTrigger: an authenticated-by-origin cancel request for the active run.\nRule: stop consuming the stream; do not call `record_decision`; do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`; end the checkpoint scope; keep artifacts already written; mark the run `cancelled`.\nEnforcement: run coordinator cancellation path.\nFallback: if the stream cannot stop cleanly, mark the run failed and preserve artifacts; never write a synthetic decision.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-005 — Checkpoint controls\n\nTrigger: a checkpoint toggle or clear-all request.\nRule: the toggle affects the next run only. Clear-all requires explicit confirmation and is disabled while a run is active. Clear-all deletes all checkpoint databases, matching the CLI flag.\nEnforcement: request validation and run coordinator.\nFallback: reject a clear during a run; report the number of cleared databases.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-006 — Server-only provider keys\n\nTrigger: configuration display or a run start.\nRule: read keys only from the server environment. Display configured/not-configured status. Never accept, persist, return, log, or export a key. A missing key does not block the run; the first provider call fails safely.\nEnforcement: configuration projection and serializers.\nFallback: show a safe configuration error and keep the run record.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-007 — Deterministic identifiers\n\nTrigger: any ticker, run id, artifact id, or path component from a client.\nRule: validate with the existing deterministic rules before filesystem use. Reject absolute paths, `..`, backslashes, and values outside the allowlist.\nEnforcement: request validation and artifact resolver.\nFallback: reject the request; never widen the path.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-008 — Artifact identifiers, not paths\n\nTrigger: a response that references an artifact.\nRule: return a stable identifier, not an absolute or repository-relative path. Resolve downloads server-side.\nEnforcement: artifact read model and serializers.\nFallback: omit the artifact and show a safe not-found message.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-009 — Read-only history\n\nTrigger: a history or backtest-history request.\nRule: read only; no delete, rename, move, rotation, migration, or index write.\nEnforcement: artifact read model exposes reads only.\nFallback: reject any mutating request.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-010 — Backtest isolation\n\nTrigger: a backtest request.\nRule: use the backtest's own run directory and memory log; never read or write the live decision log. A backtest is a run for the single-active-run rule.\nEnforcement: backtest surface and run coordinator.\nFallback: abort the backtest and report the isolation failure.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-011 — Announcement handling\n\nTrigger: page load or announcement refresh.\nRule: fetch server-side from the existing endpoint; on failure use the existing fallback; if `require_attention` is true, block interaction until acknowledged; render as untrusted text.\nEnforcement: announcement service and frontend.\nFallback: show the fallback link and do not block.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-012 — Untrusted rendering\n\nTrigger: model output, tool output, announcement, artifact text, or portfolio text.\nRule: render as escaped text or a sanitized Markdown subset. No raw HTML, no script execution, no `javascript:` or `data:` links, no server-side template evaluation.\nEnforcement: frontend renderer and response encoders.\nFallback: render as plain text.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-013 — Error redaction\n\nTrigger: any validation, upstream, storage, or internal error.\nRule: return a safe category and message; redact keys, tokens, cookies, authorization headers, absolute paths, and stack traces.\nEnforcement: error mapper and logger.\nFallback: generic internal error with a correlation id.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-014 — Bounded event buffer\n\nTrigger: event publication.\nRule: keep a bounded buffer per run; when a client falls behind the retained window, send a snapshot instead of replaying indefinitely.\nEnforcement: event projection.\nFallback: drop the client to snapshot mode; keep the run alive.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-015 — No execution authority\n\nTrigger: any rating, report, or model output.\nRule: display only. No endpoint may place an order, change a position, or treat text as a command.\nEnforcement: route inventory and security tests.\nFallback: remove the endpoint or control.\n\n## WEB-POLICY-016 — Honest run state\n\nTrigger: completion, failure, or cancellation.\nRule: derive state from actual stream completion and artifact writes. Do not report an unreadable rating as a success position. Show partial artifacts as partial.\nEnforcement: run coordinator and report projection.\nFallback: show a failed/review state and preserve the raw decision text.\n"

              "content": "# TradingAgents WebUI Memory and State Design\n\nStatus: **Draft for human review.** This document describes the existing memory mechanisms the WebUI must reuse and the new in-memory run state it must own. It does not authorize a new persistence system.\n\n## 1. Existing decision memory\n\nThe baseline decision log is implemented by `TradingMemoryLog` in `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py`.\n\n- Storage: an append-only Markdown file, default `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`, overridable with `TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH`.\n- Write path: `store_decision()` appends a pending entry with a tag containing trade date, ticker, rating, and `pending`.\n- Settlement: `update_with_outcome()` or `batch_update_with_outcomes()` replaces the pending tag with realized raw return, alpha, holding window, and an optional `resolved:<date>` field, then appends a reflection.\n- Atomicity: the file is written to a temporary path and replaced with `os.replace()`. This prevents torn files, not lost updates from concurrent read-modify-write.\n- Point-in-time: `get_past_context(..., as_of=...)` includes only entries whose resolution date is on or before the analysis date. Live runs pass `None` and keep the legacy behavior.\n- Rotation: `memory_log_max_entries` optionally prunes the oldest resolved entries; pending entries are never pruned.\n\n## 2. Existing checkpoint state\n\n- Per-ticker SQLite databases under `<data_cache_dir>/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db`.\n- `thread_id(ticker, date, signature)` derives a deterministic id; the signature includes analyst selection, debate/risk rounds, asset type, and portfolio fingerprint.\n- Successful completion clears the run's checkpoint. Cancellation and failure leave it in place.\n- `clear_all_checkpoints()` removes the databases and their `-wal`/`-shm` companions.\n\n## 3. Existing CLI preferences\n\n- `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json` stores stable choices from the last CLI run.\n- It is convenience state, not authority. Unreadable content means no defaults.\n- The web layer may read it for prefill. Whether web runs write it is an open decision (blueprint Section 13).\n\n## 4. New web run state\n\nThe web layer owns one in-memory record for the single active run and a bounded event history.\n\nRequired fields:\n\n- `run_id`: server-generated, safe path component.\n- Request: ticker, trade date, asset type, analysts, depth, provider, models, output language, checkpoint flag, portfolio fingerprint.\n- Lifecycle: `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_seq`.\n- Result: final signal, review flag, safe error category, artifact identifiers.\n- Events: bounded sequence with a snapshot fallback.\n\nOwnership:\n\n- The run coordinator is the only writer of the active run record.\n- The event projection is the only writer of the event sequence.\n- The artifact read model never writes.\n- The frontend holds only presentation state.\n\n## 5. Concurrency and write ownership\n\nThe approved scope is one active run per process. This is the synchronization mechanism for:\n\n- the process-global configuration in `src/tradingagents/dataflows/config.py`;\n- the read-modify-write decision log;\n- checkpoint databases and the run-level event buffer.\n\nThe web layer must not introduce a second writer to the decision log. It writes through the existing graph methods (`record_decision`, `_resolve_pending_entries`) and never appends directly.\n\nConcurrent runs are out of scope. Introducing them would require, at minimum:\n\n1. per-run configuration isolation instead of the global singleton;\n2. a defined decision-log write owner or a serialized writer;\n3. per-run checkpoint and artifact namespaces that cannot collide;\n4. a concurrency test that fails on lost updates.\n\n## 6. Cancellation and failure\n\nCancellation is not a memory operation:\n\n- No decision entry is written.\n- No checkpoint is cleared.\n- Partial report files and the message log remain.\n- The run record is marked `cancelled`.\n\nFailure follows the same rule: no synthetic decision, no checkpoint clear, safe error category, partial artifacts preserved. A retry is a new run with a new request.\n\n## 7. Point-in-time integrity\n\nThe web layer must not bypass the baseline's date and point-in-time rules:\n\n- The analysis date validation remains in the core.\n- The `as_of` filter for past lessons remains in the graph's run-state construction.\n- Backtests keep their own log and their own date grid.\n- History reads stored artifacts; it does not reconstruct an outcome that was not recorded.\n\n## 8. Retention and deletion\n\n- Decision memory retention remains the existing configuration; the web layer does not expose deletion or rotation controls.\n- Checkpoint clearing is the only destructive control exposed, matching the CLI flag, with confirmation and a single-run guard.\n- History is read-only; it does not delete or rewrite run artifacts.\n- No new database, cache, or index is introduced.\n\n## 9. Recovery boundaries\n\n- A browser disconnect does not affect memory or checkpoints.\n- A server restart loses the in-memory run record and event buffer. The decision log and checkpoints on disk remain.\n- The existing CLI/API can resume a checkpointed run; the web layer does not claim cross-process recovery.\n"

after_seq: int) -> AsyncIterator[Event]\n```\n\n- **单活动运行**：`active` 为 `starting/running/cancelling` 时，新请求返回 `409 conflict`。\n- **同步图跑在 worker 线程**：LangGraph 的 stream 是同步生成器；用 `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`，通过 `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` 把事件推回事件循环。\n- **状态机**：`idle → starting → running → completed | failed | cancelled`。\n- **取消**：`threading.Event`，在每个 chunk 之间检查；设置后跳出循环，**不调用** `record_decision`、**不调用** `clear_checkpoint_on_success`，`finally` 中 `end_checkpoint()`；保留已写产物。\n- **失败**：同样不写决策、不清 Checkpoint；发 `run.failed`，只带安全错误分类与 correlation id。\n- **完成**：合并 values 流的所有 chunk 得到 `final_state`；`graph.process_signal()` 得到评级；`write_report_tree()` 自动保存到 `results_dir/reports/<ticker>_<timestamp>/`；发 `run.completed`。\n- **不写 `full_states_log_*.json`**：Web 走 CLI 的 stream 路径，不调用 `propagate()` 的 `_log_state`；历史必须兼容“没有 state log”的运行。\n\n### 4.4 执行体（对齐 CLI，但不复用 Rich）\n\n```python\ndef run_blocking(request, emit, cancel_event):\n    graph = TradingAgentsGraph(\n        selected_analysts, config=build_run_config(request), debug=False,\n        callbacks=[StatsCallbackHandler()],\n    )\n    init_state = graph.create_run_state(ticker, date, asset_type, portfolio)\n    args = graph.propagator.get_graph_args(callbacks=[stats])\n    tid = graph.begin_checkpoint(ticker, date, asset_type, portfolio)\n    if tid:\n        args[\"config\"][\"configurable\"][\"thread_id\"] = tid\n    emit(run_started_or_resumed(graph._resuming))\n    try:\n        for chunk in graph.graph.stream(graph.checkpoint_input(init_state), **args):\n            if cancel_event.is_set():\n                emit(run_cancelled())\n                return\n            project_chunk(chunk)   # 消息/工具/报告/状态/统计\n        final_state = merge(chunks)\n        graph.record_decision(ticker, date, final_state)\n        graph.clear_checkpoint_on_success(ticker, date, asset_type, portfolio)\n        emit(run_completed(...))\n    except Exception:\n        emit(run_failed(safe_category))\n    finally:\n        graph.end_checkpoint()\n```\n\n细节：\n\n- `debug=False`，不使用 `pretty_print`；Web 自己投影事件。\n- `create_run_state` 会结算 pending memory、注入 past context 与 instrument identity；这一步可能调用模型，因此先发 `run.preparing`。\n- 顺序与 CLI 一致：先 `create_run_state`，再 `get_graph_args`，再 `begin_checkpoint`。\n- `stream_mode=\"values\"`，每个 chunk 是累积状态；投影器按 message id 去重、按 section 内容变化去重。\n- `record_decision` 只在真正完成后调用；取消/失败不调用。\n- `write_report_tree` 失败不改变分析结果：`run.completed` 带 `warnings:[\"report_save_failed\"]`，错误写入服务端日志（脱敏）。\n\n### 4.5 事件投影\n\n输入：`chunk`（累积状态）。输出：事件列表。\n\n```text\n事件 envelope:\n{\n  \"run_id\": \"r_...\",\n  \"seq\": 42,\n  \"timestamp\": \"2026-11-05T12:34:56.789Z\",\n  \"type\": \"agent.status\",\n  \"payload\": { ... }\n}\n```\n\n| 事件 | 触发 | 关键字段 |\n|---|---|---|\n| `run.preparing` | 接受请求、构造 graph/初始状态 | ticker, date |\n| `run.started` | 开始消费 stream | 运行参数摘要 |\n| `run.resumed` | `graph._resuming` 为真 | checkpoint step |\n| `agent.status` | 状态变化 | agent, `pending/in_progress/completed` |\n| `message` | 新消息（按 id 去重） | timestamp, type, content |\n| `tool_call` | 工具调用 | timestamp, name, args |\n| `report.section` | section 内容变化 | section, title, markdown |\n| `stats` | 节流 500ms 或变化 | agents, llm_calls, tool_calls, tokens_in/out, reports, elapsed |\n| `run.completed` | 正常完成 | signal, review, wall_times, artifact_ids, warnings |\n| `run.failed` | 异常 | category, message, correlation_id |\n| `run.cancelled` | 取消 | cancelled_at |\n| `snapshot` | 重连/缓冲溢出 | 当前状态 + last_seq |\n| `heartbeat` | 15s | SSE 注释行 `: ping` |\n\n投影规则：\n\n- 消息去重：维护 `seen_message_ids`（与 CLI 的 `_processed_message_ids` 同义）。\n- 报告去重：`last_section_content[section]`，内容变化才发。\n- Agent 状态：按 `ANALYST_NODE_SPECS` + 固定团队维护；**不伪造 `error`**（CLI 也只定义颜色、从未设置该状态）。\n- 报告 section 映射与 CLI 一致：analyst reports、`investment_plan`、`trader_investment_plan`、`final_trade_decision`。\n- 统计复用 `StatsCallbackHandler`；wall time 复用 `AnalystWallTimeTracker` 与 `sync_analyst_tracker_from_chunk`。\n- 消息分类/内容提取/工具参数格式化：在 Web 层实现纯函数，并用契约测试对齐 `cli.main` 的行为。\n\n### 4.6 SSE 契约\n\n- `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events?after_seq=N`\n- Header：`Content-Type: text/event-stream`、`Cache-Control: no-cache`、`X-Accel-Buffering: no`\n- 格式：\n\n```text\nid: 42\nevent: agent.status\ndata: {\"run_id\":\"r_...\",\"seq\":42,...}\n\n: ping\n```\n\n- 重连：浏览器发 `Last-Event-ID`；服务端优先用 query `after_seq`，否则用 header。\n- 缓冲：每 run 一个有界 deque（10,000 条或 8 MB，取先到者）；客户端落后超出窗口时先发 `snapshot`，再发实时事件。\n- 每个订阅者一个有界 `asyncio.Queue`（1,000 条）；队列满则断开该客户端，强制 snapshot 重连，避免内存无界增长。\n- 取消/完成后保留缓冲一段时间（例如 5 分钟），便于重连；随后释放。\n\n### 4.7 取消语义\n\n与分析运行一致：\n\n1. 设置 `cancel_event`。\n2. 等待 worker 在当前 chunk 结束（模型调用可能正在进行，取消在 chunk 边界生效）。\n3. 不写决策记忆；不清 Checkpoint；`end_checkpoint()`。\n4. 保留已写的 `message_tool.log`、`reports/*.md`。\n5. 状态 `cancelled`；如启用 Checkpoint，可用相同参数恢复。\n6. 若 30s 内 worker 未退出，返回 `cancelling`，待其结束后再释放单运行槽位；**不杀线程**。\n\n**回测不提供取消**：`run_backtest()` 内部循环没有取消钩子；伪造“取消”会让人误以为已停止。回测只能等待完成，或由进程关闭中断后用 `run_id` 续跑。这是有意选择，避免误导。\n\n### 4.8 Checkpoint 控制\n\n- 运行请求带 `checkpoint: bool`，映射到 `config[\"checkpoint_enabled\"]`。\n- 运行开始事件显示 `run.resumed` 或 `run.started`，对齐 CLI 的“Resuming/Starting fresh”。\n- `POST /api/checkpoints/clear`，body `{\"confirm\": \"CLEAR\"}`：\n  - 有活动运行时返回 `409`；\n  - 否则调用 `clear_all_checkpoints(DEFAULT_CONFIG[\"data_cache_dir\"])`；\n  - 返回 `{cleared: n}`，不返回路径。\n- 不提供“按 ticker 预检 step”接口，避免复制核心的 signature 逻辑；恢复状态由运行事件呈现。\n\n### 4.9 Portfolio\n\n- `POST /api/portfolio/validate`，body `{\"json\": \"<raw text>\"}`：\n  - 限制 256 KB；\n  - `json.loads` → `PortfolioContext.model_validate`；\n  - 返回 `{valid, summary, fingerprint, has_cash, position_count}`；\n  - 三态严格保留：请求中 `portfolio: null` = 未提供；`{\"positions\": []}` = 空仓；有 positions = 有持仓。\n- 运行请求直接携带原始 JSON 字符串；后端再次校验，避免信任前端。\n- 上传文件在前端读为文本后走同一接口；后端不接收服务器路径，也不落盘上传文件。\n\n### 4.10 公告\n\n- `GET /api/announcements`：\n  - 服务端调用现有 `cli.announcements.fetch_announcements(url, timeout)`（在线程中执行，避免阻塞事件循环）；\n  - 60s 缓存；\n  - 失败返回 CLI 同款 fallback；\n  - `require_attention` 透传；内容按纯文本/受限 Markdown 返回。\n- 前端 `require_attention=true` 时弹阻塞模态框，确认后才能继续。\n\n### 4.11 历史与产物读取（只读）\n\n扫描根：\n\n```text\n<results_dir>/<ticker>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/            # CLI 运行目录\n<results_dir>/<ticker>/TradingAgentsStrategy_logs/full_states_log_<date>.json  # API 运行（可选）\n<results_dir>/reports/<ticker>_<timestamp>/    # 手动/自动保存的报告树\n<results_dir>/backtest/<run_id>/               # 回测 run\n~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md      # 决策记忆（只读）\n```\n\n- 扫描上限：最多 500 个 run，按 mtime 倒序；分页 `limit=50`。\n- `artifact_id = sha256(相对路径)[:16]`；服务端每次扫描重建映射。**不把路径编码后发给浏览器**，也不持久化索引。\n- 详情：\n  - 运行目录：读 `reports/*.md`（section key 文件名）、`message_tool.log`、可选 state log；\n  - 保存目录：读 `1_analysts/…`、`2_research/…`、`3_trading/…`、`4_risk/…`、`5_portfolio/…`、`complete_report.md`；\n  - 回测：读 `trading_memory.md`，用 `summarize()` 得到结构化统计。\n- 评级：用 `extract_rating()`；无评级显示 `REVIEW`，绝不补 `Hold`。\n- 状态：有完整 final decision 为 `completed`；只有部分 section 为 `partial`；无法判断为 `unknown`。\n- 下载：\n  - `complete`：存在 `complete_report.md` 时直接返回；\n  - `archive`：内存 zip 打包现有报告文件；\n  - `section`：按白名单 section key 返回单个 md；\n  - 不合成不存在的完整报告。\n- 决策记忆页：只读解析 tag + DECISION/REFLECTION，不写、不轮转。\n\n### 4.12 回测\n\n- `POST /api/backtests` 参数对齐 CLI：\n  `tickers, start, end, every, analysts, asset_type, portfolio, run_id`。\n- 在 worker 中调用：\n  ```python\n  dates = iter_grid(start, end, every)\n  result = run_backtest(names, dates, config, asset_type, portfolio, selected_analysts, run_id)\n  summary = summarize(TradingMemoryLog({\"memory_log_path\": str(result.log_path)}))\n  ```\n- 返回结构化字段：`run_id, cells_run, skipped, resolved, pending, unscored, by_rating, holding, failures, settlement_failures`。\n- **不返回 `log_path`**；返回 artifact id 用于下载 `trading_memory.md`。\n- 进度：v1 使用不确定进度条 + 预期 cell 数；可选 Phase 3 增加只读 watcher，轮询 run 的 memory 文件计数，发 `backtest.progress`。\n- 回测占用同一个单运行槽位。\n\n### 4.13 API 清单\n\n| Method | Path | 用途 | 备注 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| GET | `/api/health` | 健康/版本/活动 run | 无敏感信息 |\n| GET | `/api/session` | CSRF token、服务器时间 | 同源 |\n| GET | `/api/config` | 默认值、provider、env 锁、key 状态、prefs | 不含路径/密钥 |\n| GET | `/api/config/models` | 按 provider/mode 列模型 | OpenRouter 服务端拉取 |\n| GET | `/api/announcements` | 公告 | 60s 缓存 |\n| POST | `/api/portfolio/validate` | 校验粘贴/上传 JSON | 256 KB 上限 |\n| POST | `/api/runs` | 发起分析 | 单运行；幂等 request id |\n| GET | `/api/runs/active` | 当前活动 run 快照 | 无则 204/空 |\n| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}` | run 快照 | 重连用 |\n| GET | `/api/runs/{run_id}/events` | SSE | `after_seq` / `Last-Event-ID` |\n| POST | `/api/runs/{run_id}/cancel` | 取消分析 | CLI 等价语义 |\n| POST | `/api/checkpoints/clear` | 清空全部 Checkpoint | `{\"confirm\":\"CLEAR\"}` |\n| GET | `/api/history` | 历史列表 | 只读、分页 |\n| GET | `/api/history/{artifact_id}` | 历史详情 | 只读 |\n| GET | `/api/history/{artifact_id}/download` | 下载 | `kind=complete|archive|section` |\n| GET | `/api/backtests` | 回测列表 | 只读 |\n| POST | `/api/backtests` | 发起回测 | 单运行 |\n| GET | `/api/backtests/{run_id}` | 回测详情/摘要 | 只读 |\n| GET | `/api/backtests/{run_id}/events` | 回测 SSE | 进度/完成 |\n\n### 4.14 错误模型\n\n```json\n{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"category\": \"validation|conflict|not_found|config|upstream|storage|cancelled|internal\",\n    \"message\": \"safe message\",\n    \"fields\": {\"ticker\": \"invalid symbol\"},\n    \"correlation_id\": \"c_...\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n- 422：Pydantic 字段错误。\n- 409：已有活动运行。\n- 404：artifact/run 不存在。\n- 403：Host/Origin/CSRF 拒绝。\n- 413：请求体过大。\n- 502：上游模型/数据失败（安全消息）。\n- 500：内部错误（只给 correlation id，不返回堆栈）。\n\n---\n\n## 5. 前端设计\n\n### 5.1 路由\n\n| 路由 | 页面 |\n|---|---|\n| `/` | New Analysis：8 步向导 + 当前活动 run 入口 |\n| `/runs/:runId` | Live Run：进度、消息/工具、当前报告、统计、取消 |\n| `/runs/:runId/report` | Report：I–V 分栏 + 完整报告 + 下载 |\n| `/history` | History：run/保存报告/回测列表、筛选 |\n| `/history/:artifactId` | History Detail：报告、元数据、下载 |\n| `/backtest` | Backtest：表单 + 历史回测 |\n| `/backtest/:runId` | Backtest Detail：评级统计、失败项、日志下载 |\n| `/decisions` | Decision Memory：只读决策日志（可选 Phase 3） |\n\n### 5.2 页面结构\n\n**App Shell**\n\n- 左侧导航：New Analysis / History / Backtest / Decision Memory。\n- 顶部：产品名、活动 run 指示、连接状态、语言切换、主题切换。\n- 底部/关于：Tauric Research 归属、版本、免责声明。\n- 空状态展示五阶段工作流：Analyst → Research → Trader → Risk → Portfolio。\n\n**New Analysis（向导）**\n\n1. Ticker：输入 + 规范化提示 + 自动识别 stock/crypto。\n2. Analysis Date：日期选择，最大今天。\n3. Output Language：现有 11 种 + 自定义。\n4. Analysts：四选多；crypto 隐藏 Fundamentals；至少一个。\n5. Research Depth：Shallow/Medium/Deep（1/3/5）。\n6. Provider & Models：provider、地区、backend URL、快/深模型、自定义 ID、推理参数；Key 状态只读。\n7. Checkpoint：开关 + 说明。\n8. Portfolio：无 / 空仓 / 粘贴 JSON / 上传 JSON；校验后显示 fingerprint 与摘要。\n9. Review：汇总所有选择；提交。\n\n交互细节：\n\n- env 锁定的字段显示锁图标与“from environment”，不可覆盖。\n- 缺 Key 显示黄色提示，但允许提交（与 CLI 一致）。\n- 上一步/下一步；每步本地 Zod 校验；提交后后端再校验。\n- 记住 UI 偏好到 `localStorage`；**不写** `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json`。\n\n**Live Run**\n\n- 顶部统计条：Agents x/y、LLM calls、Tool calls、Tokens ↑↓、Reports x/y、Elapsed。\n- 左侧 Progress：Ana lyst/Research/Trading/Risk/Portfolio 团队与 agent 状态。\n- 右侧 Messages & Tools：实时 feed；点击消息打开详情抽屉（完整内容、工具参数）。\n- 下方 Current Report：按 section tab；默认跟随最新更新；另有 Full Report 入口。\n- 顶部状态：Starting / Resuming / Running / Cancelling / Completed / Failed / Cancelled。\n- 取消按钮：仅分析运行可用；二次确认。\n- 断线：显示 Reconnecting；自动 snapshot + SSE 重连。\n- REVIEW：完成后显著黄色横幅，说明“不是持仓，需要人工复核”。\n\n**Report**\n\n- I–V 分栏：Analyst Team、Research、Trading、Risk、Portfolio。\n- 每个 section 用 sanitized Markdown 渲染。\n- “Complete Report” 单页视图。\n- 下载：Complete Markdown / Report Archive。\n- 元数据：ticker、date、asset type、analysts、depth、provider、models、language、rating、review、wall times。\n\n**History**\n\n- 表格列：Ticker、Date、Status、Rating、Review、Source（run/saved/backtest）、Updated、Actions。\n- 筛选：ticker、日期范围、source、rating。\n- 空状态与错误状态。\n- 详情页复用 Report 组件；只读。\n- 不提供删除/重命名/清理。\n\n**Backtest**\n\n- 表单：tickers、start、end、every、analysts、asset type、portfolio（粘贴/上传）、run id。\n- 运行中：不确定进度 + 预期 cell 数；无取消按钮，显示“回测会运行至完成”。\n- 结果：Resolved/Pending/Unscored、按评级 n/命中率/均值 alpha、holding window、failures、settlement failures、日志下载。\n- 历史回测列表：run id、时间、tickers、状态。\n\n### 5.3 状态管理\n\n```text\nuseRunStore (Zustand)\n  runId, status, connection, lastSeq\n  agentStatus, stats, sections, messages, toolCalls\n  signal, review, warnings, error\n  actions: reset, applyEvent, applySnapshot, setConnection\n\nuseUiStore (Zustand)\n  language, theme, sidebarOpen, modal\n\nTanStack Query\n  ['config'], ['models', provider, mode], ['announcements']\n  ['history', filters, cursor], ['history', artifactId]\n  ['backtests'], ['backtest', runId]\n```\n\nSSE hook：\n\n```ts\nuseRunStream(runId) -> { connection, lastSeq }\n// 1. GET /api/runs/{id} 获取 snapshot\n// 2. new EventSource(`/api/runs/${id}/events?after_seq=${lastSeq}`)\n// 3. onmessage: parse envelope -> store.applyEvent\n// 4. onerror: store.setConnection('reconnecting')\n// 5. EventSource 自动重连；服务端用 Last-Event-ID 续传\n```\n\n事件合并规则：\n\n- `seq <= lastSeq` 丢弃。\n- `message` 按 message id 去重。\n- `report.section` 覆盖同 section。\n- `stats` 覆盖。\n- `run.completed/failed/cancelled` 设为终态，关闭 SSE。\n- `snapshot` 重置 store 到快照，再继续。\n\n### 5.4 设计系统\n\n- 深色默认（终端/金融仪表盘气质），提供浅色 token。\n- 颜色：中性炭黑/深蓝底；状态色：pending 灰、in_progress 蓝、completed 绿、failed/cancelled 红/橙、REVIEW 琥珀。\n- 数字使用等宽字体；表格右对齐数值。\n- 间距 4px 基准；圆角小；边框清晰；避免大面积渐变/玻璃拟态。\n- 可访问性：Radix 提供键盘/焦点；所有图标按钮有 aria-label；状态变化用 `aria-live=\"polite\"`；对比度满足常用标准。\n- 桌面优先：最小 1024px；1280px+ 为主布局；不做手机专门适配（按已确认范围）。\n\n### 5.5 i18n\n\n- `en.json` / `zh.json`，key 完全一致；测试保证无缺失/多余。\n- **默认英文**（项目文档与课程语境为英文），可切换中文；选择存 `localStorage`。\n- 报告正文不翻译；报告语言仍由“Output Language”决定。\n- 日期/数字格式按 UI 语言本地化；ticker/模型 ID 不翻译。\n\n---\n\n## 6. 关键时序\n\n### 6.1 发起分析\n\n```text\nBrowser                     FastAPI                     Core/worker\n  | POST /api/runs             |                             |\n  |--------------------------->| validate request            |\n  |                            | acquire single-run lock     |\n  | 201 {run_id, status}       | create RunRecord            |\n  |<---------------------------| start worker task --------->|\n  | GET /events?after_seq=0    |                             |\n  |--------------------------->| SSE subscribe               |\n  | event: run.preparing       |<---- emit ------------------|\n  | event: run.started         |                             |\n  | event: agent.status ...    |                             |\n  | event: message ...         |                             |\n  | event: report.section ...  |                             |\n  | event: stats ...           |                             |\n  | event: run.completed       |                             |\n  |<---------------------------|                             |\n```\n\n### 6.2 取消\n\n```text\nBrowser --POST /runs/{id}/cancel--> Coordinator\n                                      set cancel_event\n                                      wait worker (bounded)\n                                      no record_decision\n                                      no clear_checkpoint\n                                      end_checkpoint()\n                                      state=cancelled\nBrowser <-- event: run.cancelled --- EventBuffer\n```\n\n### 6.3 断线重连\n\n```text\nBrowser reload\n  -> GET /api/runs/{id}  (snapshot, last_seq)\n  -> EventSource /events?after_seq=last_seq\n  -> server replays buffered events or sends snapshot if behind\n  -> live continues\n```\n\n### 6.4 历史读取\n\n```text\nBrowser -> GET /api/history\n        -> ArtifactIndex.scan(roots, cache 5s)\n        -> hash ids, metadata, rating\n        -> page\nBrowser -> GET /api/history/{id}\n        -> resolve hash -> validated relative path\n        -> read sections / complete report\nBrowser -> GET /api/history/{id}/download?kind=archive\n        -> in-memory zip -> attachment\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. 安全设计\n\n| 威胁 | 控制 |\n|---|---|\n| 非本机访问 | 仅绑定 `127.0.0.1`；启动时拒绝其他 host |\n| DNS rebinding / 恶意网页 | 校验 `Host` 仅允许 `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`；校验 `Origin`；无 CORS；CSRF token |\n| CSRF | `GET /api/session` 返回进程级 token；POST/DELETE 必须带 `X-CSRF-Token`；SameSite/同源 |\n| 密钥泄漏 | 只读服务器 env；序列化 allowlist；错误/日志/事件/下载全面脱敏 |\n| 路径穿越 | 浏览器只拿哈希 artifact id；服务端解析后必须落在允许根目录；`safe_ticker_component` |\n| XSS | `rehype-sanitize` 白名单；禁用原始 HTML；链接仅 `http/https`；外链 `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`；默认阻止外部图片 |\n| 恶意 Markdown | 限制 section 大小；不执行内联 HTML/JS；CSP |\n| 请求体过大 | 1 MB 总上限；portfolio 256 KB |\n| 事件缓冲内存膨胀 | 有界 buffer + 有界订阅队列 + snapshot 退化 |\n| 错误信息泄漏 | 统一错误分类；correlation id；不返回堆栈/路径/凭据 |\n| 日志泄漏 | 不记录 key、cookie、Authorization、完整 prompt；只记录 run/ticker/date/耗时/分类 |\n| 未授权执行 | 无交易/下单端点；评级只展示 |\n| 依赖供应链 | 新增依赖逐项审批、锁定、审计；前端 lockfile |\n\nCSP 建议：\n\n```text\ndefault-src 'self';\nscript-src 'self';\nstyle-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';\nimg-src 'self' data:;\nfont-src 'self';\nconnect-src 'self';\nframe-ancestors 'none';\nbase-uri 'none';\nform-action 'self';\n```\n\n其他响应头：`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`、`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`、`Permissions-Policy` 最小化。\n\n---\n\n## 8. 与现有系统的契约\n\n### 8.1 复用而非重写\n\n| 能力 | 复用的现有实现 |\n|---|---|\n| 图编排/流式执行 | `TradingAgentsGraph`、`create_run_state`、`begin_checkpoint`、`graph.stream` |\n| 评级 | `process_signal`、`extract_rating`、`is_review` |\n| 报告 | `write_report_tree` |\n| 组合 | `PortfolioContext`、`load_portfolio` 的校验语义 |\n| 路径 | `safe_ticker_component` |\n| 回测 | `iter_grid`、`run_backtest`、`summarize` |\n| 记忆 | `TradingMemoryLog`（只读历史；运行通过 graph 写入） |\n| Checkpoint | `has_checkpoint`、`clear_all_checkpoints` |\n| 参数/模型 | `DEFAULT_CONFIG`、`_ENV_OVERRIDES`、`cli.utils` 的 provider/model 助手 |\n| 统计 | `StatsCallbackHandler` |\n| 公告 | `fetch_announcements` |\n\n### 8.2 TUI 内容覆盖矩阵\n\n| TUI 内容 | Web 位置 | 说明 |\n|---|---|---|\n| ASCII 欢迎/五阶段说明 | App Shell/空状态 | 保留品牌与工作流语义，不复刻 ASCII |\n| 公告面板 | 顶部公告 + 阻塞模态 | 完全对齐 |\n| 8 步参数选择 | Wizard | 完全对齐；Step 6 的 Key 输入改为只读状态 |\n| Analyst/深度/Provider/模型/推理参数 | Wizard | 完全对齐；含 env 锁提示 |\n| 上次偏好 | Wizard 预填 | 只读 `cli_prefs.json` |\n| 实时 Progress 表 | Live Run 左栏 | pending/in_progress/completed |\n| Messages & Tools | Live Run 右栏 + 详情抽屉 | 摘要 + 完整内容 |\n| Current Report | Live Run 下方 tabs | 比 TUI 多 section 切换 |\n| Footer 统计 | Live Run 顶部统计条 | 6 类统计 |\n| Checkpoint 恢复/新建提示 | 运行状态横幅 | `run.resumed` / `run.started` |\n| 完成提示/REVIEW/wall time | 完成横幅 | 完全对齐 |\n| Save report 提示 | 自动保存 + 下载 | 路径提示改为下载（已确认偏离） |\n| Display full report | Report 页面 | I–V + Complete |\n| Backtest 文本摘要 | Backtest 页面 | 表格化，字段对齐 |\n| 错误提示 | inline/toast | 安全文本 |\n| API Key 粘贴 | Key 状态只读 | 已确认偏离 |\n| Windows 无控制台提示 | 不适用 | Web 无终端依赖 |\n\n### 8.3 确定性边界\n\n- 不把 `REVIEW` 变成 `Hold` 或交易。\n- 不把“未提供组合”当成空仓。\n- 不绕过分析日期/时点过滤。\n- 回测不读写 live 决策日志。\n- 用户输入不能成为任意文件访问权限。\n- 模型/公告/报告文本不成为权限或执行指令。\n\n---\n\n## 9. 测试与 CI\n\n### `tradingagents_web/static/index.html`。\n- 干净环境安装后：`tradingagents-web --help`、启动、`GET /api/health`。\n- 全部现有 `test/offline` 回归。\n\n### 9.4 CI 新增 job\n\n```text\nweb-backend      : pip install -e '.[dev,web]' && pytest test/offline/test_web_*.py\nweb-frontend     : npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test && npm run build\nweb-e2e          : playwright install --with-deps && npm run e2e\nweb-packaging    : build wheel; clean install; health check\nblocking-gate    : 纳入以上 job\n```\n\n---\n\n## 10. 实施计划\n\n| 阶段 | 内容 | 退出标准 | 估算 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **0. 批准与骨架** | It does not approve a web framework, a service implementation, a storage engine, an event transport, a frontend build system, or final module names. No product implementation may begin until the approval gates in Section 15 are satisfied.\n4: \n5: Owner: human project owner. Prepared by the Docs role on 2026-11-05.\n6: \n7: ## 1. Authority and scope\n8: \n9: This blueprint is subordinate to `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `.agent/rules.md`, `.opencode/rules.md`, and `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md`. It extends the TradingAgents v0.5.0 baseline at commit `2d17df8da1536c121e4d7395ac5a5dcec9e96d6f` on branch `feature/webui`. It does not replace the baseline, the CLI, the Python API, or any existing business rule.\n10: \n11: The WebUI is a **local, single-user, single-active-run presentation layer**. Its job is to display and orchestrate capabilities that already exist. It must not add analysis capability, data sources, model providers, trading behaviour, or agent logic.\n12: \n13: <a id=\"goals\"></a>\n14: ## 2. Goals\n15: \n16: 1. Expose the complete CLI analysis workflow through a browser: the eight selection steps, live run view, completion summary, and full I–V report.\n17: 2. Preserve every deterministic boundary already enforced by the core and CLI: ticker and path validation, analysis-date limits, rating integrity, portfolio semantics, point-in-time data access, memory isolation, and checkpoint behaviour.\n18: 3. Keep the core and CLI unchanged. The WebUI may call existing public Python interfaces, read existing artifacts, and write only the artifact types the CLI already writes.\n19: 4. Provide read-only history over existing artifacts without introducing a new database or changing retention.\n20: 5. Expose the existing backtest capability with the same parameters and result semantics as the CLI.\n21: 6. Keep secrets server-side. The browser never receives provider keys or server filesystem paths.\n22: 7. Support Chinese/English UI switching, independent of the report output language.\n23: \n24: <a id=\"non-goals\"></a>\n25: ## 3. Non-goals\n26: \n27: The following are explicitly out of scope for this iteration:\n28: \n29: - Trading execution, order placement, position changes, or brokerage integration.\n30: - New data vendors, model providers, model catalogues, prompts, agents, or rating rules.\n31: - Multi-user accounts, tenants, billing, quotas, or authentication.\n32: - New databases, message queues, caches, or cross-process run persistence.\n33: - Cloud deployment, container orchestration, domain/TLS provisioning, or CI/CD release automation.\n34: - PDF or Word export; native mobile applications.\n35: - Multi-ticker batch analysis outside the existing backtest command.\n36: - Cross-run comparison, scoring dashboards, or backtest charts beyond the confirmed result view.\n37: - Any change to CLI arguments, defaults, output, exit codes, or core behaviour.\n38: \n39: ## 4. Baseline code facts that constrain the design\n40: \n41: These facts are derived from the current source and must be treated as constraints, not preferences.\n42: \n43: | Fact | Evidence | Consequence |\n44: | --- | --- | --- |\n45: | Core configuration is a module-level singleton | `src/tradingagents/dataflows/config.py` (`_config`, `set_config`) | Two graphs with different configs must not run concurrently in one process. |\n46: | The CLI message buffer is a module-level singleton | `src/cli/main.py` (`message_buffer = MessageBuffer()`) | The web layer must own its own run state and must not reuse this object. |\n47: | The CLI streams the graph directly | `src/cli/main.py` (`run_analysis`, `graph.graph.stream`) | The CLI path is the behavioural reference for live updates; it is not identical to `propagate()`. |\n48: | `propagate()` writes a state log | `src/tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` (`_log_state`) | API-style runs may have `full_states_log_*.json`; CLI-style runs do not. |\n49: | Decision memory is read-modify-write with atomic replacement | `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py` | Concurrent writers are not proven safe; the single-run rule protects the log. |\n50: | Checkpoints are per-ticker SQLite databases | `src/tradingagents/graph/checkpointer.py` | A run can resume only when checkpointing was enabled and the process that owns it is available. |\n51: | Report serialization is shared | `src/tradingagents/reporting.py` (`write_report_tree`) | The web layer must call this writer rather than reimplement section layout. |\n52: | Path safety is deterministic | `src/tradingagents/dataflows/utils.py` (`safe_ticker_component`) | The web layer must reuse it for every ticker/run-id path component. |\n53: | Rating extraction is deterministic | `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/rating.py` | The web layer must not infer or \"repair\" a rating. |\n54: | Portfolio states are distinct | `src/tradingagents/portfolio.py` | No portfolio, an empty book, and a populated book are three different inputs. |\n55: \n56: ## 5. System context\n57: \n58: ```\n59: Browser\n60:   |  same-origin HTTP + server-to-client event stream\n61:   v\n62: Web presentation layer (new, outside src/tradingagents and src/cli)\n63:   |-- Configuration projection (read-only)\n64:   |-- Run coordinator (single active run)\n65:   |-- Event projection\n66:   |-- Artifact read model\n67:   |-- Backtest surface\n68:   v\n69: Existing public Python interfaces and on-disk artifacts\n70:   |-- TradingAgentsGraph (public methods)\n71:   |-- run_backtest / summarize\n72:   |-- write_report_tree\n73:   |-- TradingMemoryLog (read/write through existing graph methods only)\n74:   |-- results_dir, checkpoint directory, CLI preferences\n75: ```\n76: \n77: The browser never imports Python, never receives a server path, and never receives a secret. The core never imports the web layer.\n78: \n79: ## 6. Logical components\n80: \n81: <a id=\"w1-entry-and-parameter-surface\"></a>\n82: ### 6.1 W1 — Entry and parameter surface\n83: \n84: Responsibility: render the eight selection steps, validate inputs, and submit a run request.\n85: \n86: Inputs: ticker, analysis date, output language, analyst selection, research depth, provider and endpoint, quick/deep model, provider thinking parameters, checkpoint flag, portfolio JSON, and the announcement acknowledgement.\n87: \n88: Outputs: a validated run request or a field-level error.\n89: \n90: Boundaries:\n91: - Validation mirrors the CLI and core rules; it does not replace them. The core remains authoritative.\n92: - The provider/API-key step is deliberately different from the CLI: the web surface displays \"configured / not configured\" from the server environment and never accepts a key.\n93: - Environment-locked values are shown as locked with their source, matching the CLI's \"from environment\" messages.\n94: - Crypto detection filters out the fundamentals analyst, matching `filter_analysts_for_asset_type`.\n95: \n96: Failure modes: invalid ticker, future date, no analyst, unknown provider/model, invalid portfolio, missing server key (allowed to start, fails at the first provider call, matching the CLI).\n97: \n98: <a id=\"w2-run-coordinator\"></a>\n99: ### 6.2 W2 — Run coordinator\n100: \n101: Responsibility: own the lifecycle of the single active analysis run.\n102: \n103: Inputs: a validated run request.\n104: Outputs: a run record, an event sequence, and final artifacts.\n105: \n106: Ownership:\n107: - Creates one fresh `TradingAgentsGraph` per run.\n108: - Calls the existing state construction path (`create_run_state`), checkpoint methods (`begin_checkpoint`, `checkpoint_input`, `end_checkpoint`, `clear_checkpoint_on_success`), the graph stream, `record_decision`, `process_signal`, and `write_report_tree`.\n109: - Owns cancellation, completion, failure, and reattachment.\n110: - Holds run state in process memory only.\n111: \n112: Rules:\n113: - At most one run may be active. A second submission is rejected with a conflict error.\n114: - A browser disconnect does not cancel the run. The coordinator continues consuming the stream.\n115: - Cancellation follows CLI `Ctrl-C` semantics: stop consuming, do not call `record_decision`, do not clear the checkpoint, end the checkpoint scope, and keep artifacts already written.\n116: - The coordinator never fabricates a rating. It reads the deterministic signal from the existing processor and surfaces `REVIEW` as a review state.\n117: - The coordinator must not write `full_states_log_*.json` unless it deliberately uses the `propagate()` path; the chosen path and its artifact consequences must be explicit in the implementation plan.\n118: \n119: <a id=\"w3-configuration-projection\"></a>\n120: ### 6.3 W3 — Configuration projection\n121: \n122: Responsibility: present the effective configuration and choices without becoming a second source of truth.\n123: \n124: Rules:\n125: - Reads `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, `TRADINGAGENTS_*` environment overrides, the provider table, the model catalogue, and `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json`.\n126: - Never writes the core configuration singleton except indirectly through constructing `TradingAgentsGraph`, which the existing code already does.\n127: - Environment precedence is displayed, not re-implemented differently.\n128: - The CLI preferences file is read-only for the web layer; whether web runs update it is a pending decision.\n129: \n130: <a id=\"w4-event-projection\"></a>\n131: ### 6.4 W4 — Event projection\n132: \n133: Responsibility: translate graph stream chunks into a stable server-to-client event sequence.\n134: \n135: Event envelope fields (minimum): `run_id`, `seq`, `timestamp`, `type`, `payload`.\n136: \n137: Required event types:\n138: \n139: | Type | Payload (minimum) |\n140: | --- | --- |\n141: | `run.started` | ticker, trade_date, asset_type, analysts, depth, provider, models, checkpoint flag |\n142: | `run.resumed` | checkpoint step or \"fresh\" |\n143: | `agent.status` | agent, status in {pending, in_progress, completed} |\n144: | `message` | timestamp, message type, content |\n145: | `tool_call` | timestamp, tool name, arguments |\n146: | `report.section` | section key, title, content |\n147: | `stats` | agents completed/total, llm calls, tool calls, tokens in/out, reports completed/total, elapsed |\n148: | `run.completed` | final signal, review flag, wall-time summary, artifact references |\n149: | `run.failed` | error category, safe message |\n150: | `run.cancelled` | cancellation point |\n151: | `announcement` | sanitized announcement payload |\n152: \n153: Rules:\n154: - Events are ordered by `seq`; reattachment replays from the last acknowledged sequence.\n155: - The stream is one-way (server to client). Client actions use separate request endpoints.\n156: - Event payloads must not contain secrets, absolute server paths, stack traces, or raw credentials.\n157: - The event buffer is bounded; if a client falls too far behind, the server sends a snapshot event rather than unbounded memory growth.\n158: - The transport is not selected by this blueprint. The contract above is transport-neutral.\n159: \n160: <a id=\"w5-artifact-read-model\"></a>\n161: ### 6.5 W5 — Artifact read model\n162: \n163: Responsibility: read existing artifacts for completion views and history.\n164: \n165: Sources:\n166: - Run directory: `<results_dir>/<ticker>/<date>/` with `message_tool.log` and `reports/*.md`.\n167: - API-style state log: `<results_dir>/<ticker>/TradingAgentsStrategy_logs/full_states_log_<date>.json` when present.\n168: - Saved report tree: `<results_dir>/reports/<ticker>_<timestamp>/` with `1_analysts` … `5_portfolio` and `complete_report.md`.\n169: - Backtest run: `<results_dir>/backtest/<run_id>/` and its `trading_memory.md`.\n170: - Decision memory: `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`, read-only.\n171: \n172: Rules:\n173: - Read-only. No deletion, rotation, migration, or index database.\n174: - The model exposes stable artifact identifiers; it never returns absolute paths to the browser.\n175: - Every identifier resolves through a validated allowlist of roots and path components.\n176: - Missing optional artifacts are reported as absent, not synthesized.\n177: - History must work for CLI-style runs that lack `full_states_log_*.json`.\n178: \n179: <a id=\"w6-backtest-surface\"></a>\n180: ### 6.6 W6 — Backtest surface\n181: \n182: Responsibility: launch and display existing backtests.\n183: \n184: Rules:\n185: - Parameters mirror the CLI: tickers, start, end, every, analysts, asset type, portfolio, run id.\n186: - The summary mirrors `summarize(...)`: resolved, pending, unscored, per-rating count/hit rate/mean alpha, holding window, failures, settlement failures, and log path.\n187: - Backtest and live analysis remain isolated. The web layer must not point a backtest at the live memory log.\n188: - A backtest is a run for the single-active-run rule.\n189: - Whether a backtest can be cancelled with the same semantics as an analysis is a pending decision; if implemented, `run_id` resume must remain available.\n190: \n191: <a id=\"w7-security-boundary\"></a>\n192: ### 6.7 W7 — Security boundary\n193: \n194: Responsibilities and rules:\n195: \n196: 1. **Network**: bind to `127.0.0.1` only. Reject non-loopback `Host` headers. No authentication is required by the confirmed scope, so the loopback and same-origin checks are mandatory compensating controls.\n197: 2. **Secrets**: provider keys come only from the server environment. The browser receives a boolean/status, never a value. Errors and events are redacted.\n198: 3. **Paths**: the browser receives artifact identifiers, not filesystem paths. Server-side resolution uses `safe_ticker_component` and a root allowlist.\n199: 4. **Untrusted content**: model output, tool output, announcements, and artifact text are data. Render as escaped text or a sanitized Markdown subset. No raw HTML, no script execution, no `javascript:` or `data:` links, no server-side template evaluation of model text.\n200: 5. **Requests**: state-changing requests require same-origin checks; no wildcard CORS. Request size and event buffer size are bounded.\n201: 6. **Files**: no generic file browser, upload-to-server-path, or download-by-path endpoint. Uploads are parsed as portfolio JSON and discarded after validation.\n202: 7. **Logging**: logs must not contain keys, cookies, authorization headers, server absolute paths, or full model prompts controlled by third parties.\n203: \n204: <a id=\"w8-frontend\"></a>\n205: ### 6.8 W8 — Frontend\n206: \n207: Responsibility: present the wizard, live view, report, history, backtest, announcements, errors, and language switch.\n208: \n209: Rules:\n210: - UI state is derived from server events and snapshots; the frontend does not compute ratings or business decisions.\n211: - The live view mirrors the TUI's information set: progress table, messages and tools, current report, footer statistics.\n212: - The report view mirrors sections I–V and the complete report.\n213: - History and backtest views are read-only.\n214: - Chinese/English strings are UI-only; report content follows the existing output-language setting.\n215: - The frontend must remain usable when the event stream reconnects; it requests a snapshot after reconnect.\n216: \n217: <a id=\"proposed-ownership-paths\"></a>\n218: ## 7. Proposed ownership paths (pending approval)\n219: \n220: The following paths are proposals for the implementation plan. They are not approved module names.\n221: \n222: | Element | Proposed path | Boundary |\n223: | --- | --- | --- |\n224: | Web package (presentation only) | `src/tradingagents_web/` | Must never be imported by `src/tradingagents/` or `src/cli/`. |\n225: | Run coordinator and lifecycle | `src/tradingagents_web/run/` | Owns in-process run state. |\n226: | HTTP surface and validation | `src/tradingagents_web/http/` | Owns request parsing and error mapping. |\n227: | Event projection | `src/tradingagents_web/events/` | Owns the event envelope and buffer. |\n228: | Artifact read model | `src/tradingagents_web/artifacts/` | Read-only filesystem access through a root allowlist. |\n229: | Backtest surface | `src/tradingagents_web/backtest/` | Wraps `run_backtest` and `summarize`. |\n230: | Frontend assets | `src/tradingagents_web/static/` and `src/tradingagents_web/templates/` | No server Python or secrets. |\n231: | Offline contract tests | `test/offline/test_web_*.py` | Deterministic, no network. |\n232: | Live tests | `test/live/test_web_live.py` | Requires external-service and cost authorization. |\n233: \n234: Why `src/tradingagents_web/`: the existing setuptools package discovery includes `tradingagents*` and `cli*`; a sibling `tradingagents_web` package is includable without changing `pyproject.toml`. The structural check forbids `src/tradingagents/` from importing presentation frameworks; keeping the web package outside that tree preserves the rule. If the implementation instead chooses a path that requires a packaging change, that change needs explicit approval.\n235: \n236: ## 8. Interface contracts\n237: \n238: <a id=\"run-request\"></a>\n239: ### 8.1 Run request\n240: \n241: Required fields: confirmed run parameters plus a client request id for idempotency. Optional: portfolio object, checkpoint flag.\n242: \n243: Validation:\n244: - Ticker: same charset/length rules as the CLI, then canonicalization.\n245: - Date: `YYYY-MM-DD`, not in the future.\n246: - Analysts: at least one known key; crypto excludes fundamentals.\n247: - Depth: one of 1, 3, 5.\n248: - Provider/model: must resolve through the existing provider/catalogue code.\n249: - Portfolio: validated by `PortfolioContext`; three states preserved.\n250: - No client-supplied filesystem path is accepted.\n251: \n252: Errors: field-level validation errors before a run starts; a conflict error when a run is already active.\n253: \n254: <a id=\"run-state\"></a>\n255: ### 8.2 Run state\n256: \n257: States: `idle`, `starting`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.\n258: \n259: Only one run may be in `starting` or `running`.\n260: \n261: A run record contains: `run_id`, request fields, `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_seq`, `signal`, `review`, `artifact_ids`, and a safe error category.\n262: \n263: <a id=\"cancellation\"></a>\n264: ### 8.3 Cancellation\n265: \n266: 1. Stop consuming the graph stream.\n267: 2. End the checkpoint scope in a `finally` block.\n268: 3. Do not call `record_decision`.\n269: 4. Do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`.\n270: 5. Keep artifacts already written.\n271: 6. Mark the run `cancelled` and publish `run.cancelled`.\n272: \n273: If checkpointing was disabled, the run cannot be resumed. If it was enabled, the existing checkpoint remains available to the existing resume path.\n274: \n275: <a id=\"reattachment\"></a>\n276: ### 8.4 Reattachment\n277: \n278: - The run continues while the server process lives.\n279: - A reconnecting client presents the run id and last seen sequence.\n280: - The server replays buffered events from that sequence or sends a snapshot.\n281: - After a server process restart, the run is gone; on-disk artifacts and checkpoints may remain for the existing CLI/API paths. Cross-process run recovery is out of scope.\n282: \n283: <a id=\"report-artifact-contract\"></a>\n284: ### 8.5 Report and artifact contract\n285: \n286: - The web layer calls `write_report_tree` for the report tree; it does not reimplement section layout.\n287: - The run directory layout follows the CLI path.\n288: - Download is generated from an allowlisted artifact, not from a client-supplied path.\n289: - The complete report and its existing report artifacts are the confirmed download targets; the exact packaging (single file, directory archive, or both) remains an open decision.\n290: \n291: <a id=\"history-contract\"></a>\n292: ### 8.6 History contract\n293: \n294: - History is a read-only projection over the sources in Section 6.5.\n295: - A history item is identified by a stable, validated artifact id.\n296: - Missing fields are shown as absent.\n297: - No delete, rename, move, retention change, or index write is permitted.\n298: \n299: <a id=\"error-taxonomy\"></a>\n300: ### 8.7 Error taxonomy\n301: \n302: | Category | Meaning | Client behaviour |\n303: | --- | --- | --- |\n304: | `validation` | A request field is invalid | Show field errors; do not start |\n305: | `conflict` | A run is already active | Explain and offer to view the active run |\n306: | `not_found` | Run or artifact id does not resolve | Show a safe not-found message |\n307: | `config` | Provider/model/key configuration is unusable | Show the safe configuration error |\n308: | `upstream` | Data vendor or model provider failed | Show a safe retryable message; preserve the run record |\n309: | `storage` | Artifact write/read failed | Show a safe storage message; do not expose paths |\n310: | `cancelled` | The user cancelled | Show the cancellation state |\n311: | `internal` | Unexpected failure | Show a generic message; log a redacted diagnostic |\n312: \n313: <a id=\"state-ownership-and-concurrency\"></a>\n314: ## 9. State ownership and concurrency\n315: \n316: - The run coordinator owns the active run and the graph instance.\n317: - The core owns checkpoints and the decision log; the web layer calls the existing methods.\n318: - The artifact read model owns no writes.\n319: - The frontend owns only presentation state.\n320: - There is one process and one active run. This is the synchronization mechanism for the core's global configuration and the decision log.\n321: - If future work introduces concurrent runs, it must first define configuration isolation and memory write ownership; this blueprint does not authorize that change.\n322: \n323: <a id=\"deterministic-boundaries-preserved\"></a>\n324: ## 10. Deterministic boundaries preserved\n325: \n326: The web layer must call, not reimplement:\n327: \n328: - `_validate_trade_date`/date validation rules.\n329: - `safe_ticker_component` for every path component derived from user input.\n330: - `PortfolioContext` validation and fingerprinting.\n331: - `extract_rating`/`parse_rating` and the `REVIEW` sentinel.\n332: - `write_report_tree` for report layout.\n333: - `TradingMemoryLog` through the graph's existing methods.\n334: - `run_backtest` and `summarize` for backtest semantics.\n335: \n336: The web layer must never:\n337: \n338: - Convert `REVIEW` to `Hold` or to a trade.\n339: - Treat an absent portfolio as a flat book.\n340: - Read the live memory log from a backtest.\n341: - Bypass point-in-time data filters.\n342: - Accept a ticker, run id, or path that the core would reject.\n343: \n344: ## 11. Configuration and deployment\n345: \n346: - Default bind: `127.0.0.1`.\n347: - No authentication, by confirmed scope.\n348: - One process. No worker pool, no external broker.\n349: - Run state in memory. Restart loses active runs.\n350: - Existing `results_dir`, `data_cache_dir`, and `memory_log_path` defaults apply.\n351: - The web layer must not write `.env` or provider keys.\n352: - No container, cloud, domain, TLS, or orchestration work in this iteration.\n353: \n354: ## 12. Dependency and packaging policy\n355: \n356: - No new runtime dependency is approved by this blueprint.\n357: - A web framework, ASGI/WSGI server, frontend build tool, or event-transport library requires an explicit dependency and architecture decision before use.\n358: - The implementation plan must state the exact dependency additions, versions ranges, rationale, license/security review, and fallback.\n359: - The core must not depend on the web layer or its framework.\n360: - If the selected framework cannot be packaged without changing `pyproject.toml`, that packaging change needs governance approval.\n361: \n362: ## 13. Browser support matrix (confirmed: desktop modern browsers; exact versions to be recorded in tests).\n376: \n377: ## 14. Use temporary directories and fakes.\n388: \n389: ## 15. Approval gates\n390: \n391: Before product implementation:\n392: \n393: 1.                 "text": "Read file [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents/docs/architecture/memory-design.md, lines 1-96\n1: # TradingAgents WebUI Memory and State Design\n2: \n3: Status: **Draft for human review.** This document describes the existing memory mechanisms the WebUI must reuse and the new in-memory run state it must own. It does not authorize a new persistence system.\n4: \n5: ## 1. Existing decision memory\n6: \n7: The baseline decision log is implemented by `TradingMemoryLog` in `src/tradingagents/agents/utils/memory.py`.\n8: \n9: - Storage: an append-only Markdown file, default `~/.tradingagents/memory/trading_memory.md`, overridable with `TRADINGAGENTS_MEMORY_LOG_PATH`.\n10: - Write path: `store_decision()` appends a pending entry with a tag containing trade date, ticker, rating, and `pending`.\n11: - Settlement: `update_with_outcome()` or `batch_update_with_outcomes()` replaces the pending tag with realized raw return, alpha, holding window, and an optional `resolved:<date>` field, then appends a reflection.\n12: - Atomicity: the file is written to a temporary path and replaced with `os.replace()`. This prevents torn files, not lost updates from concurrent read-modify-write.\n13: - Point-in-time: `get_past_context(..., as_of=...)` includes only entries whose resolution date is on or before the analysis date. Live runs pass `None` and keep the legacy behavior.\n14: - Rotation: `memory_log_max_entries` optionally prunes the oldest resolved entries; pending entries are never pruned.\n15: \n16: ## 2. Existing checkpoint state\n17: \n18: - Per-ticker SQLite databases under `<data_cache_dir>/checkpoints/<TICKER>.db`.\n19: - `thread_id(ticker, date, signature)` derives a deterministic id; the signature includes analyst selection, debate/risk rounds, asset type, and portfolio fingerprint.\n20: - Successful completion clears the run's checkpoint. Cancellation and failure leave it in place.\n21: - `clear_all_checkpoints()` removes the databases and their `-wal`/`-shm` companions.\n22: \n23: ## 3. Existing CLI preferences\n24: \n25: - `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json` stores stable choices from the last CLI run.\n26: - It is convenience state, not authority. Unreadable content means no defaults.\n27: - The web layer may read it for prefill. Whether web runs write it is an open decision (blueprint Section 13).\n28: \n29: ## 4. New web run state\n30: \n31: The web layer owns one in-memory record for the single active run and a bounded event history.\n32: \n33: Required fields:\n34: \n35: - `run_id`: server-generated, safe path component.\n36: - Request: ticker, trade date, asset type, analysts, depth, provider, models, output language, checkpoint flag, portfolio fingerprint.\n37: - Lifecycle: `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_seq`.\n38: - Result: final signal, review flag, safe error category, artifact identifiers.\n39: - Events: bounded sequence with a snapshot fallback.\n40: \n41: Ownership:\n42: \n43: - The run coordinator is the only writer of the active run record.\n44: - The event projection is the only writer of the event sequence.\n45: - The artifact read model never writes.\n46: - The frontend holds only presentation state.\n47: \n48: ## 5. Concurrency and write ownership\n49: \n50: The approved scope is one active run per process. This is the synchronization mechanism for:\n51: \n52: - the process-global configuration in `src/tradingagents/dataflows/config.py`;\n53: - the read-modify-write decision log;\n54: - checkpoint databases and the run-level event buffer.\n55: \n56: The web layer must not introduce a second writer to the decision log. It writes through the existing graph methods (`record_decision`, `_resolve_pending_entries`) and never appends directly.\n57: \n58: Concurrent runs are out of scope. Introducing them would require, at minimum:\n59: \n60: 1. per-run configuration isolation instead of the global singleton;\n61: 2. a defined decision-log write owner or a serialized writer;\n62: 3. per-run checkpoint and artifact namespaces that cannot collide;\n63: 4. a concurrency test that fails on lost updates.\n64: \n65: ## 6. Cancellation and failure\n66: \n67: Cancellation is not a memory operation:\n68: \n69: - No decision entry is written.\n70: - No checkpoint is cleared.\n71: - Partial report files and the message log remain.\n72: - The run record is marked `cancelled`.\n73: \n74: Failure follows the same rule: no synthetic decision, no checkpoint clear, safe error category, partial artifacts preserved. A retry is a new run with a new request.\n75: \n76: ## 7. Point-in-time integrity\n77: \n78: The web layer must not bypass the baseline's date and point-in-time rules:\n79: \n80: - The analysis date validation remains in the core.\n81: - The `as_of` filter for past lessons remains in the graph's run-state construction.\n82: - Backtests keep their own log and their own date grid.\n83: - History reads stored artifacts; it does not reconstruct an outcome that was not recorded.\n84: \n85: ## 8. Retention and deletion\n86: \n87: - Decision memory retention remains the existing configuration; the web layer does not expose deletion or rotation controls.\n88: - Checkpoint clearing is the only destructive control exposed, matching the CLI flag, with confirmation and a single-run guard.\n89: - History is read-only; it does not delete or rewrite run artifacts.\n90: - No new database, cache, or index is introduced.\n91: \n92: ## 9. Recovery boundaries\n93: \n94: - A browser disconnect does not affect memory or checkpoints.\n95: - A server restart loses the in-memory run record and event buffer. The decision log and checkpoints on disk remain.\n96: - The existing CLI/API can resume a checkpointed run; the web layer does not claim cross-process recovery."

They do not approve an implementation. Every policy names an enforcement point and a fallback action.\n4: \n5: ## WEB-POLICY-001 — Loopback-only listener\n6: \n7: Trigger: server start.\n8: Rule: bind to `127.0.0.1` only. Reject non-loopback `Host` headers. Do not enable wildcard CORS.\n9: Enforcement: startup configuration and request middleware.\n10: Fallback: refuse to start on a non-loopback address.\n11: \n12: ## WEB-POLICY-002 — Single active run\n13: \n14: Trigger: a new analysis or backtest request.\n15: Rule: if a run is `starting` or `running`, reject the request with a conflict error that identifies the active run. Do not queue silently.\n16: Enforcement: run coordinator admission check.\n17: Fallback: return the active run id so the client can reattach.\n18: \n19: ## WEB-POLICY-003 — Process-lifetime run state\n20: \n21: Trigger: browser disconnect, refresh, or network loss.\n22: Rule: continue the run; allow reattachment from the last acknowledged event sequence within the server process lifetime. A process restart loses the active run.\n23: Enforcement: run coordinator and event buffer.\n24: Fallback: show \"run no longer available\"; on-disk artifacts and checkpoints remain for CLI/API paths.\n25: \n26: ## WEB-POLICY-004 — Cancellation\n27: \n28: Trigger: an authenticated-by-origin cancel request for the active run.\n29: Rule: stop consuming the stream; do not call `record_decision`; do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`; end the checkpoint scope; keep artifacts already written; mark the run `cancelled`.\n30: Enforcement: run coordinator cancellation path.\n31: Fallback: if the stream cannot stop cleanly, mark the run failed and preserve artifacts; never write a synthetic decision.\n32: \n33: ## WEB-POLICY-005 — Checkpoint controls\n34: \n35: Trigger: a checkpoint toggle or clear-all request.\n36: Rule: the toggle affects the next run only. Clear-all requires explicit confirmation and is disabled while a run is active. Clear-all deletes all checkpoint databases, matching the CLI flag.\n37: Enforcement: request validation and run coordinator.\n38: Fallback: reject a clear during a run; report the number of cleared databases.\n39: \n40: ## WEB-POLICY-006 — Server-only provider keys\n41: \n42: Trigger: configuration display or a run start.\n43: Rule: read keys only from the server environment. Display configured/not-configured status. Never accept, persist, return, log, or export a key. A missing key does not block the run; the first provider call fails safely.\n44: Enforcement: configuration projection and serializers.\n45: Fallback: show a safe configuration error and keep the run record.\n46: \n47: ## WEB-POLICY-007 — Deterministic identifiers\n48: \n49: Trigger: any ticker, run id, artifact id, or path component from a client.\n50: Rule: validate with the existing deterministic rules before filesystem use. Reject absolute paths, `..`, backslashes, and values outside the allowlist.\n51: Enforcement: request validation and artifact resolver.\n52: Fallback: reject the request; never widen the path.\n53: \n54: ## WEB-POLICY-008 — Artifact identifiers, not paths\n55: \n56: Trigger: a response that references an artifact.\n57: Rule: return a stable identifier, not an absolute or repository-relative path. Resolve downloads server-side.\n58: Enforcement: artifact read model and serializers.\n59: Fallback: omit the artifact and show a safe not-found message.\n60: \n61: ## WEB-POLICY-009 — Read-only history\n62: \n63: Trigger: a history or backtest-history request.\n64: Rule: read only; no delete, rename, move, rotation, migration, or index write.\n65: Enforcement: artifact read model exposes reads only.\n66: Fallback: reject any mutating request.\n67: \n68: ## WEB-POLICY-010 — Backtest isolation\n69: \n70: Trigger: a backtest request.\n71: Rule: use the backtest's own run directory and memory log; never read or write the live decision log. A backtest is a run for the single-active-run rule.\n72: Enforcement: backtest surface and run coordinator.\n73: Fallback: abort the backtest and report the isolation failure.\n74: \n75: ## WEB-POLICY-011 — Announcement handling\n76: \n77: Trigger: page load or announcement refresh.\n78: Rule: fetch server-side from the existing endpoint; on failure use the existing fallback; if `require_attention` is true, block interaction until acknowledged; render as untrusted text.\n79: Enforcement: announcement service and frontend.\n80: Fallback: show the fallback link and do not block.\n81: \n82: ## WEB-POLICY-012 — Untrusted rendering\n83: \n84: Trigger: model output, tool output, announcement, artifact text, or portfolio text.\n85: Rule: render as escaped text or a sanitized Markdown subset. No raw HTML, no script execution, no `javascript:` or `data:` links, no server-side template evaluation.\n86: Enforcement: frontend renderer and response encoders.\n87: Fallback: render as plain text.\n88: \n89: ## WEB-POLICY-013 — Error redaction\n90: \n91: Trigger: any validation, upstream, storage, or internal error.\n92: Rule: return a safe category and message; redact keys, tokens, cookies, authorization headers, absolute paths, and stack traces.\n93: Enforcement: error mapper and logger.\n94: Fallback: generic internal error with a correlation id.\n95: \n96: ## WEB-POLICY-014 — Bounded event buffer\n97: \n98: Trigger: event publication.\n99: Rule: keep a bounded buffer per run; when a client falls behind the retained window, send a snapshot instead of replaying indefinitely.\n100: Enforcement: event projection.\n101: Fallback: drop the client to snapshot mode; keep the run alive.\n102: \n103: ## WEB-POLICY-015 — No execution authority\n104: \n105: Trigger: any rating, report, or model output.\n106: Rule: display only. No endpoint may place an order, change a position, or treat text as a command.\n107: Enforcement: route inventory and security tests.\n108: Fallback: remove the endpoint or control.\n109: \n110: ## WEB-POLICY-016 — Honest run state\n111: \n112: Trigger: completion, failure, or cancellation.\n113: Rule: derive state from actual stream completion and artifact writes. Do not report an unreadable rating as a success position. Show partial artifacts as partial.\n114: Enforcement: run coordinator and report projection.\n115: Fallback: show a failed/review state and preserve the raw decision text."
