                "text": "## 8. Interface contracts\n\n<a id=\"run-request\"></a>\n### 8.1 Run request\n\n`POST /api/runs` accepts:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"client_request_id\": \"uuid\",\n  \"ticker\": \"NVDA\",\n  \"trade_date\": \"2026-11-05\",\n  \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n  \"output_language\": \"English\",\n  \"analysts\": [\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"],\n  \"research_depth\": 1,\n  \"llm_provider\": \"openai\",\n  \"backend_url\": null,\n  \"quick_think_llm\": \"gpt-5.6-luna\",\n  \"deep_think_llm\": \"gpt-5.6\",\n  \"google_thinking_level\": null,\n  \"openai_reasoning_effort\": null,\n  \"anthropic_effort\": null,\n  \"checkpoint\": false,\n  \"portfolio_json\": null\n}\n```\n\nValidation:\n- Ticker: CLI charset/length rules, then canonicalization.\n- Date: `YYYY-MM-DD`, not in the future.\n- Analysts: at least one known key; crypto excludes fundamentals.\n- Depth: one of 1, 3, 5.\n- Provider/model: resolve through the existing provider/catalogue code.\n- Portfolio: validated by `PortfolioContext`; three states preserved.\n- No client-supplied filesystem path or config dictionary is accepted.\n- `client_request_id` deduplicates double submits within the active run.\n\nSuccess: `201` with `{run_id, status, started_at}`. Conflict: `409`.\n\n<a id=\"run-state\"></a>\n### 8.2 Run state\n\nStates: `idle`, `starting`, `running`, `cancelling`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.\n\nOnly one run may be in `starting`, `running`, or `cancelling`.\n\nRun record: `run_id`, request fields, `status`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `last_seq`, `signal`, `review`, `artifact_ids`, `warnings`, and a safe error category.\n\n`GET /api/runs/{run_id}` returns the snapshot; `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` returns SSE.\n\n<a id=\"cancellation\"></a>\n### 8.3 Cancellation\n\n1. Set the cancellation event.\n2. Stop consuming the graph stream at the next chunk boundary.\n3. End the checkpoint scope in `finally`.\n4. Do not call `record_decision`.\n5. Do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`.\n6. Keep artifacts already written.\n7. Mark `cancelled` and publish `run.cancelled`.\n\nIf checkpointing was disabled, the run cannot be resumed. If enabled, the existing checkpoint remains for the existing resume path. If the worker does not finish within 30 seconds, return `cancelling`; the single-run slot remains occupied until the worker exits.\n\n<a id=\"reattachment\"></a>\n### 8.4 Reattachment\n\n- The run continues while the server process lives.\n- The client gets a snapshot, then connects to SSE with `after_seq`.\n- The server replays the buffer or sends a snapshot if the sequence is too old.\n- After a server restart the active run is gone; on-disk artifacts and checkpoints may remain for CLI/API paths. Cross-process recovery is out of scope.\n\n<a id=\"report-artifact-contract\"></a>\n### 8.5 Report and artifact contract\n\n- `write_report_tree` remains the only report-layout writer.\n- The run directory layout follows the CLI path.\n- The runtime artifact writer mirrors the CLI's `message_tool.log` and `reports/<section>.md` writes.\n- On successful completion the coordinator auto-saves the complete report tree to `results_dir/reports/<ticker>_<timestamp>/`, matching the CLI default save choice.\n- Downloads resolve an artifact id server-side; `kind=complete|archive|section`.\n- The complete Markdown report and a zip of existing report artifacts are the supported downloads. No PDF/Word.\n- A report-save failure produces `run.completed` with `warnings: [\"report_save_failed\"]`; it does not rewrite the analysis result.\n\n<a id=\"history-contract\"></a>\n### 8.6 History contract\n\n- Read-only projection over the sources in Section 6.5.\n- History item identified by a stable hash artifact id.\n- Missing fields are shown as absent.\n- No delete, rename, move, retention change, or index write.\n- No server path is returned.\n\n<a id=\"error-taxonomy\"></a>\n### 8.7 Error taxonomy\n\n| Category | Meaning | Client behaviour |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `validation` | A request field is invalid | Show field errors; do not start |\n| `conflict` | A run is already active | Explain and offer to view the active run |\n| `not_found` | Run or artifact id does not resolve | Show a safe not-found message |\n| `config` | Provider/model/key configuration is unusable | Show the safe configuration error |\n| `upstream` | Data vendor or model provider failed | Show a safe retryable message; preserve the run record |\n| `storage` | Artifact write/read failed | Show a safe storage message; do not expose paths |\n| `cancelled` | The user cancelled | Show the cancellation state |\n| `internal` | Unexpected failure | Show a generic message with a correlation id |\n\nHTTP mapping: `422 validation`, `409 conflict`, `404 not_found`, `403 security`, `413 size`, `502 upstream`, `500 storage/internal`.\n\n<a id=\"state-ownership-and-concurrency\"></a>\n## 9. State ownership and concurrency\n\n| State | Owner | Storage | Lifetime | Writers | Readers |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Active run record | `RunCoordinator` | Process memory | Until server exit or 5 min after terminal state | Coordinator only | API, SSE |\n| Event sequence | `EventBuffer` | Bounded process memory | Run + 5 min | Projector only | SSE subscribers |\n| Graph/checkpoint | `TradingAgentsGraph` | Core objects + SQLite | Run / existing checkpoint | Worker thread | Coordinator |\n| Decision log | `TradingMemoryLog` via graph | Markdown file | Persistent | Graph only | History read model |\n| Run artifacts | `RunArtifactWriter` | Existing `results_dir` layout | Persistent | Worker thread | History read model |\n| History index | `ArtifactIndex` | Process memory cache | 5 s TTL | Scan only | History API |\n| UI state | Zustand store | Browser memory | Tab lifetime | Frontend | Frontend |\n| CLI preferences | `cli.prefs` | `~/.tradingagents/cli_prefs.json` | Persistent | CLI only | Config projection |\n\n- One process, one active run, one worker thread. This is the synchronization mechanism for the global configuration, decision log, and checkpoint database.\n- The artifact read model never writes.\n- Introducing concurrent runs requires per-run configuration isolation, a serialized or owned decision-log writer, per-run artifact namespaces, and a lost-update test. This blueprint does not authorize that change.\n\n<a id=\"deterministic-boundaries-preserved\"></a>\n## 10. Deterministic boundaries preserved\n\nThe web layer calls, not reimplements:\n\n- `_validate_trade_date` and the core date rules.\n- `safe_ticker_component` for every path component.\n- `PortfolioContext` validation and fingerprinting.\n- `extract_rating` / `parse_rating` and the `REVIEW` sentinel.\n- `write_report_tree` for report layout.\n- `TradingMemoryLog` through the graph's existing methods.\n- `run_backtest` and `summarize` for backtest semantics.\n\nThe web layer never:\n\n- Converts `REVIEW` to `Hold` or to a trade.\n- Treats an absent portfolio as a flat book.\n- Reads the live memory log from a backtest.\n- Bypasses point-in-time filters.\n- Accepts a ticker, run id, or path the core would reject.\n- Exposes a provider key or server filesystem path.\n\n## 11. Security and permission boundary\n\nThe full matrix is `docs/architecture/permission-model.md`. Summary:\n\n- Loopback-only listener; no authentication; Host/Origin/CSRF/CSP compensating controls.\n- Server-only provider keys; status-only UI.\n- Artifact identifiers, not paths; root allowlist.\n- Untrusted content sanitized; no raw HTML; URL scheme allowlist.\n- No trading or position-changing endpoint.\n- Destructive checkpoint clear requires explicit confirmation and is disabled during a run.\n- History is read-only.\n- Errors and logs are redacted.\n\n## 12. Deployment, build, and packaging\n\n- Python 3.10+; `pip install -e '.[dev,web]'`.\n- Frontend: Node 22 LTS, npm, `npm ci`, `npm run build`.\n"

\"\n    \"script-src 'self'; \"\n    \"style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; \"\n    \"img-src 'self' data:; \"\n    \"font-src 'self'; \"\n    \"connect-src 'self'; \"\n    \"frame-ancestors 'none'; \"\n    \"base-uri 'none'; re.compile(r\"_(\\d{8})_\")\nCOMPLETE_TICKER_RE = re.compile(r\"Trading Analysis Report:\\s*([A-Za-z0-9._\\-^=+]+)\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Artifact:\n    artifact_id: str\n    source: return {\n            \"artifact_id\": self.artifact_id,\n            \"source\": self.source,\n            \"ticker\": self.ticker,\n            \"date\": self.date,\n            \"status\": self.status,\n            \"rating\": self.rating,\n            \"review\": self.review,\n            \"updated_at\": datetime.fromtimestamp(\n                self.updated_at, tz=timezone.utc\n            ).isoformat(),\n            \"title\": self.title,\n        }\n\n\ndef _digest(path: Path, root: Path, prefix: str = \"\") -> str:\n    try:\n        relative = path.relative_to(root)\n    except ValueError:\n        relative = path\n    return sha256(f\"{prefix}{relative}\".encode()).hexdigest()[:16]\n\n\ndef _mtime(path: Path) -> float:\n    if path.is_file():\n        return path.stat().st_mtime\n    times = [entry.stat().st_mtime for entry in path.rglob(\"*\") if entry.is_file()]\n    return max(times, default=path.stat().st_mtime)\n\n\ndef _read(path: Path) -> str:\n | None:\n    try:\n        return safe_ticker_component(name)\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\nclass ArtifactIndex:\n    \"\"\"Scan the configured results directory and memory log on items\n\n    def find(self, artifact_id: str) -> Artifact | None:\n        return next(\n            (item for item in self.scan() if item.artifact_id == artifact_id),\n            None,\n        )\n\n    def _scan_runs(self) -> list[Artifact]:\n        found: list[Artifact] = []\n        if not self.results_dir.is_dir():\n            return found\n        for ticker_dir in               "content": "\"\"\"Server-side announcement fetch with a short cache and safe fallback.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport time\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Request\n\nfrom cli.announcements import fetch_announcements\nfrom cli.config import CLI_CONFIG\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/api\", tags=[\"announcements\"])\n\nCACHE_SECONDS = 60.0\n_RICH_TAG_RE = re.compile(r\"\\[/?[A-Za-z][^\\]]*\\]\")\n\n\ndef _fallback_text() -> str:\n    return _RICH_TAG_RE.sub(\"\", str(CLI_CONFIG[\"announcements_fallback\"])).strip()\n\n\ndef _normalise(data: Any) -> dict:\n    if not isinstance(data, dict):\n        raise ValueError(\"announcement payload must be an object\")\n    raw = data.get(\"announcements\")\n    if not isinstance(raw, list):\n        raise ValueError(\"announcements must be a list\")\n    announcements = [str(item) for item in raw if isinstance(item, str) and item]\n    return {\n        \"announcements\": announcements or [_fallback_text()],\n        \"require_attention\": bool(data.get(\"require_attention\", False)),\n    }\n\n\n@router.get(\"/announcements\")\ndef get_announcements(request: Request):\n    cached = getattr(request.app.state, \"announcement_cache\", None)\n    now = time.monotonic()\n    if cached is not None and now - cached[\"at\"] < CACHE_SECONDS:\n        return cached[\"data\"]\n\n    try:\n        payload = _normalise(fetch_announcements(timeout=1.0))\n    except Exception:\n        payload = {\n            \"announcements\": [_fallback_text()],\n            \"require_attention\": False,\n        }\n    request.app.state.announcement_cache = {\"at\": now, \"data\": payload}\n    return payload\n",

null : parsed;\n}\n\nfunction validateTicker(value: string): string | null {\n  const ticker = value.trim();\n  if (!ticker) return \"Ticker is required.\";\n  if (ticker.length > 32 || !TICKER_RE.test(ticker)) {\n    return \"Ticker contains unsupported characters.\";\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport function validateBacktest(\n  values: Record<string, unknown>,\n): BacktestValidationResult {\n  const tickers = Array.isArray(values.tickers) ?                 "type": "text",
                "text": "# TradingAgents WebUI Architecture Blueprint\n\nStatus: **Architecture decisions approved for documentation by the human owner on 2026-11-05.** No product implementation is approved. Implementation remains blocked until the test plan, safety review, governance review, and dependency approval listed in Section 15 are complete.\n\nOwner: human project owner. Prepared by the Docs role on 2026-11-05. The selected stack is recorded in ADR-001 through ADR-007.\n\n## 1. Authority and scope\n\nThis blueprint is subordinate to `AGENTS.md`, `Prompt.md`, `.agent/rules.md`, `.opencode/rules.md`, and `docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md`. It extends the TradingAgents v0.5.0 baseline at commit `2d17df8da1536c121e4d7395ac5a5dcec9e96d6f` on branch `feature/webui`. It does not replace the baseline, the CLI, the Python API, or any existing business rule.\n\nThe WebUI is a **local, single-user, single-active-run presentation layer**. It displays and orchestrates capabilities that already exist. It must not add analysis capability, data sources, model providers, trading behaviour, agent logic, or persistence.\n\n<a id=\"goals\"></a>\n## 2. Goals\n\n1. Expose the complete CLI analysis workflow through a browser: the eight selection steps, live run view, completion summary, and full I–V report.\n2. Preserve every deterministic boundary already enforced by the core and CLI: ticker and path validation, analysis-date limits, rating integrity, portfolio semantics, point-in-time data access, memory isolation, and checkpoint behaviour.\n3.             "content": [
              {
                "type": "text",
                "text": "# ADR-007: Single-Run Slot, Cancellation, Reattachment, and Backtest Controls\n\n- Status: **Accepted for documentation** by the human owner on 2026-11-05.\n- Date: 2026-11-05\n- Related requirements: `REQ-WEB-003`, `REQ-WEB-005`, `REQ-WEB-006`, `REQ-WEB-007`, `REQ-WEB-011`, `REQ-WEB-029`, `REQ-WEB-030`\n- Related invariants: `INV-WEB-008`, `INV-WEB-009`, `INV-WEB-010`, `INV-WEB-014`\n- Related ADRs: ADR-001, ADR-002\n- Related blueprint: `architecture-blueprint.md` Sections 6.2, 6.6, 8.2–8.4, 9, 13\n\n## Context\n\nThe core exposes a synchronous graph stream and a synchronous `run_backtest`. It has no cancellation hook inside `run_backtest`, and its configuration and decision log are not proven safe under concurrent writers. The confirmed scope is one active run, analysis cancellation with CLI-equivalent semantics, process-lifetime reattachment, and backtest launch/view. The UI must not present a capability the core does not have.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **One active run per process.** The coordinator admits one analysis or backtest; a second request receives `409` with the active run id. There is no queue.\n2. **Worker-thread execution.** The synchronous graph stream runs in a single-worker `ThreadPoolExecutor`; events return through `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`.\n3. **Analysis cancellation.** Set a `threading.Event`; stop at the next chunk boundary; do not call `record_decision`; do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`; call `end_checkpoint()` in `finally`; keep partial artifacts; publish `run.cancelled`.\n4. **Cancellation timeout.** If the worker does not stop within 30 seconds, mark the run `cancelling`; the slot remains occupied until the worker exits. Do not kill the thread.\n5. **Reattachment.** The client fetches a snapshot and reconnects to SSE with `after_seq`. The server replays buffered events or sends a snapshot. Process restart loses the active run.\n6. **Backtest has no cancel button.** `run_backtest` has no cooperative cancellation hook. The UI states that the backtest runs to completion and can be resumed with `run_id` after an interruption.\n7. **Checkpoint clear.** Requires explicit `{\"confirm\": \"CLEAR\"}` and is rejected during an active run.\n8. **Honest states.** Do not emit an `error` agent status (the CLI never sets it). Failures are run-level `run.failed`; REVIEW is a review state, not a position.\n\n## Consequences\n\n### Positive\n\n- No unproven concurrent writers.\n- Cancellation semantics match the CLI's actual `Ctrl-C` behavior.\n- Reattachment survives browser reloads without new storage.\n- The UI does not promise backtest cancellation that cannot be delivered.\n- The single-run slot is easy to reason about and test.\n\n### Negative / costs\n\n- No parallel analyses.\n- Cancellation can take up to the current model call to take effect.\n- A hung provider call can occupy the slot for a long time; the 30-second timeout only reports `cancelling`.\n- Backtests may run for a long time without a stop control.\n- Reattachment is lost on server restart.\n\n### Risks and mitigations\n\n- **Stuck worker.** Show `cancelling`, keep the slot, log the state; do not spawn a second run.\n- **User expects backtest cancel.** Explicit UI copy; no disabled-looking control that pretends to work.\n- **Race between cancel and completion.** Use a single state transition under the coordinator lock; completion wins only if it occurred before cancellation was observed.\n- **SSE reconnect storms.** Heartbeat, bounded queue, and a short retry delay.\n- **Restart confusion.** Health/snapshot returns \"run no longer available\"; artifacts remain.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. Serial queue — deferred; adds a scheduler without confirmed need.\n2. Parallel runs — rejected; requires core configuration isolation and memory write ownership.\n3. Kill the worker thread — rejected; Python cannot safely kill threads, and it could corrupt checkpoints.\n4. Wrap `run_backtest` with a fake cancel flag — rejected; it would report a stop that did not happen.\n5. Persist run state to disk — deferred; new storage and recovery design.\n=== 005 ===\n# ADR-005: Read-Only History and Artifact Identifiers\n\n- Status: **Accepted for documentation** by the human owner on 2026-11-05.\n- Date: 2026-11-05\n- Related requirements: `REQ-WEB-009`, `REQ-WEB-010`, `REQ-WEB-024`, `REQ-WEB-030`\n- Related invariants: `INV-WEB-004`, `INV-WEB-005`, `INV-WEB-011`\n- Related ADRs: ADR-001, ADR-006\n- Related blueprint: `architecture-blueprint.md` Sections 6.5, 8.5, 8.6\n\n## Context\n\nThe CLI and API already write run artifacts in several places: per-run directories, API-style state logs, manually saved report trees, and backtest run directories. The decision memory is a separate Markdown log. The user selected read-only history over existing artifacts and explicitly excluded a new database or message queue. The browser must not receive server filesystem paths.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **History is a read-only projection** over existing artifacts. No delete, rename, move, rotation, migration, or index database.\n2. **Artifact identifier: `sha256(canonical_relative_path)[:16]`.** The server builds the id-to-path map during a scan and keeps it in a short-lived in-memory cache (5 s TTL). Nothing is persisted.\n3. **Resolution:** decode the id through the map; reject unknown ids. The resolved path must stay under an allowlisted root and pass `safe_ticker_component` for every user-derived component.\n4. **Sources:** run directories, saved report trees, backtest runs, and the decision memory. API-style `full_states_log_*.json` is optional.\n5. **Downloads:** `kind=complete` serves `complete_report.md` when present; `kind=archive` streams an in-memory zip of existing report files; `kind=section` serves an allowlisted section. The server does not synthesize a complete report that does not exist.\n6. **No server paths in responses.** Responses include ticker, date, source, status, rating, review flag, timestamps, section ids, and artifact ids.\n7. **Limits:** at most 500 runs per scan, 50 per page, bounded report size, and no unbounded log reads.\n\n## Consequences\n\n### Positive\n\n- No second source of truth and no database migration.\n- Existing CLI/API artifacts become browsable without copying them.\n- Hash ids avoid exposing host paths.\n- Read-only design eliminates most destructive failure modes.\n- Works for CLI-style runs that lack a state log.\n\n### Negative / costs\n\n- Every history request may need a directory scan; the cache mitigates but does not eliminate cost.\n- Hash ids are not human-readable; the UI must display ticker/date metadata.\n- Artifacts written by different paths have different shapes; readers must handle missing fields.\n- Downloads cannot reconstruct a report tree that was never saved.\n- The cache must be invalidated on mtime/size change.\n\n### Risks and mitigations\n\n- **Path traversal.** Never accept paths; map ids; validate roots; reject `..`, absolute paths, backslashes.\n- **Large directories.** Scan limits and pagination.\n- **Partial runs.** Derive status from explicit artifacts; show partial, never synthesize.\n- **Stale cache.** TTL plus mtime/size checks.\n- **Zip memory.** Bound total archive size; stream to the client; reject oversized sets.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. New index database — rejected; second source of truth, new dependency, storage approval.\n2. Current-session-only history — rejected; confirmed requirement reads existing artifacts.\n3. Base64 of the path as the id — rejected; reversible encoding still leaks path structure.\n4. Raw relative paths in responses — rejected; violates the no-path boundary.\n5. Reconstructing reports from `full_states_log` — rejected for CLI-style runs that lack it; no synthesis.\n"

              "content": "# ADR-011: Backtest Surface and Isolation\n\n- Status: **Implemented under the user-approved Iteration-3 plan; architecture review pending.**\n- Date: 2026-11-06\n- Related requirements: `REQ-WEB-006`, `REQ-WEB-011`, `REQ-WEB-027`, `REQ-WEB-030`\n- Related invariants: `INV-WEB-008`, `INV-WEB-009`, `INV-WEB-011`, `INV-WEB-014`\n- Related ADRs: ADR-005, ADR-007\n- Related blueprint: `architecture-blueprint.md` Sections 6.2, 6.5, 6.6, 8.6, 9\n\n## Context\n\n`run_backtest` is synchronous and has no cancellation hook. It writes an\nisolated `results_dir/backtest/<run_id>/trading_memory.md`, while the live\ndecision memory must stay untouched. The WebUI needs launch, status, summary,\nlog download, and read-only history without adding a second execution engine or\nnew analysis capability.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **Reuse the core.** The web layer calls `iter_grid`, `run_backtest`, and\n   `summarize`; it does not reimplement grid generation or scoring.\n2. **Single slot.** A backtest and an analysis share the coordinator's\n   single-active-run slot. A second request returns `409`.\n3. **Isolation.** The wrapper passes the live `results_dir` to\n   `run_backtest` (so the core owns the run directory) and points\n   `memory_log_path` at the backtest run directory. The live decision log is\n   never opened for writing.\n4. **Identity.** The browser-facing run id is a `bt_<hex>` identifier. A\n   client-supplied `run_id` is validated with `safe_ticker_component` and\n   forwarded to the core for resume; otherwise the core chooses its timestamp\n   id, matching CLI behaviour.\n5. **No cancellation.** No cancel route or UI control exists. The UI states\n   that a backtest runs to completion and can be resumed with `run_id`.\n6. **Summary.** Responses expose resolved, pending, unscored, per-rating\n   count/hit rate/mean alpha, holding window, failures, settlement failures,\n   and a log artifact id. They never expose `log_path`.\n7. **Read-only history.** `GET /api/backtests` scans existing backtest\n   directories and merges process-memory records. No deletion or mutation\n   endpoint exists. The log is downloadable through the existing artifact-id\n   download path with `kind=log`.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Backtests use the existing semantics and artifacts, but can occupy the only\n  run slot for a long time.\n- The browser never receives a filesystem path.\n- A backtest cannot be stopped through the WebUI.\n- After a process restart, a completed backtest is discoverable by its on-disk\n  id; the browser-facing `bt_` id is retained only for the process lifetime\n  when no client `run_id` was supplied.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. Separate backtest worker pool — rejected; adds concurrency and memory-write\n   risk the core does not support.\n2. Fake cancellation flag — rejected; it would claim a stop that did not\n   happen.\n3. New backtest database or queue — rejected; no new persistence is approved.\n4. Reimplementing summary calculations — rejected; `summarize` is\n   authoritative.\n",

            "input": {
              "content": "# ADR-012: Announcements and Untrusted External Content\n\n- Status: **Implemented under the user-approved Iteration-3 plan; architecture review pending.**\n- Date: 2026-11-06\n- Related requirements: `REQ-WEB-012`, `REQ-WEB-020`, `REQ-WEB-023`, `REQ-WEB-024`, `REQ-WEB-025`\n- Related invariants: `INV-WEB-012`, `INV-WEB-013`\n- Related ADRs: ADR-006\n- Related blueprint: `architecture-blueprint.md` Sections 6.1, 6.7, 8\n\n## Context\n\nThe CLI fetches announcements at startup and prints a fallback when the request\nfails. The WebUI must preserve that advisory behaviour without letting external\ntext become executable content or block a run on a failed request.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **Server-side fetch.** The browser calls `GET /api/announcements`; the\n   server calls the existing `cli.announcements.fetch_announcements`.\n2. **Timeout and fallback.** The request uses a short timeout. Any exception,\n   malformed payload, or empty list returns the existing fallback URL text with\n   `require_attention: false`.\n3. **Cache.** Successful and fallback payloads are cached in process memory for\n   60 seconds. No external text is persisted.\n4. **Attention flag.** `require_attention: true` is forwarded. The frontend\n   shows a blocking dialog until the user acknowledges it; the server does not\n   create a session or persist the acknowledgement.\n5. **Untrusted rendering.** Announcement strings are rendered as text nodes.\n   The component does not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; HTML tags in upstream\n   text remain inert.\n6. **No secrets or paths.** The response contains only announcement strings and\n   the attention flag.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- A failed announcement service cannot prevent a run.\n- Upstream markup is shown literally instead of being interpreted.\n- The acknowledgement is per browser mount, not a durable user preference.\n- The server performs one external request per cache window.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n1. Browser-side fetch — rejected; it exposes the endpoint to client policy and\n   complicates timeout/fallback parity.\n2. Markdown rendering of announcements — rejected; a plain-text boundary is\n   smaller and safer.\n3. Persisting acknowledgement — rejected; no new storage or session feature is\n   approved.\n",
              "path": "[LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents/docs/architecture/adr/012-announcements.md"

            "content": [
              {
                "type": "text",
                "text": "# TradingAgents WebUI Permission Model\n\nStatus: **Approved for documentation by the human owner on 2026-11-05.** Implementation still requires `[safety-approved]` and `[governance-approved]` where applicable. This document defines the WebUI runtime permission boundary and its relationship to the coding-agent roles.\n\n## 1. Scope\n\nThis model covers:\n\n1. What the browser, web service, run coordinator, artifact reader, and core may do.\n2. Which data classes may cross which boundary.\n3. Which actions require explicit confirmation.\n4. How the coding-agent roles in `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` relate to the product boundary.\n\nIt does not replace the OS sandbox, the OpenCode permission configuration, or a human approval decision.\n\n## 2. Subjects and ownership\n\n| Subject | Owns | May read | May write | May execute |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Browser SPA | Presentation state | Same-origin API responses | Browser local storage only | No server code |\n| FastAPI HTTP layer | Request parsing, validation, error mapping | Request body, config projection | HTTP response | No arbitrary command |\n| Run coordinator | Active run record, worker future, cancel event, event buffer | Validated run request, graph state | Run record, event buffer, run artifacts through the writer | Calls existing Python APIs |\n| Graph runner | One `TradingAgentsGraph` instance | Core config and state | Graph/checkpoint/decision-log through existing methods | Runs the analysis graph |\n| Artifact read model | Read-only index cache | Allowlisted artifact roots | Nothing | No |\n| Backtest runner | One backtest invocation | Backtest request, isolated run dir | Backtest log through `run_backtest` | Calls existing backtest |\n| Core (`tradingagents`) | Business rules, ratings, data access, memory, checkpoints | Its own config/data | Its own artifacts | Existing behaviour only |\n| CLI (`cli`) | Terminal interaction | Core API, prefs | CLI files/artifacts | Existing behaviour only |\n| Operator | Server process, environment | Server logs and artifacts | Environment, filesystem | Starts/stops the server |\n\n## 3. Runtime permission matrix\n\n| Action | Browser | Web API | Coordinator | Artifact reader | Core/CLI |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Read effective config | via API, redacted | allow | read | — | source |\n| Read provider key value | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — | server env only |\n| Read key status | allow | allow | — | — | — |\n| Start analysis | allow | allow if validated | allow if no active run | — | — |\n| Start backtest | allow | allow if validated | allow if no active run | — | — |\n| Cancel analysis | allow | allow | allow | — | — |\n| Cancel backtest | **deny** (no route) | **deny** | **deny** | — | no hook |\n| Read live run state | allow | allow | own | — | — |\n| Read history | allow | allow | — | allow | — |\n| Delete/rename history | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — |\n| Download report | allow via id | allow via id | — | allow | writer source |\n| Accept server path | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — |\n| Clear all checkpoints | allow with confirmation | allow with confirmation | allow if idle | — | clear method |\n| Place an order | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — | **deny** |\n| Change agent/prompt/rating rules | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — | out of scope |\n| Write `.env` / keys | **deny** | **deny** | **deny** | — | CLI only, not web |\n\n## 4. Data classification\n\n| Class | Examples | Allowed destinations | Prohibited destinations |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Secret | Provider API keys, tokens, cookies, authorization headers | Server process environment and provider SDK | Browser, events, logs, reports, downloads, errors, snapshots |\n| Internal path | `results_dir`, `data_cache_dir`, `memory_log_path`, absolute paths | Server code and redacted logs | Browser responses, events, errors, downloads |\n| User data | Ticker, date, portfolio, selected models | Browser ↔ API, run artifacts | Third-party services beyond the configured model/data providers |\n| Model/external text | Reports, tool output, announcements | Sanitized rendering and stored artifacts | Executable HTML, server-side evaluation, permission decisions |\n| Run metadata | Run id, status, rating, review flag, timestamps | Browser and artifacts | — |\n| History artifact | Report sections, decision log entries | Read-only browser view and downloads | Mutation by the web layer |\n\n## 5. Permission boundary enforcement\n\n| Boundary | Rule | Enforcement | Fallback |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Network | Loopback only; no auth | `settings.py` rejects non-loopback bind; `security.py` Host/Origin checks | Refuse to start or reject request |\n| Request origin | Same-origin state-changing requests | CSRF token, Origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site`, no wildcard CORS | 403 |\n| Secrets | Server-only | Config projection returns status; serializers allowlist; error redaction | Remove field / rotate credential |\n| Filesystem | Artifact ids only | Hash index; root allowlist; `safe_ticker_component` | 404/400 |\n| Uploads | Portfolio JSON text only | Size limit; parse; discard | 413/422 |\n| Execution | No trading route | Route inventory; security test | Remove endpoint |\n| History | Read-only | No mutating route; read model | Reject mutation |\n| Checkpoints | Clear is destructive | `{\"confirm\":\"CLEAR\"}`; disabled while running | 409 |\n| Rendering | Untrusted content is data | `rehype-sanitize`; no raw HTML; CSP; URL allowlist | Plain text |\n\n## 6. Destructive and privileged actions\n\n1. **Clear all checkpoints**: requires an explicit confirmation token, is disabled while a run is active, and reports only the count cleared.\n2. **Cancel analysis**: requires a same-origin state-changing request; no decision is written and no checkpoint is cleared.\n3. **Start a run**: may consume paid provider capacity; the UI must show provider/model and key status before submission.\n4. **Read decision memory**: read-only; no rotation or deletion from the web.\n5. **Download artifacts**: only through a resolved artifact id; filenames are sanitized; no path input.\n\n## 7. Coding-agent role boundary\n\nThe development roles remain defined by `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` and `AGENTS.md`. This document does not grant additional tool or path access.\n\n| Role | Product-code edits | Docs edits | Tests | Git/remote |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Plan | Denied | Denied | Read-only | Status only |\n| Build | Allowlisted `src/` and `test/`; protected paths require review | Only authorized records | May add tests after approval | Status/diff only |\n| Verify | Denied | Denied | Run only; no weakening | Status/diff only |\n| Docs | Denied | Allowlisted docs | Data validators only | Status/diff only |\n\nAn ACL `allow` is not plan approval. `permission-model.md` itself is a documentation artifact; it does not authorize implementation.\n\n## 8. Denials and fallback actions\n\n- A denied action returns a safe error category; it is not retried through a shell or another tool.\n- A missing key is a configuration state, not a permission bypass.\n- A rejected Host/Origin/CSRF request is logged with a reason but no payload.\n- A failed artifact resolution returns `not_found`; it never falls back to a broader root.\n- A failed sanitizer render falls back to plain text.\n\n## 9. Review and change control\n\n- Changes to this model require human review and a corresponding update to `docs/architecture/invariants.md`, `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md`, and the relevant ADR.\n- Any proposal to add authentication, network exposure, new storage, execution, or browser key input is a scope change, not a configuration tweak.\n- No agent may edit `.opencode/rules.md` or `.opencode/permissions.jsonc` to widen its own access.\n=== runtime policy ===\n14:Trigger: a new analysis or backtest request.\n15:Rule: if a run is `starting`, `running`, or `cancelling`, return `409` with the active run id. No queue.\n26:## WEB-POLICY-004 — Analysis cancellation\n28:Trigger: a same-origin cancel request for the active analysis.\n29:Rule: set the cancel event; stop at the next chunk; do not call `record_decision`; do not call `clear_checkpoint_on_success`; `end_checkpoint()` in `finally`; keep partial artifacts; publish `run.cancelled`.\n31:Fallback: if the worker does not stop in 30 s, report `cancelling` and keep the slot until it exits.\n63:Trigger: history or backtest-history request.\n70:Trigger: backtest request.\n71:Rule: use the backtest's own run directory and memory log; never read or write the live decision log. A backtest occupies the single-run slot.\n72:Enforcement: `runtime/backtest_runner.py`.\n79:Enforcement: `api/announcements.py`, `frontend/src/components/Announcements`.\n84:Trigger: model output, tool output, announcements, artifact text, portfolio text.\n112:Trigger: completion, failure, cancellation.\n117:## WEB-POLICY-017 — Backtest has no cancel control\n119:Trigger: a backtest is running.\n120:Rule: do not expose a cancel route or button. State that the backtest runs to completion and can be resumed with `run_id`.\n121:Enforcement: `api/backtests.py`, `frontend/src/pages/Backtest`.\n141:Rule: write `message_tool.log` and `reports/<section>.md` in the CLI layout; auto-save the complete tree on success; keep partial artifacts on cancel/failure; do not write `full_states_log`.\n"
              }
            ],

          "text": "# 项目启动命令\n\n## 1. 最短启动（依赖已安装、前端已构建）\n\n```bash\ncd [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents\nsource .venv/bin/activate\ntradingagents-web --port 8000\n```\n\n打开：\n\n```text\nhttp://127.0.0.1:8000\n```\n\n也可以使用：\n\n```bash\npython -m tradingagents_web --port 8000\n```\n\n## 2. 首次安装或环境重建\n\n```bash\ncd [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents\n\npython3 -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate\n\npython -m pip install -e '.[dev,web]'\n\ncd src/tradingagents_web/frontend\nnpm ci\nnpm run build\ncd -\n```\n\n然后启动：\n\n```bash\ntradingagents-web --port 8000\n```\n\n## 3. 前端开发模式\n\n终端 1，启动后端：\n\n```bash\ncd [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents\nsource .venv/bin/activate\ntradingagents-web --port 8000\n```\n\n终端 2，启动 Vite：\n\n```bash\ncd [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents/src/tradingagents_web/frontend\nnpm run dev\n```\n\n访问 Vite 输出的地址，通常是：\n\n```text\nhttp://127.0.0.1:5173\n```\n\n`/api` 会代理到 `http://127.0.0.1:8000`。\n\n## 4. CLI 分析入口\n\n```bash\nsource .venv/bin/activate\ntradingagents --help\ntradingagents backtest --help\n```\n\n## 5. 测试命令\n\n```bash\n# 后端\n.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --disable-socket --allow-unix-socket test/offline\n\n# 前端单元测试\ncd src/tradingagents_web/frontend\nnpm test\n\n# Chromium E2E（需先 npm run build）\nnpm run build\nnpm run e2e\n```\n\n## 6. 注意事项\n\n- WebUI 只监听 `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`。\n- 模型密钥只放在服务端环境变量中，例如 `OPENAI_API_KEY`，不要放到前端。\n- 回测和实际分析共享同一个运行槽位，同时只能运行一个任务。\n- 回测没有取消按钮，必须运行至完成或使用同一 `run_id` 续跑。\n- 启动时如果静态资源缺失，会提示先执行 `npm run build`。"

          "text": "# 设置 DeepSeek API Key\n\nDeepSeek 使用环境变量：\n\n```text\nDEEPSEEK_API_KEY\n```\n\nWebUI **不接受浏览器端输入的 Key**，只读取服务端环境变量。\n\n## 方式一：写入项目根目录 `.env`（推荐）\n\n在项目根目录创建或编辑 `.env`：\n\n```bash\ncd [LOCAL_USER_HOME]/Workspace/Projects/cityu/cs5351/TradingAgents\ntouch .env\nchmod 600 .env\n```\n\n写入：\n\n```dotenv\nDEEPSEEK_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]\n```\n\n然后重启 WebUI：\n\n```bash\nsource .venv/bin/activate\ntradingagents-web --port 8000\n```\n\n项目启动时会自动加载当前工作目录的 `.env`。`.env` 已在 `.gitignore` 中，不要提交。\n\n## 方式二：当前终端临时导出\n\n```bash\nexport DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]\"\ntradingagents-web --port 8000\n```\n\n必须在**启动 WebUI 的同一个终端**里执行 `export`。\n\n## 验证是否生效\n\n启动 WebUI 后：\n\n```bash\ncurl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/config \\\n  | python3 -c \"import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['key_status']['deepseek'])\"\n```\n\n输出：\n\n```text\nconfigured\n```\n\n如果输出 `not_configured`，说明当前服务进程没有读到该变量；设置后需要重启 WebUI。\n\n## 在 WebUI 中选择 DeepSeek\n\n新建分析时：\n\n- LLM Provider：`deepseek`\n- Quick model：`deepseek-flash`\n- Deep model：`deepseek-v4-pro` 或 `deepseek-flash`\n\n## 注意事项\n\n- 不要把 Key 写成 `VITE_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`；`VITE_` 变量会被打包进前端。\n- 不要通过 WebUI 页面提交 Key。\n- `.env` 建议权限 `600`。\n- 如果是长期运行的服务，建议使用服务管理器或 shell profile 注入环境变量，而不是把 Key 写进源码或 Docker 镜像。\n- CLI 首次使用 DeepSeek 时也会提示输入 Key，并可保存到 `.env`；WebUI 不会弹出该提示。"

                "text": "# TradingAgents research workspace — interaction prototype\n\nAn independent, offline UI concept derived from the Python backend. Open\n**index.html** directly in a modern browser. No installation, build, server, API\nkey, or backend process is required.\n\nAll content, provider status, reports, durations, and evaluation results are\nillustrative fixtures. Nothing in this directory connects to an API, executes a\ntrade, reads actual history, or changes server checkpoints.\n\n## Scope and approach\n\nThe current user request explicitly authorizes this new demo directory. It is\na design exploration, not a replacement for the application or a prerequisite\nfor product development. Existing frontend implementation files were not used\nas a design reference. Backend, CLI, application frontend, project dependencies,\nand governance configuration remain unchanged.\n\nThe ui-ux-pro-max skill informed the visual and interaction review. Its\nfinancial/dashboard search supplied useful data-density, semantic-color,\nreadability, and restrained-motion guidance. Its page-pattern matches described\nmarketing sites rather than a research application; those patterns were not\nadopted or persisted as an approved design system. The information architecture\nbelow is a product-specific synthesis of the actual backend.\n\n## Backend-to-interface mapping\n\n| Backend reference                                                         | Observed capability                                                                                                        | Prototype treatment                                                                                                         |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| src/tradingagents_web/models/requests.py, api/runs.py                     | Instrument/date, stock or crypto, report language, analyst selection, depth, model choices, optional portfolio, checkpoint | Three-step analysis sheet: Instrument → Research setup → Review & run                                                       |\n| api/config.py                                                             | Defaults, provider/model catalog, environment locks and server-side key status                                             | Provider-linked example models; read-only sample key status in settings; no credential input                                |\n| runtime/coordinator.py, runtime/graph_runner.py                           | One active task, run states, cancellation, progress, complete snapshots and bounded events                                 | Local staged analysis, background continuation across navigation, active-slot conflict and cancellation                     |\n| runtime/projector.py                                                      | Analyst reports, research plan, trader plan and final risk/portfolio decision                                              | Selected-analyst tabs, a grouped five-stage process and available report sections only                                      |\n| errors.py                                                                 | Distinct market-data failures, configuration failures, safe correlated errors                                              | Explicit market-data-unavailable state; no invented final decision                                                          |\n| api/history.py, artifacts/readers.py                                      | Read-only analysis/saved reports, backtest artifacts, decision memory and report downloads                                 | Searchable/sortable analysis history, report reader, local Markdown sample export and decision journal                      |\n| api/backtests.py, models/backtest_requests.py, runtime/backtest_runner.py | Fixed-date ticker grid, cadence, analysts, optional book/run ID, aggregate counts and by-rating hit rate/mean alpha        | Configurable sample sweep, categorical alpha chart and equivalent accessible table; no equity curve or cancellation control |\n| api/portfolio.py, src/tradingagents/portfolio.py                          | Optional book validation; absent, explicitly flat and populated books are distinct                                         | Optional JSON context with inline errors; disabling context differs from {\"positions\":[]}                                   |\n| api/checkpoints.py                                                        | Idle-only checkpoint clearing with confirm: CLEAR                                                                          | Idle-only typed confirmation; cleared count appears only after the sample response                                          |\n| api/announcements.py                                                      | Announcements, attention flag and safe fallback; dismissal is local                                                        | Workspace notes dialog; local fixture only                                                                                  |\n\nPaths in the table are relative to src/tradingagents_web unless fully qualified.\n\n## Visual direction\n\nA quiet research desk: warm paper surfaces, pine-green actions, graphite text,\nand a serif accent within the research brief. Data, readable reasoning, and task\nstates take priority over decorative market graphics.\n\n- **Navigation:** persistent desktop sidebar; compact mobile navigation.\n- **Hierarchy:** one primary New analysis action, followed by the latest\n  assessment, research process, and recent history.\n- **Color:** semantic CSS variables in styles.css; independent light/paper and\n  dark/forest palettes. Ratings and task states always have text equivalents.\n- **Typography:** system sans-serif for controls and tables, Georgia for brief\n  headings, tabular figures for numeric values. No remote fonts.\n- **Motion:** short state transitions, no ambient animation, and reduced-motion\n  support through the user's browser preference.\n- **Charts:** grouped backend-supported summary metrics, with explicit values\n  and table equivalents. No simulated live quotes, calibrated probabilities, brokerage\n  balance, order execution, or invented portfolio return chart.\n\n## Explore the interactions\n\n1. **Overview:** switch research perspectives, open a report, search or filter\n   recent work, and navigate to history or backtests.\n2. **New analysis:** use the three-step sheet; invalid tickers, future dates,\n   missing analysts/models, and malformed portfolio JSON retain editable inputs\n   and show a focusable error summary. Crypto excludes company fundamentals.\n3. **Sample run:** starting an analysis advances five stages locally. It can be\n   cancelled; a successful sample adds a history record and enables Markdown\n   export. Starting a second task opens an active-run explanation.\n4. **Design preview:** the sidebar selector exposes completed, running,\n   market-data-unavailable, manual-review, cancelled, partial-report and report-save-warning states. REVIEW is\n   explicitly distinct from Hold.\n5. **History:** filter by ticker and status, sort dates, inspect empty\n   results, and open a report.\n6. **Backtesting:** validate instruments/date range, run a short local\n   simulation, inspect per-rating results, and download an illustrative log.\n   There is no cancel control. A new sample grid updates the illustrative\n   aggregate counts; score values remain illustrative. Hold has no directional hit rate; zero-count groups have no score. Reusing a sample run ID skips existing cells.\n7. **Journal:** inspect independent read-only sample decision, outcome and reflection entries; a full report is not assumed.\n8. **Settings:** switch themes, inspect sample provider status, and require\n   CLEAR before clearing sample checkpoints.\n9. **Research audit:** inspect five quality-check classes, filter evidence,\n   open provenance details, review debate participation/claims/conflicts,\n   distinguish debate budget from whole-run usage, and preview/download four\n   sample artifact families. The scenario selector exposes normal, degraded,\n   blocked, unreadable-accounting and legacy/missing-audit states.\n10. **Policy comparison:** inspect fixed-round and dynamic policies on scripted\n    cases D/E/F and the input-exhaustion regression G. Try a mismatched snapshot,\n    replay the local fixtures, or export the sample view. Human rubric scores\n    stay pending.\n\nKeyboard: **N** opens a new analysis; **?** opens help; **Cmd/Ctrl K** opens search; **Escape**\ncloses native dialogs and mobile navigation. Report tabs also support arrow,\nHome, and End keys. Native dialogs provide modal focus containment. Closed\nmobile navigation is inert.\n\n## Local state and data boundaries\n\n- Theme and non-sensitive analysis setup are optionally stored under\n  tradingagents.demo.* in browser local storage.\n- Portfolio JSON and endpoint overrides are deliberately excluded from persistent drafts.\n- Runs, history additions, backtest settings/results, and sample checkpoint\n  changes live in memory and reset when the page reloads.\n- Successful analysis and backtest results are fixtures, not financial\n  evaluations. The sample date reference is November 19, 2026.\n- Prototype validation illustrates backend contracts; a future integration must\n  still use authoritative backend validation.\n- Model/environment lock presentation would come from the real configuration\n  projection during an explicitly approved integration. This prototype does not\n  claim that a real key or endpoint is configured. Endpoint and provider-specific thinking overrides are optional local form inputs. Server environment locks and model capability checks must take precedence during integration. Provider labels must be mapped to canonical config keys; this prototype sends no request payload.\n\n## Files\n\n- **index.html** — accessible shell, navigation and dialog containers.\n- **styles.css** — semantic tokens, themes and responsive layouts.\n- **app.js** — fixtures, local navigation, form/state simulation and downloads.\n- **README.md** — design rationale, backend capability mapping and usage.\n\n## Capability audit — November 19, 2026\n\nThe audit compares the prototype to Python request schemas, API handlers,\ncoordinator, event projector, artifact readers/writer, decision memory and core\nbacktest code. Existing application frontend implementation was not inspected.\nAn existing core capability counts as feasible even if an HTTP projection would\nbe needed. No new backend implementation or interface was added.\n\n### Pages and controls\n\n| Page / control                                                           | Existing support or client responsibility                              | Audited behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Brand, sidebar routes, recent links, History / All research / Back links | Browser navigation; history artifact IDs                               | Local navigation; unknown report IDs show an unavailable state.                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n| Overview totals, recent analyses and backtest preview                    | `/api/history`, `/api/backtests`; client aggregation                   | Counts, filtering and sorting are derived presentation, not new business evaluation. Run and saved copies must not be double-counted as separate logical analyses during integration.                                                                       |\n| Market / Sentiment / News / Fundamentals tabs and arrow/Home/End keys    | Projected analyst reports / persisted sections                         | Only selected analyst perspectives appear; crypto has no fundamentals.                                                                                                                                                                                      |\n| New analysis, N, Continue, Back, close/save draft                        | `RunRequest`, config/model projection; local draft                     | Inputs map to existing analysis parameters. Endpoint/thinking overrides are optional; defaults remain available. Not an application API or user workflow.                                                                                                                     |\n\n### Corrections made during the audit\n\n- Removed the invented 50% Hold hit rate and scores for zero-count groups.\n- Removed unselected analyst sections from tabs, full reports and exports.\n- Added cooperative Stopping state and retained-slot behavior, plus partial\n  report reading; checkpoint recovery is conditional on matching inputs.\n- Separated journal decisions/outcomes/reflections from analysis report history.\n- Replaced missing historical provider/depth/duration/language with unavailable\n  labels. The first fixture represents a coordinator snapshot; other examples\n  represent records after runtime metadata is gone.\n- Removed a pre-clear checkpoint count; added partial and save-warning states\n  so a completed run does not imply a downloadable complete artifact.\n- Corrected backtest run-ID validation, repeat-run skipping, ticker deduplication,\n  crypto controls, server-default explanation, current-result downloads and\n  zero-sample behavior.\n- Changed research/final section labels to the actual projected decision\n  outputs. Ticker search no longer promises a company-name directory.\n\nCompany names and sectors are optional, static fixture labels. The history API\ndoes not provide an instrument master. previews and downloads for run summary, evidence manifest, gate summary and debate trace; quality/summary sections in Markdown export |\n| `comparison/fixtures.py`, `comparison/schemas.py`, `comparison/report.py`    | Separate offline policy comparison with the four-part identity check, scripted calls/estimated tokens, stop reasons and pending human rubric                          |\n| `tradingagents_web/models/requests.py`, `api/config.py`                      | Twenty provider display choices including regional aliases; optional endpoint and Google/OpenAI/Anthropic thinking controls; locally selected portfolio JSON          |\n| `tradingagents_web/runtime/projector.py` and callback stats                  | Sample message/tool-call stream, event filter, model/tool calls, token counters and simulated elapsed time during a running sample                                    |\n\nReferences without a package prefix are under `src/tradingagents/`.\nThese artifacts are deliberately reduced view fixtures, not complete serialized\nbackend schemas or integration-ready request/response contracts. Several\ncore capabilities would need an HTTP/read projection in a future integration.\nNo interface work is included here.\n\nQuality semantics are preserved in the presentation: a single evidence record\nis at most Medium; High is a corroborated market-category result.                 "type": "text",
                "text": "// REQ-WEB-005/007, INV-WEB-003: surface only safe server failure details.\nexport type RunConfig = {\n  defaults: Record<string, unknown>;\n  providers: Array<{ key: string; label: string; default_url: string | null }>;\n  env_locks: Record<string, boolean>;\n  key_status: Record<string, string>;\n  prefs: Record<string, unknown>;\n  backend_url_configured?: boolean;\n};\n\nexport type RunSnapshot = {\n  run_id: string;\n  status: string;\n  ticker: string;\n  trade_date: string;\n  last_seq: number;\n  signal?: string | null;\n  review: boolean;\n  warnings: string[];\n  error?: Record<string, unknown> | null;\n};\n\nlet csrfToken: string | null = null;\n\nexport async function getSessionToken(): Promise<string> {\n  if (csrfToken) return csrfToken;\n  const response = await fetch(\"/api/session\", {\n    headers: { Accept: \"application/json\" },\n  });\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`session failed: ${response.status}`);\n  const payload = (await response.json()) as { csrf_token: string };\n  csrfToken = payload.csrf_token;\n  return csrfToken;\n}\n\nasync function jsonRequest<T>(url: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {\n  const response = await fetch(url, init);\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as {\n      error?: {\n        message?: string;\n        correlation_id?: string;\n        fields?: { active_run_id?: string };\n      };\n      detail?: Array<{ msg: string }>;\n    } | null;\n    const message =\n      body?.error?.message ??\n      body?.detail?.map((item) => item.msg).join(\"; \") ??\n      `Request failed: ${response.status}`;\n    const reference = body?.error?.correlation_id;\n    throw new Error(`${message}${reference ? ` (${reference})` : \"\"}`);\n  }\n  return (await response.json()) as T;\n}\n\nexport function getRunConfig() {\n  return jsonRequest<RunConfig>(\"/api/config\");\n}\n\nexport function getRunModels(provider: string, mode: \"quick\" | \"deep\") {\n  return jsonRequest<{ models: Array<{ value: string; label: string }> }>(\n    `/api/config/models?provider=${encodeURIComponent(provider)}&mode=${mode}`,\n  );\n}\n\nexport async function startRun(\n  body: Record<string, unknown>,\n): Promise<RunSnapshot> {\n  const token = await getSessionToken();\n  return jsonRequest<RunSnapshot>(\"/api/runs\", {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: {\n      \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",\n      \"X-CSRF-Token\": token,\n    },\n    body: JSON.stringify(body),\n  });\n}\n\nexport function getRun(runId: string) {\n  return jsonRequest<RunSnapshot>(`/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}`);\n}\n\nexport async function cancelRun(runId: string): Promise<RunSnapshot> {\n  const token = await getSessionToken();\n  return jsonRequest<RunSnapshot>(\n    `/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/cancel`,\n    {\n      method: \"POST\",\n      headers: { \"X-CSRF-Token\": token },\n    },\n  );\n}\n\nexport function runEventsUrl(runId: string, afterSeq: number) {\n  return `/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/events?after_seq=${afterSeq}`;\n}\n"

                "text": "\"\"\"Checkpoint clearing with explicit confirmation and a single-run guard.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Request\n\nfrom tradingagents.graph.checkpointer import clear_all_checkpoints\nfrom tradingagents_web.errors import error_response\nfrom tradingagents_web.models.requests import CheckpointClearRequest\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/api\", tags=[\"checkpoints\"])\n\n\n@router.post(\"/checkpoints/clear\")\ndef clear_checkpoints(request: Request, body: CheckpointClearRequest):\n    if body.confirm != \"CLEAR\":\n        return error_response(422, \"validation\", \"confirm must be the word CLEAR\")\n    if request.app.state.coordinator.active_snapshot() is not None:\n        return error_response(409, \"conflict\", \"a run is active\")\n    cleared = clear_all_checkpoints(request.app.state.settings.data_cache_dir)\n    return {\"cleared\": cleared}\n"
              }

              "content": "import { useEffect, useRef } from \"react\";\nimport type { ReactNode } from \"react\";\n\ntype ModalProps = {\n  open: boolean;\n  title: string;\n  onClose: () => void;\n  children: ReactNode;\n  className?: string;\n  closeLabel?: string;\n};\n\nexport function Modal({\n  open,\n  title,\n  onClose,\n  children,\n  className,\n  closeLabel = \"Close dialog\",\n}: ModalProps) {\n  const ref = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const dialog = ref.current;\n    if (!dialog) return;\n    if (open && !dialog.open) dialog.showModal();\n    if (!open && dialog.open) dialog.close();\n  }, [open]);\n\n  return (\n    <dialog\n      ref={ref}\n      className={`modal ${className ?? \"\"}`}\n      aria-labelledby=\"modal-title\"\n      onClose={onClose}\n      onCancel={(event) => {\n        event.preventDefault();\n        onClose();\n      }}\n    >\n      <div className=\"modal-header\">\n        <h2 id=\"modal-title\">{title}</h2>\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          className=\"icon-button\"\n          aria-label={closeLabel}\n          onClick={onClose}\n        >\n          <span className=\"close-glyph\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n            ×\n          </span>\n        </button>\n      </div>\n      <div className=\"modal-body\">{children}</div>\n    </dialog>\n  );\n}\n",

              "content": "import { useQuery } from \"@tanstack/react-query\";\nimport { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from \"react\";\nimport { useTranslation } from \"react-i18next\";\nimport { Link, useLocation, useNavigate } from \"react-router-dom\";\nimport type { ReactNode } from \"react\";\n\nimport { getAnnouncements } from \"../api/backtestClient\";\nimport { getHistory } from \"../api/client\";\nimport { clearCheckpoints, getRunConfig } from \"../api/runClient\";\nimport { AnnouncementsGate } from \"./Announcements\";\nimport { Icon } from \"./Icon\";\nimport { Modal } from \"./Modal\";\n\nconst NAV = [\n  { route: \"overview\", label: \"Overview\", icon: \"grid\" },\n  { route: \"history\", label: \"Analysis history\", icon: \"clock\" },\n  { route: \"backtest\", label: \"Backtesting\", icon: \"sliders\" },\n  { route: \"audit\", label: \"Research audit\", icon: \"shield\" },\n  { route: \"comparison\", label: \"Policy comparison\", icon: \"layers\" },\n  { route: \"journal\", label: \"Decision journal\", icon: \"book\" },\n] as const;\n\ntype ModalKind = \"settings\" | \"help\" | \"search\" | \"announcements\" | null;\n\nconst BREADCRUMBS: Record<string, string> = {\n  overview: \"Overview\",\n  history: \"Analysis history\",\n  backtest: \"Backtesting\",\n  audit: \"Research audit\",\n  comparison: \"Policy comparison\",\n  journal: \"Decision journal\",\n  new: \"New analysis\",\n  runs: \"Live run\",\n};\n\nexport function AppShell({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();\n  const location = useLocation();\n  const navigate = useNavigate();\n  const [mobileOpen, setMobileOpen] = useState(false);\n  const [modal, setModal] = useState<ModalKind>(null);\n  const [theme, setTheme] = useState(\n    () => window.localStorage.getItem(\"ta.theme\") ?? \"light\",\n  );\n  const [search, setSearch] = useState(\"\");\n  const [confirmClear, setConfirmClear] = useState(\"\");\n  const [clearState, setClearState] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme;\n    window.localStorage.setItem(\"ta.theme\", theme);\n  }, [theme]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    setMobileOpen(false);\n    setModal(null);\n    window.scrollTo({ top: 0 });\n  }, [location.pathname]);\n\n  const history = useQuery({\n    queryKey: [\"history\", \"shell\"],\n    queryFn: () => getHistory({ limit: 50 }),\n  });\n  const config = useQuery({\n    queryKey: [\"config\", \"shell\"],\n    queryFn: getRunConfig,\n    enabled: modal === \"settings\",\n    retry: false,\n  });\n  const announcements = useQuery({\n    queryKey: [\"announcements\"],\n    queryFn: getAnnouncements,\n    retry: false,\n  });\n\n  const items = history.data?.items ?? [];\n  const top = location.pathname.split(\"/\")[1] || \"overview\";\n  const activeRoute = top === \"history\" || top === \"runs\" ? \"history\" : top;\n  const breadcrumb = BREADCRUMBS[top] ?? \"Overview\";\n  const matches = useMemo(() => {\n    const query = search.trim().toLowerCase();\n    if (!query) return items.slice(0, 6);\n    return items\n      .filter(\n        (item) =>\n          item.ticker.toLowerCase().includes(query) ||\n          item.title.toLowerCase().includes(query),\n      )\n      .slice(0, 8);\n  }, [items, search]);\n\n  function openNew() {\n    navigate(\"/new\");\n  }\n\n  async function handleClear() {\n    if (confirmClear !== \"CLEAR\") {\n      setClearState(\"Type CLEAR to confirm.\");\n      return;\n    }\n    try {\n      const result = await clearCheckpoints();\n      setClearState(\n        `${result.cleared} checkpoint ${result.cleared === 1 ? \"file\" : \"files\"} cleared.`,\n      );\n      setConfirmClear(\"\");\n    } catch (exc) {\n      setClearState(exc instanceof Error ? exc.message : String(exc));\n    }\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"app-shell\">\n      <a className=\"skip-link\" href=\"#main\">\n        Skip to workspace\n      </a>\n      <aside\n        className={`sidebar ${mobileOpen ? \"open\" : \"\"}`}\n        id=\"sidebar\"\n        aria-label=\"Workspace navigation\"\n      >\n        <Link className=\"brand\" to=\"/overview\">\n          <span className=\"brand-mark\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n            <Icon name=\"chart\" />\n          </span>\n          <span>\n            TradingAgents\n            <span className=\"brand-caption\">A RESEARCH WORKSPACE</span>\n          </span>\n        </Link>\n        <div className=\"workspace-selector\">\n          <span className=\"workspace-symbol\">W</span>\n          <span>\n            Personal workspace\n            <small>Local · Single user</small>\n          </span>\n          <span className=\"workspace-dot\" aria-hidden=\"true\" />\n        </div>\n        <p className=\"nav-label\">WORKSPACE</p>\n        <nav className=\"nav-list\">\n          {NAV.map((item) => (\n            <Link\n              key={item.route}\n              to={`/${item.route}`}\n              className={activeRoute === item.route ? \"active\" : \"\"}\n              aria-current={activeRoute === item.route ? \"page\" : undefined}\n            >\n              <Icon name={item.icon} />\n              {item.label}\n              {item.route === \"history\" ? (\n                <span className=\"nav-count\">{items.length}</span>\n              ) : null}\n            </Link>\n          ))}\n        </nav>\n        <div className=\"sidebar-divider\" />\n        <div className=\"nav-label nav-label-row\">\n          <span>RECENT RESEARCH</span>\n          <Icon name=\"layers\" />\n        </div>\n        <nav className=\"research-links\" aria-label=\"Recent research\">\n          {items.slice(0, 3).map((item) => (\n            <Link key={item.artifact_id} to={`/history/${item.artifact_id}`}>\n              <span className=\"research-symbol\">{item.ticker}</span>\n              <span>{item.title}</span>\n              <Icon name=\"chevron\" />\n            </Link>\n          ))}\n        </nav>\n        <div className=\"sidebar-bottom\">\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            className=\"sidebar-button\"\n            onClick={() => setModal(\"settings\")}\n          >\n            <Icon name=\"settings\" />\n            Workspace settings\n          </button>\n          <button\n            type=\"button\"\n            className=\"sidebar-button\"\n            onClick={() => setModal(\"help\")}\n          >\n            <Icon name=\"help\" />\n            Help & shortcuts\n            <span className=\"nav-shortcut\">?</span>\n          </button>\n          <div className=\"sidebar-footer\">\n            <span className=\"local-indicator\" />\n            Runs locally. Thinks together.\n            <span className=\"version\">v0.5</span>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </aside>\n\n      <div className=\"workspace\">\n        <header className=\"topbar\">\n          <div className=\"breadcrumbs\">\n            <button\n              className=\"icon-button mobile-menu\"\n              type=\"button\"\n              aria-label=\"Open navigation\"\n              aria-expanded={mobileOpen}\n              onClick={() => setMobileOpen((open) => !open)}\n            >\n              <Icon name=\"menu\" />\n            </button>\n            <span className=\"breadcrumb-icon\">\n              <Icon name=\"layers\" />\n            </span>\n            <span>Workspace</span>\n            <span className=\"breadcrumb-slash\">/</span>\n            <span>{breadcrumb}</span>\n          </div>\n          <div className=\"topbar-actions\">\n            <span className=\"preview-badge\">\n              <span />\n              Local workspace\n            </span>\n            <button\n              className=\"search-trigger\"\n              type=\"button\"\n              onClick={() => setModal(\"search\")}\n            >\n              <Icon name=\"search\" />\n              <span>Find research...</span>\n              <kbd>⌘ K</kbd>\n            </button>\n            <button\n              className=\"icon-button notification-button\"\n              type=\"button\"\n              aria-label=\"View announcements\"\n              onClick={() => setModal(\"announcements\")}\n            >\n              <Icon name=\"bell\" />\n              {announcements.data?.announcements.length ? <i /> : null}\n            </button>\n            <button\n              className=\"avatar-button\"\n              type=\"button\"\n              aria-label=\"Open local workspace settings\"\n              onClick={() => setModal(\"settings\")}\n            >\n              W\n            </button>\n            <button className=\"button primary\" type=\"button\" onClick={openNew}>\n              <Icon name=\"plus\" />\n              New analysis\n            </button>\n          </div>\n        </header>\n\n        <main id=\"main\" tabIndex={-1}>\n          <div className=\"page-enter\">\n            <AnnouncementsGate />\n            {children}\n          </div>\n        </main>\n\n        <footer className=\"main-footer\">\n          <span>Built for research. Decisions remain yours.</span>\n          <span>\n            <span className=\"local-indicator\" /> Runs locally\n            <span className=\"footer-dot\">·</span> Single user\n          </span>\n        </footer>\n      </div>\n\n      <Modal\n        open={modal === \"settings\"}\n        title=\"Workspace settings\"\n        onClose={() => setModal(null)}\n      >\n        <p>\n          Local preferences and server-owned configuration. No credentials are\n          read or accepted.\n        </p>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>\n            Appearance\n            <small>Comfortable in daylight or after hours.</small>\n          </span>\n          <label className=\"sr-only\" htmlFor=\"theme\">\n            Appearance\n          </label>\n          <select\n            id=\"theme\"\n            value={theme}\n            onChange={(event) => setTheme(event.target.value)}\n          >\n            <option value=\"light\">Light / paper</option>\n            <option value=\"dark\">Dark / forest</option>\n          </select>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>\n            Interface language\n            <small>Report output language is a separate run setting.</small>\n          </span>\n          <select\n            aria-label={t(\"nav.language\")}\n            value={i18n.language.startsWith(\"zh\") ? \"zh\" : \"en\"}\n            onChange={(event) => {\n              void i18n.changeLanguage(event.target.value);\n              window.localStorage.setItem(\"ta.language\", event.target.value);\n            }}\n          >\n            <option value=\"en\">English</option>\n            <option value=\"zh\">中文</option>\n          </select>\n        </div>\n        <p className=\"setting-section\">MODEL PROVIDERS · SERVER STATUS</p>\n        {config.isLoading ? <p>Loading configuration...</p> : null}\n        {config.isError ? (\n          <p className=\"field-error\">Configuration is unavailable.</p>\n        ) : null}\n        {config.data\n          ? Object.entries(config.data.key_status)\n              .slice(0, 10)\n              .map(([provider, status]) => (\n                <div className=\"setting-row\" key={provider}>\n                  <span>{provider}</span>\n                  <span\n                    className={`status-tag ${status === \"configured\" ? \"\" : \"neutral\"}`}\n                  >\n                    {status}\n                  </span>\n                </div>\n              ))\n          : null}\n        <p className=\"setting-section\">RECOVERY</p>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>\n            Checkpoint storage\n            <small>\n              Clearing never removes saved reports. Type CLEAR to confirm.\n            </small>\n          </span>\n          <div className=\"inline-actions\">\n            <input\n              aria-label=\"Checkpoint confirmation\"\n              value={confirmClear}\n              onChange={(event) => setConfirmClear(event.target.value)}\n              placeholder=\"CLEAR\"\n            />\n            <button className=\"button\" type=\"button\" onClick={() => void handleClear()}>\n              Clear\n            </button>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n        {clearState ? <p className=\"inline-note\">{clearState}</p> : null}\n      </Modal>\n\n      <Modal\n        open={modal === \"help\"}\n        title=\"Help & shortcuts\"\n        onClose={() => setModal(null)}\n      >\n        <p>\n          This workspace runs against the local TradingAgents server. Analysis\n          and backtest results are advisory, not executed positions.\n        </p>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>New analysis</span>\n          <kbd>N</kbd>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>Find research</span>\n          <kbd>⌘ K</kbd>\n        </div>\n        <div className=\"setting-row\">\n          <span>Close dialog</span>\n          <kbd>Esc</kbd>\n        </div>\n      </Modal>\n\n      <Modal\n        open={modal === \"search\"}\n        title=\"Find a perspective\"\n        className=\"search-modal\"\n        onClose={() => setModal(null)}\n      >\n        <label className=\"sr-only\" htmlFor=\"command-input\">\n          Search research by ticker or title\n        </label>\n        <input\n          className=\"input\"\n          id=\"command-input\"\n          placeholder=\"Search a ticker...\"\n          value={search}\n          onChange={(event) => setSearch(event.target.value)}\n        />\n        <div className=\"search-results\">\n          {matches.length ? (\n            matches.map((item) => (\n              <button\n                key={item.artifact_id}\n                type=\"button\"\n                className=\"search-result\"\n                onClick={() => {\n                  setModal(null);\n                  navigate(`/history/${item.artifact_id}`);\n                }}\n              >\n                <span>\n                  <strong>{item.ticker}</strong>\n                  <small>\n                    {item.date ?? \"Date not recorded\"} · {item.status}\n                  </small>\n                </span>\n                <span className=\"rating\">{item.rating ?? \"—\"}</span>\n              </button>\n            ))\n          ) : (\n            <div className=\"empty-state\">\n              <strong>No matching research</strong>\n              <p>Try another ticker.</p>\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </div>\n      </Modal>\n\n      <Modal\n        open={modal === \"announcements\"}\n        title=\"Announcements\"\n        onClose={() => setModal(null)}\n      >\n        {announcements.data?.announcements.length ? (\n          announcements.data.announcements.map((item, index) => (\n            <p key={index}>{item}</p>\n          ))\n        ) : (\n          <p>No announcements are available.</p>\n        )}\n      </Modal>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n",

0)),\n        );\n        source.onopen = () => store.getState().setConnection(\"live\");\n        source.onerror = () => store.getState().setConnection(\"reconnecting\");\n\n        const handleEvent = (message: MessageEvent) => {\n          try {\n            const event = JSON.parse(message.data) as RunEvent;\n            store.getState().applyEvent(event);\n            if (TERMINAL.has(store.getState().status)) {\n              source?.close();\n              store.getState().setConnection(\"closed\");\n            }\n          } catch {\n            // Ignore malformed frames; the next valid event continues the stream.\n          }\n        };\n\n        for (const eventType of [\n          \"run.preparing\",\n          \"run.phase\",\n          \"run.started\",\n          \"run.resumed\",\n          \"agent.status\",\n          \"message\",\n          \"tool_call\",\n          \"report.section\",\n          \"stats\",\n          \"run.completed\",\n          \"run.failed\",\n          \"run.cancelled\",\n          \"snapshot\",\n        ]) {\n          source.addEventListener(eventType, handleEvent as EventListener);\n        }\n      } catch (exc) {\n        store.getState().applySnapshot({\n          run_id: runId,\n          status: \"failed\",\n          last_seq: 0,\n          error: exc instanceof Error ? (\n        <p role=\"alert\" className=\"mb-5 text-sm text-red-300\">\n          {state.error}\n        </p>\n      ) : null}\n      {state.warnings.map((warning) => (\n        <p key={warning} className=\"mb-3 text-amber-300\">\n          {warning}\n        </p>\n      ))}\n      {state.signal ? {section}\n                  </h3>\n                  <Markdown>{content}</Markdown>\n                </article>\n              ))}\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </div>\n      </section>\n    </main>\n  );\n}\nimport { createStore } from \"zustand/vanilla\";\n\nexport type RunStatus =\n  | \"idle\"\n  | \"starting\"\n  | \"running\"\n  | \"cancelling\"\n  | \"completed\"\n  | \"failed\"\n  | \"cancelled\";\nexport type Connection =\n  \"idle\" | \"connecting\" | \"live\" | \"reconnecting\" | \"closed\";\nexport type RunMessage = {\n  id: string;\n  timestamp?: string;\n  type?: string;\n  content: string;\n};\nexport type RunEvent = {\n  run_id?: string;\n  seq: number;\n  type: string;\n  payload?: Record<string, unknown>;\n};\nexport type RunState = {\n  runId: applySnapshot: (snapshot: Record<string, unknown>) => void;\n  setConnection: (connection: Connection) => void;\n  reset: () => void;\n};\nconst TERMINAL = new Set<RunStatus>([\"completed\", \"failed\", \"cancelled\"]);\nconst initial = () => ({\n  runId: null,\n  status: \"idle\" as RunStatus,\n  connection: \"idle\" as Connection,\n  lastSeq: 0,\n  messages: [] as RunMessage[],\n {\n  const status = (snapshot.status as RunStatus) ?? \"running\";\n  return {\n    runId: String(snapshot.run_id ?? \"\"),\n    status,\n    connection: TERMINAL.has(status) ? \"closed\" : \"connecting\",\n    lastSeq: Number(snapshot.last_seq ?? 0),\n    messages: (snapshot.messages as RunMessage[]) ?? [],\n    sections: (snapshot.sections as Record<string, string>) ?? {},\n    agents: (snapshot.agents as Record<string, string>) ?? {},\n    stats: (snapshot.stats as Record<string, number>) ?? {},\n    phase: String(snapshot.phase ?? \"preparing\"),\n    signal: snapshot.signal as string | undefined,\n    review: Boolean(snapshot.review),\n    error: errorMessage(snapshot.error),\n    warnings: (snapshot.warnings as string[]) ?? [],\n    artifactId: snapshot.artifact_id as string | undefined,\n  };\n}\n\n// REQ-WEB-007: hydrate display state and its cursor atomically before SSE replay.\nexport function createRunStore() {\n  return createStore<RunState>((set, get) => ({\n    ...initial(),\n    applyEvent(event) {\n      const state = get();\n      if (event.run_id && state.runId && event.run_id !== state.runId) return;\n      if (event.seq <= state.lastSeq) return;\n      const payload = event.payload ??           "text": "# Demo 视觉与交互复刻完成\n\n已按 `demo/` 的布局、配色、字体、间距和组件细节重建生产前端，并接入现有后端能力。`demo/` 未修改。\n\n## 已完成\n\n### 新增生产壳层\n\n- 持久侧边栏：Overview、Analysis history、Backtesting、Research audit、Policy comparison、Decision journal。\n- 顶栏搜索、公告、设置、主题切换、移动端导航。\n- Demo 的浅色 paper / 深色 forest 主题。\n- 快捷键：`N` 新建分析、`?` 帮助、`Cmd/Ctrl K` 搜索。\n- 设置面板接入真实 `/api/config` 和 `/api/checkpoints/clear`。\n- 公告接入真实 `/api/announcements`。\n\n### 页面重建\n\n- `/overview`：真实历史统计、最新报告、报告 section、pipeline、近期分析和回测摘要。\n- `/history`：真实历史、搜索、状态过滤、排序、只读打开。\n- `/history/:id`：真实 run/saved/backtest/decision artifacts、section 导航、报告下载。\n- `/backtest`、`/backtest/:id`：真实回测配置、运行状态、摘要、失败项、日志下载、历史列表。\n- `/new`：保留 8 步 CLI 对等流程，使用 Demo 的视觉样式；接入真实 config、models、portfolio、checkpoint 和 run API。\n- `/runs/:id`：真实 SSE、消息、工具调用、agent 状态、stats、报告 section、取消。\n- `/journal`：真实 decision memory，只读展示决策、结果、reflection。\n- 公告、设置、搜索均使用原生 dialog 交互风格。\n\n### 移除的生产内容\n\n- 删除 Demo 的 preview state 选择器。\n- 删除 sample report、sample backtest、sample progress、sample journal。\n- 删除 fixture 公司名、行业、伪造图表数据。\n- 历史中后端未提供的字段显示 `Not recorded`，不填零、不推断。\n\n### 真实接口接入\n\n已使用：\n\n```text\nGET  /api/history\nGET  /api/history/{id}\nGET  /api/backtests\nPOST /api/backtests\nGET  /api/backtests/{run_id}\nPOST /api/runs\nGET  /api/runs/{run_id}\nGET  /api/runs/{run_id}/events\nPOST /api/runs/{run_id}/cancel\nGET  /api/config\nGET  /api/config/models\nPOST /api/portfolio/validate\nPOST /api/checkpoints/clear\nGET  /api/announcements\n```\n\n未修改后端路由、`src/tradingagents/`、`src/cli/` 或依赖。\n\n## 接口缺口与最小方案\n\n### Research audit\n\n核心已有 evidence、gate、debate、usage、confidence 等能力，但 WebUI 没有读投影。最小方案：\n\n```text\nGET /api/runs/{run_id}/audit\nGET /api/history/{artifact_id}/audit\nGET /api/history/{artifact_id}/download?kind=evidence|gate|debate|summary\n```\n\n返回只读的 gate verdict、reason codes、category coverage、evidence manifest、debate participation/claims/conflicts、usage 和 confidence。当前页面明确显示接口缺口，不渲染 fixture。\n\n### Policy comparison\n\n核心有 comparison 模块，但没有 WebUI 读投影。最小方案：\n\n```text\nGET /api/comparisons\nGET /api/comparisons/{case_id}\n```\n\n只返回已生成的比较结果、四段身份校验、stop
